10.3389/fenvs.2026.1975174: Fish supplies up to 30% of animal protein in Malawi, so pesticide residues in fish are a public-health concern. We assessed the dietary risk, and screened the ecological risk, posed by four endocrine-disrupting pesticides (EDPs): atrazine, malathion, total DDT (ΣDDT; DDT and its metabolites) and endosulfan. Wet-season residues were measured in two fisheries, analysed separately because each is represented by different species: Oreochromis karongae and Engraulicypris sardella from nine Lake Malawi landing sites (n = 72) and Clarias gariepinus and Oreochromis shiranus from five Shire River sites (n = 40). Estimated daily intakes for children and adults, based on national household-survey ingestion rates, were compared with USEPA reference doses to derive Hazard Indices (HIs), and ΣDDT Lifetime Cancer Risk (LCR) was estimated with the USEPA slope factor. Because water concentrations were not measured, ecological risk was screened by back-calculating water concentrations from tissue residues with literature bioconcentration factors (BCFs) and comparing them with predicted no-effect concentrations (PNECs) as risk quotients (RQs). Within each water body, residues differed significantly among sites (two-way ANOVA, p < 0.001). The maximum HI was 0.074 at baseline and 0.279 in the combined worst case. LCR fell in the tolerable range (10 -6 -10 -4 ) for three species (maximum 1.61 × 10 -5 in the worst case) and was acceptable (<10 -6 ) for E. sardella . In a 200,000-iteration Monte Carlo analysis, fewer than 0.1% of simulations gave an HI above 1. In contrast, 41%-75% gave a ΣDDT screening RQ above 1 for C. gariepinus , depending on the PNEC, and malathion RQs for the Shire River species also exceeded 1 with the more protective PNEC, although these are indicative only. At the sampled sites, dietary risk is low, but the ecological screening for the Shire River species is inconclusive and cannot be inferred from dietary safety. We recommend dry-season sampling, direct measurement of water concentrations, and precautionary dietary guidance for frequent consumers of Shire River fish.
10.36359/scivp.2026-27-2.36: The intensive development of industrial-energy complexes and the increasing anthropogenic pressure on aquatic ecosystems necessitate the search for reliable bioindication methods to assess the ecological status of river basins. The middle reach of the Western Bug River near the Dobrotvir thermal power plant is affected by heated water discharge, coal combustion products, municipal wastewater carried by the Poltva River and agricultural runoff. While the results of physicochemical water monitoring capture the ecological situation only at the exact moment of sampling, aquatic organisms, particularly fish, accumulate and integrate the toxic impact of pollutants over a prolonged period. This study aims to investigate developmental stability, as well as the patterns of accumulation and topographic distribution of Cu, Zn, Fe, and Pb in target organs (muscles, liver, gills) of four fish species with different trophic preferences: roach, bleak, European perch, and Prussian carp. The research was conducted at the monitoring station near the village of Staryi Dobrotvir. Fluctuating asymmetry was assessed from five bilateral meristic traits; metals were determined by atomic absorption spectrophotometry. Fluctuating asymmetry was highest in roach (0.48) and bleak (0.42), intermediate in perch (0.35) and lowest in Prussian carp (0.21), corresponding to environmental quality classes II-IV. The mean total metal content increased in the order planktivore (bleak, 28.1 mg/kg dry weight)
10.1021/acsomega.6c12717: Abstract Marine fish-derived collagen has gained attention as a promising source for collagen extraction for tissue engineering applications. In this study, collagen was isolated from the scales of Asian seabass (Lates calcarifer) using acetic acid and pepsin extraction methods, followed by physicochemical characterization. Sodium dodecyl sulfate-polyacrylamide gel electrophoresis (SDS-PAGE) revealed characteristic α1, α2, and β chains, while Fourier Transform Infrared (FTIR) showed characteristic amide bands, supporting the molecular and structural similarity of the extracted collagen to standard type I collagen. The amino acid compositions, thermal stability, and structural organization were evaluated. The extracted collagen was subsequently incorporated into scaffold fabrication using the freeze-drying technique by blending with agarose, chitosan, and gelatin. The resulting scaffold demonstrated successful formation of a three-dimensional (3D) scaffold with porous and sponge-like characteristics. The fabricated scaffolds exhibited pore sizes of 75 to 200 μm, a high water absorption capacity of up to 90%, and a degradation rate of 39% after 4 weeks. Mechanical compression analysis revealed elastic modulus values ranging from 112 to 141 kPa. Furthermore, chondrocytes cultured on the scaffolds for 3 weeks were able to proliferate and grow effectively. These findings suggest that the natural biomaterial-based scaffolds developed in this study were noncytotoxic and capable of supporting chondrocyte proliferation. Importantly, the research also demonstrates the value-added utilization of fish scale waste through collagen extraction for the development of scaffolds with properties suitable for future tissue engineering applications.
10.29303/jfh.v6i4.12251: Aeromonas hydrophila (A. hydrophila) is an opportunistic Gram-negative bacterium commonly found in aquatic environments and is the principal causative agent of Motile Aeromonas Septicaemia (MAS) in cultured fish, including Sangkuriang catfish (Clarias gariepinus). Infection with A. hydrophila can cause substantial economic losses due to increased morbidity and mortality in cultured fish. Bacterial infections are commonly controlled using antibiotics; however, indiscriminate and repeated antibiotic use may induce antibiotic resistance, thereby reducing treatment efficacy. This study aimed to identify the presence of A. hydrophila and to determine its resistance status against ciprofloxacin, gentamicin, and tetracycline in Sangkuriang catfish (C. gariepinus) cultured at Aqsa Sabar Subur Farm, Kupang City. A descriptive method with purposive sampling was employed. A total of 30 kidney samples from apparently healthy Sangkuriang catfish were isolated on Rimler-Shotts Agar (RSA), followed by confirmatory testing through Gram staining and biochemical assays. Antibiotic susceptibility testing was carried out using the Kirby-Bauer disc diffusion method on Mueller-Hinton Agar (MHA), with results interpreted according to Clinical and Laboratory Standards Institute (CLSI) breakpoints. Data were analysed descriptively and presented in tabular form. The results showed that 12 of 30 samples (40%) were confirmed positive for A. hydrophila. All isolates were fully susceptible to ciprofloxacin (100%) and predominantly susceptible to gentamicin (58.33% susceptible, 41.67% intermediate), whereas 25% of isolates were resistant to tetracycline, 16.67% intermediate, and 58.33% susceptible.
10.5194/gh-81-843-2026: This paper examines how emerging biotechnologies are transforming Japan's seafood sector, driving the exploitation of new ocean frontiers and the commodification of marine life, and reshaping food sovereignty. Drawing on ethnographic fieldwork, qualitative interviews, and industry publications, it traces how the three exemplary innovations - bioactive “functional foods”, industrialized aquaculture and genome-editing, and cell-based seafood - are reconfiguring ocean-fishery assemblages and seafood geographies. The paper argues that capital-intensive “promissory proteins” are shifting power from coastal fisheries toward urban, terrestrial centres. This polarization is intensified by recent legal reforms prioritizing corporate capital investment over community-based resource management, under the banner of promoting self-sufficiency and economic growth. Meanwhile, large transnationally operating seafood corporations are eager to expand their pharmaceutical and life sciences divisions. Corporate, biotech-driven models are thus recasting multi-species relations, consumer practices, and the governance of ocean resources, blurring the social and spatial boundaries of the ocean as the primary space of marine resource extraction and food sovereignty.
10.1111/jfb.70723: Abstract Information on the feeding ecology of intertidal notothenioid fishes remains limited in Argentine Patagonia, particularly for Patagonotothen sima . This study examined the diets of P. sima and P. cornucola and their spatial and seasonal variation using stomach-content analysis. Sampling was conducted at four coastal localities between March 2021 and March 2022. Patagonotothen sima was collected at two localities and P. cornucola at three; the interspecific comparison was restricted to Cerro Avanzado during winter. Patagonotothen sima fed mainly on polychaetes and small crustaceans, including tanaidaceans, amphipods and decapods, and exhibited an intermediate niche breadth (0.44). In P. cornucola , amphipods and polychaetes were important at Cerro Avanzado, whereas Exosphaeroma sp. and amphipods were prominent at Yamana. At El Pique, the diet was dominated by Exosphaeroma sp., with a narrow niche breadth (0.25), compared with intermediate values at Cerro Avanzado (0.56) and Yamana (0.59). Significant Site × Season interactions were detected in both species, as well as an interspecific difference at Cerro Avanzado during winter. These findings provide a detailed characterisation of the diet of P. sima in Argentine Patagonia and highlight spatial and seasonal variation in the trophic ecology of both species.
10.1007/s10499-026-02749-y: Robust state detection of Portunus trituberculatus in industrial aquaculture is essential for screening abnormal individuals and issuing risk alerts. However, nonuniform illumination, visibility degradation, and complex backgrounds weaken object boundaries and local phenotypic cues, hindering individual localization and state detection. In this study, the detection task distinguishes three observable phenotypic states, namely Sick, Healthy, and Dead. Specifically, the Sick class represents individuals exhibiting visually abnormal external phenotypes, rather than individuals with clinically or etiologically confirmed disease. Image enhancement can recover partial visual information, yet its utility varies markedly across space: the same operation may reveal structures in dark regions while introducing noise and pseudo-textures in highlights or reflections. A central challenge is therefore to exploit useful cues from enhanced views without allowing unreliable enhancement features to corrupt the original representation. To address this issue, we propose CRAB-DETR. Built on RT-DETR-L, CRAB-DETR treats the original image as the primary representation and introduces a detail-enhanced view and an illumination-compensated view as complementary visual evidence. We further develop TriStemFusion, a discrepancy-guided selective multi-view fusion module that explicitly describes changes between each enhanced view and the original representation, dynamically modulates their local contributions, and performs controlled feature correction through original-anchored bounded residual compensation. During training, progressive multi-scale dense auxiliary supervision provides more positive learning signals for difficult objects, while inference retains the standard RT-DETR detection path. Under a unified experimental protocol, CRAB-DETR achieved competitive performance on our Portunus trituberculatus dataset and outperformed several representative detectors. Stratified evaluation under multiple imaging-degradation conditions further demonstrates its practical potential.
10.29303/jbt.v26i4a.13243: Effective water quality management is essential for optimizing fish growth in the Budikdamber (fish-in-a-bucket) aquaponic system. This study evaluated the effects of different EM4 probiotic concentrations on the growth performance of catfish (Clarias gariepinus). The experiment used a completely randomized design with four treatments and three replicates: 0 (A), 10 (B), 15 (C), and 20 ml/L EM4 (D). Parameters included relative growth rate (RGR), feed utilization efficiency (EPP), survival rate (SR), and water quality. EM4 significantly affected RGR, which increased from 5.54% in the control to 7.24% in treatment D. EPP showed an increasing trend, reaching 5.27% in treatment D, although differences among treatments were not significant. Survival rates ranged from 7.77% to 44.43%, with the highest values recorded in treatments B and D. Although pH and dissolved oxygen remained within acceptable ranges, ammonia concentrations exceeded recommended standards in all treatments, while nitrate levels exceeded the limits in treatments A and B. In conclusion, EM4 at 20 ml/L produced the highest RGR but did not yield the best results across all parameters. Therefore, improved water quality management remains necessary.
10.1111/fme.70135: ABSTRACT Small-scale fisheries (SSF) play an important role in coastal Mediterranean communities but may also produce high proportions of discards and interact with vulnerable marine taxa. This study provides a comparative assessment of three métiers practiced in a Mediterranean SSF, each targeting a different species using static nets: gillnets for surmullet ( Mullus surmuletus ; MULLUS), and trammel nets for common cuttlefish ( Sepia officinalis ; SEPIA) and common sole ( Solea solea ; SOLE). A total of 334 hauls were analyzed between 2019 and 2023 under commercial fishing conditions. Catch composition was recorded at species level and categorized as target, retained bycatch, and discards, while elasmobranchs, predominantly comprising batoid species of varying conservation status, were treated as a separate category. Indicators describing catch characteristics and fishing practices included the proportions of immature and physically damaged individuals, catch-category biomass, fuel consumption standardized by landed commercial catch, soak time, fishing depth, haul income, and dolphin-depredation frequency. Principal component analysis and cumulative dominance curves were used to explore métier-specific patterns. The métiers differed in catch composition and in the profiles of ecological and operational indicators. MULLUS exhibited lower discard biomass shares and negligible recorded chondrichthyans biomass compared with two trammel-net métiers, but higher proportions of immature and damaged individuals and a higher frequency of dolphin depredation than SEPIA. SOLE had a high recorded contribution of elasmobranchs, while fuel-use intensity relative to landed commercial catch was highest in SEPIA. Hypothetical reclassification scenarios also illustrated how local market practices can affect estimates of retained bycatch and discards. The findings show that métiers operating in the same fishery can exhibit contrasting profiles, underscoring the need for métier-specific assessments and tailored management measures rather than assuming that interventions will be equally effective across fishing practices.
10.1111/fog.70096: ABSTRACT The northern Humboldt Current System (nHCS) is among the most productive marine ecosystems worldwide, supporting highly dynamic pelagic communities. However, the relative contributions of environmental conditions, spatial processes and species associations to community organization have not been quantified together. We asked to what extent community structure is dominated by environmental variables versus residual (biotic or abiotic) dependencies. We fitted year-specific Joint Species Distribution Models (JSDMs) to acoustic data for six pelagic taxa from summer surveys collected by the Instituto del Mar del Perú (IMARPE) between 2013 and 2019. We modelled the community abundance matrix using a two-part hurdle approach to account for zero inflation in the acoustic data, allowing the joint analysing of species occurrence and abundance patterns in relation to environmental and spatial drivers. Occurrence models showed good predictive performance (mean cross-validated AUC = 0.83), whereas abundance models had low explanatory power (mean = 0.07). Environmental covariates, led by distance to the shelf break, dissolved oxygen and sea surface temperature, jointly accounted for 69%-83% of the explained variance in occurrence, versus 17%-31% for the spatial random effect. Significant residual species associations were observed only in occurrence models and were weaker or absent in years of strong environmental anomalies. Environmental filtering is therefore the primary organising mechanism of pelagic community structure in the nHCS, with spatial and biotic processes modulating it among years. For ecosystem-based management, these results support monitoring and managing co-occurrence of pelagic taxa jointly, using oxygen and temperature conditions as early indicators of community reorganization under ENSO and climate variability.
10.1007/s11357-026-02654-5: Abstract Consumption of foods such as fruit, vegetables and fish has been associated with a reduced risk of non-communicable diseases (NCDs) and greater longevity. These effects could, at least in part, be underpinned by epigenetic alterations, including changes in DNA methylation (DNAm) patterns. The aim of the current study was to characterise cross-sectional associations between three selected food components (fruit, vegetables and fish) and measures of DNA methylation associated with biological ageing (DNAm PhenoAge, DNAm GrimAge and DNAm Telomere Length), and epigenetic scores-or EpiScores-for 109 proteins in Generation Scotland. This study used dietary data collected on frequency and consumption quantities of fresh fruit ( n = 8648), vegetables ( n = 8686) and fish ( n = 5070). Linear regression models were used to test associations between food components and DNAm GrimAge, DNAm PhenoAge, DNAm Telomere Length, DNAm IL6 and the 109 EpiScores), After correction for multiple testing, there were several significant associations between food and the epigenetic biomarkers.. These findings provide additional evidence that dietary behaviours are associated with DNA methylation-derived biomarkers of ageing and health. Future research could focus on external validation of our results, and use longitudinal data to explore causal pathways.
10.53941/ale.2026.100019: Circadian rhythms constitute an endogenous timekeeping system that fish have evolved to anticipate the alternation of light and darkness, and their molecular basis centers on the rhythmic expression of core clock genes. Teleosts display a markedly decentralized organization, in which multiple brain regions and peripheral tissues harbor endogenous, directly photoreceptive oscillators; consequently, fish rhythms are highly sensitive and plastic with respect to environmental factors such as light, temperature, salinity, dissolved oxygen and feeding. Advances in multi-omics, gene editing and live imaging have substantially deepened understanding of fish circadian biology, including the functional dissection of clock genes, the characterization of tissue-specific expression profiles, and the characterization of interactions between the clock and metabolism, immunity and reproduction. Against this background, chrono-aquaculture-the scheduling of farming practice to match the endogenous rhythms of the cultured species-has emerged as a promising framework for improving production efficiency and animal welfare while reducing environmental load. Nevertheless, important challenges remain, including a pronounced reliance on a small number of model species, limited understanding of multi-factor interactions, and a persistent gap between laboratory findings and large-scale application. This review synthesizes the molecular regulatory networks of fish circadian rhythms, the mechanisms through which environmental factors act, physiological and behavioral rhythms, and their application in aquaculture, and discusses key bottlenecks and future directions, with the aim of supporting both fish chronobiology and precision aquaculture management.
10.3389/fmars.2026.1943645: Holoplanktonic gastropods are important components of oceanic ecosystems and contribute to trophic transfer, biogeochemical cycling, and pelagic carbonate production. Despite their importance, we know surprisingly little about the vertical distribution and mitochondrial genomes of holoplanktonic gastropods in the deep Indian Ocean. To shed light on this topic, we investigated surveys in the waters above the Central Indian Ridge in June 2018 and July 2019. Depth-stratified samples were collected using a Multiple Opening/Closing Net and Environmental Sensing System, and then employed next-generation sequencing to identify the species present and assess phylogenetic relationships. Our result revealed two species of holoplanktonic gastropods: Atlanta oligogyra , and Heliconoides inflatus . A. oligogyra was restricted to the Onnuri Vent Field but was deepest recorded down to 1,600 m, while H. inflatus peaked abundance in the epipelagic zone. Environmental analyses indicated a positive association between H. inflatus abundance and temperature, whereas no clear relationships were detected for the A. oligogyra . COX1 sequences showed 98.9-100% similarity to public reference sequences, supporting the morphological identifications for both species. Phylogenetic analyses recovered the major Atlantidae and Pteropoda lineages but provided limited resolution among closely related Atlanta species. Genomic divergence among H. inflatus specimens despite identical COX1 barcodes may indicate cryptic diversity. These findings provide the first integrated ecological and molecular assessment of holoplanktonic gastropods from the Central Indian Ridge and establish a baseline for future studies of pelagic biodiversity in the Indian Ocean.
10.36685/jlssm.v3i2.2534: Background: Small-scale fisheries in Southeast Sulawesi face significant socio-ecological pressures driven by maritime modernization programs and technological change. Objectives: This study aims to assess the socio-ecological impacts of maritime modernization on small-scale fishing communities in Southeast Sulawesi, Indonesia. Method: A mixed-methods approach was employed, combining structured interviews with 120 fishing households across four coastal villages in Kendari, Baubau, Muna, and Wakatobi districts, with ecological assessments of fish catch trends over five years (2019-2023). Results: Findings reveal that modernization has increased fishing capacity and short-term income, yet has simultaneously eroded traditional ecological knowledge (TEK), disrupted customary fishing territories, and intensified resource competition. Ecological indicators show declining fish abundance near inshore areas, while fishers increasingly venture into deeper waters. Social stratification has widened as capital-intensive technologies favor wealthier fishers. Conclusion: Maritime modernization in Southeast Sulawesi has generated a dual socio-ecological transformation: improved economic efficiency for some, but increased vulnerability and reduced ecological resilience for many. Adaptive co-management integrating local knowledge systems is urgently needed. Keywords: small-scale fisheries, socio-ecological transformation, maritime modernization, Southeast Sulawesi, coastal resilience
10.35314/ya7fr495: Small scale fishing vessels are central to Indonesian coastal fisheries, yet traditional wooden hulls often fall short on hydrodynamic efficiency, operational safety, and stability. This study evaluates hydrodynamic resistance, propulsion power requirements, hydrostatic characteristics, and intact stability in traditional wooden and redesigned Fiberglass Reinforced Plastic (FRP) fishing vessels. The comparison was carried out numerically on a 3 GT vessel measuring 8.50 m in length, 2.20 m in breadth, and 0.80 m in draft. Across the speed range examined, the FRP configuration cuts total resistance and effective propulsion power by about 12.49%; at 10 knots, resistance falls from 46.735 kN to 40.899 kN and effective power from 240.43 kW to 210.40 kW. Hydrostatic analysis shows gains of roughly 1.9-4.8% in the selected parameters. The FRP vessel also yields a higher initial metacentric height (0.606 m) and a larger maximum righting lever (0.699 m) than the wooden vessel (0.566 m and 0.308 m, respectively). These results point to the potential of an integrated FRP hull redesign to improve both hydrodynamic performance and intact stability, and thereby to support safer, more efficient small-scale fishing vessel development in Indonesian coastal waters.
10.38124/ijsrmt.v5i11.1778: Recurring droughts lead to environmental degradation, reduce agricultural yields and render the social fabric of the Androy region highly vulnerable. Indeed, rural communities are restructuring their productive systems to exploit marine resources, despite the social constraints involved. This study aims to understand the dynamics of the community-led institutionalisation of marine fishing and to examine the socio-environmental management of this new productive model. The study was conducted in three coastal villages in Ambovombe district during April 2025. A total 93 of fishermen and several fisherwomen were sampled using purposive and snowball sampling techniques. Primary data were collected through in-depth guided interviews, focus-group discussions and informal conversations. The study’s findings reveal the characteristics of small-scale fishers in Androy and the challenges they face. Subsistence fisheries tend to be deeply rooted in local communities, with 67% of participants being family members (Fly), reflecting historical links to adjacent fishery resources dating back to the 1990s as sources of household income (Gn) for 100% of respondents. Subsistance fishers face a variety of challenges to their livelihoods. These challenges are from socio-economics conditions (SuW ; SoL), climate variability (Cv) and environmental degradation, the most felt compromising ressources collection (Rs). Mean while, as from the political dimensions, government policies (Ste) are most felt problems. Androy coastal fishers face different threats, and have different coping mechanism and resources reflecting their traditions and values, and supporting social cohesion through seasonal ocean sacrifice (SC). Studies of the key characteristics of subsistance marine fisheries in Androy and the challenges they face are deemed very necessary for small-scalled fisreries sustainability.

10.3390/foods15234269: The nanoliposomes coated with carboxymethyl chitosan (CM-NLs) were prepared to deliver fish oil. The encapsulation efficiency (EE) of CM-NLs was 95.82% at 0.3% carboxymethyl chitosan (CMCS), with an average particle size of 89.24 nm and a zeta potential of 3.43 mV. The shape of nanoliposomes changed from spherical to irregular ellipsoidal after modification with CMCS. Structural analysis indicated that CMCS mainly encapsulated the nanoliposomes through hydrogen bonding, increasing the phase transition temperature from 183 °C to 208 °C. The in vitro release profiles showed that CM-NLs exhibited a significant sustained-release effect in simulated gastrointestinal fluids, with an approximately 18 h delay in release compared to NLs; yet, the release rates at 48 h were 53.87% and 67.32% for NLs and CM-NLs, respectively. CM-NLs remained relatively stable in the oral and gastric phases, while it was digested in the intestinal phase, resulting in a decrease in particle size. Moreover, CM-NLs were more sensitive to pH compared to NLs, and its particle size significantly increased under strong acid and alkali conditions. This study developed a nanoliposome delivery system for fish oil with enhanced encapsulation, sustained release, and pH-responsive properties. It provides an approach for the development and application of fish oil liposomes.
10.3390/biom16121721: Distant hybridization brings divergent parental genomes into a shared nucleus and may trigger genomic shock. TE derepression can accompany this response and further promote genomic instability. Yet some hybrids remain stable and fertile. How divergent parental TEs are retained and regulated in such hybrids remains unclear. We investigated a fertile diploid intergeneric hybrid (Megalobrama amblycephala, ♀ × Culter alburnus, ♂) that retains both parental chromosome sets. This hybrid system allows us to compare TE occupancy and regulatory patterns associated with each parental species across the F1 haplotypes. Here, we generated a 2.11 Gb chromosome-level, haplotype-resolved genome of hybrid and performed multi-omics analyses. Among 6347 parent-informative Pan-TE clusters, 507 (8.0%) showed ≥2-fold parental differences in genomic occupancy, with divergence concentrated in LTR-associated elements. Of these parent-biased clusters, 90.7% retained the same bias in F1 haplotypes. Pan-TE transcription largely remained within the parental range. Parental DNA methylation and chromatin accessibility showed strong matched-parent rank correspondence, although relative parental contrasts were less concordant, particularly for chromatin accessibility. Parental divergence in TE genomic occupancy was associated with larger deviations in chromatin accessibility, but not with transgressive expression. Together, these findings reveal stable TE accommodation, characterized by broad retention of matched-parent epigenetic patterns, selective reorganization of parental contrasts, and largely parental-range TE transcription. This work advances understanding of hybrid genome compatibility and may inform the development of stable hybrid breeding materials.
10.56201/ijgem.vol.12.no11.2026.pg192.20: Aquaculture effluent can introduce dissolved nutrients, metals and veterinary pharmaceuticals to shallow groundwater where ponds and waste-disposal structures are hydraulically connected to permeable sediments. This study evaluated the spatial occurrence of selected heavy metals and antibiotic residues in groundwater associated with unlined fish ponds in Kokori, western Niger Delta, Nigeria. Seventeen groundwater sampling locations associated with eight fish-farming areas yielded 25 water samples comprising eight borehole samples and 17 hand-dug-well samples. Ten subsurface soil samples were collected by hand auger to a maximum depth of 4 m and characterized by sieve analysis. Field measurements included pH, electrical conductivity (EC), total dissolved solids (TDS), dissolved oxygen (DO) and biochemical oxygen demand (BOD); cadmium (Cd), lead (Pb), chromium (Cr) and manganese (Mn) were determined by atomic absorption spectrophotometry, while tetracycline, chloramphenicol and formalin were analyzed using procedures based on HPLC and Nash methods respectively. Groundwater was acidic, with mean pH values of 5.58-5.77. Mean Cd concentrations were 0.0041 mg/L in boreholes and 0.0048 mg/L in hand-dug wells close to ponds, compared with 0.0020 mg/L in hand-dug wells located farther from the farms; the first two means exceed the 0.003 mg/L value. The Mean Pb and Cr concentrations remained below the corresponding drinking-water values. Mean Mn increased from 0.14 mg/L in wells near ponds to 0.17 mg/L in the farther well group. Mean tetracycline declined from 0.26 to 0.006 µg/L between the near-pond and farther well groups, corresponding to approximately 97.7% spatial attenuation, whereas chloramphenicol declined from 0.011 to 0.005 µg/L (approximately 54.5%). The patterns are consistent with attenuation during subsurface transport. The findings demonstrate localized deterioration of shallow groundwater quality near aquaculture facilities and support improved effluent management, appropriate siting of water supply wells, and routine monitoring of aquaculture-impacted groundwater.
10.3389/fmars.2026.2021262: The aquaculture industry supplied 94.4 million tonnes of aquatic animals in 2022, which constituted nearly half of global aquatic animal production, yet most feeds still rely on fishmeal and fish oil from forage-fish fisheries that cannot be scaled any further. This review considers alternative proteins, feed biotechnology, and gut microbiome modulation as one connected system rather than three separate research lines. It covers six groups of alternative proteins, eight processing and biotechnology tools (microbiological, biochemical, thermal, and chemical), and nine microbiome modulation strategies, and it compares marine carnivorous species with freshwater omnivorous species. Replacement ceilings depend largely on habitat and feeding guilds, where freshwater omnivores such as tilapia tolerate high plant-protein inclusion, whereas marine carnivores usually keep growth and gut health only up to roughly 20 to 35% fishmeal protein replacement with a single ingredient. Processing that removes anti-nutritional factors or opens cell walls raises these ceilings in some trials but not in others. The gut microbiome is a plausible mediator between ingredient and host health; substrate supply and taxonomic shifts are better documented than microbial metabolites and signaling, and causal evidence is scarce. From a One Health perspective, lower antimicrobial use, reduced nutrient discharge, and preserved fillet omega-3 content have each been supported in part, but never together for the same feed. A central gap is the lack of studies linking life cycle assessment to microbiome-mediated health outcomes. Future work should focus on precision aquafeeds, artificial intelligence (AI)-assisted formulation, and non-lethal biomarkers.
10.3390/microorganisms14122763: Intensive aquaculture creates interconnected host, microbial, and environmental conditions that facilitate bacterial disease emergence and spread. Conventional surveillance relies heavily on clinical signs, bacterial isolation, and laboratory confirmation, potentially delaying intervention until infection is established. This review summarizes advances in bacterial disease surveillance in aquaculture, focusing on the transition from individual-animal diagnosis to population-level monitoring and early warning. Culture-based methods remain essential for recovering viable bacteria and obtaining isolates for further characterization. Biochemical identification and MALDI-TOF MS facilitate bacterial identification, whereas immunological assays provide complementary antigen- or antibody-based detection. Phenotypic antimicrobial susceptibility testing further supports the characterization of resistance profiles. Molecular methods, including PCR, quantitative PCR, multiplex PCR, and digital PCR, improve sensitivity and support pathogen quantification, whereas loop-mediated isothermal amplification, recombinase polymerase amplification (RPA), recombinase-aided amplification (RAA), and CRISPR/Cas assays offer opportunities for rapid, field-deployable detection. Environmental DNA monitoring, biosensors, microfluidic systems, whole-genome sequencing, and metagenomics extend surveillance to water, sediment, biofilms, and connected production environments, enabling the analysis of pathogen dynamics, strain relationships, virulence-associated determinants, and antimicrobial resistance. However, detecting bacterial nucleic acids or resistance genes alone does not establish pathogen viability, disease causation, or phenotypic resistance. Moreover, subclinical pathogen detection should not automatically be interpreted as predictive early warning because lead times and farm-specific alert thresholds remain insufficiently validated for most bacterial pathogens. Effective early warning therefore requires standardized sampling, validated assays, longitudinal field studies, and interpretation alongside host health, environmental conditions, and epidemiological evidence. Integrating complementary technologies into risk-based surveillance frameworks could support earlier intervention and strengthen bacterial disease prevention and biosecurity in aquaculture.
10.3389/fmars.2026.1995737: Introduction The marine environment contains vicariant barriers that are less apparent than those of freshwater or terrestrial systems. These obstacles, often oceanographic features and seafloor topography, can hinder dispersal and gene flow. This is particularly true amongst bottom dwelling species such as demersal fishes. To overcome this, many demersal species have biphasic life histories that can facilitate gene flow through pelagic larvae, connecting otherwise isolated populations. One such species is the gelatinous snailfish, Liparis fabricii . It is amongst the most widespread and abundant fish species native to the Arctic Ocean, and is an important forage species, linking both pelagic and demersal components of Arctic food webs. Materials and methods Here, we used genome-wide single nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) and mitochondrial protein-coding genes (mtPCGs) to investigate its population structure throughout the Arctic. Results We found small, but significant, population genetic structuring between regions, with the most distinctive structural signature observed in individuals from Baffin Bay. Despite vast distances between sampling sites, gene flow and physical migration was evident between regions, likely facilitated through its prolonged pelagic larval stage. Discussion As climate change affects Arctic fish communities, identifying patterns of genetic connectivity and biogeographic boundaries amongst fish populations is crucial for the understanding and management of Arctic marine ecosystems.
10.3390/su182312002: Seafood ecolabeling has recently highlighted the global concern about overexploitation of fish stocks. While seafood ecolabeling is generally viewed as a valuable tool for increasing the value of certified fisheries, it has faced criticism regarding the credibility and fairness of its assessments. This study matches MSC assessment scores with fishery statuses in the RAM Legacy Stock Assessment Database using scientific species names and fishing grounds as criteria, and constructs a comparison group of uncertified fisheries targeting the same species in different fishing areas, to investigate whether the assessment scores are appropriately set to preserve fish stocks and regulate fishing activity. MSC-certified fisheries were associated with higher stock levels and lower exploitation rates. The results generally support the notion that MSC-certified fisheries were associated with higher stock levels in the post-certification period. 10.1111/fme.70124: ABSTRACT Dominica's small-scale fisheries provide vital food and income for coastal communities but face increasing pressure from climate-driven shifts in fish distributions, reef degradation, and extreme events such as Hurricane Maria in 2017, which caused catastrophic damage. The dataset, comprising 3007 measurements sampled at 12 landing sites, provides a detailed picture of catches and size distributions. 10.3390/foods15234227: This study aimed to assess the potential human health risks associated with metal and metalloids exposure through the consumption of gilthead seabream (Sparus aurata), common sole (Solea solea), and marbled spinefoot (Siganus rivulatus) collected from the Suez Canal, Egypt. 10.1128/aem.01597-26: ABSTRACT Intensive aquaculture is experiencing bottlenecks due to diseases caused by bacterial pathogens, such as Flavobacterium psychrophilum , the agent of Bacterial Cold-Water Disease and Rainbow Trout Fry Syndrome in salmonids. With rising antimicrobial resistance and limited vaccine efficacy, biocontrol alternatives are needed. Here, we developed an integrated screening pipeline to isolate native bacterial antagonists of F. psychrophilum from a rainbow trout recirculating aquaculture system. Combining an agar-based inhibition assay, in silico antimicrobial resistance, and virulence screening, and ecotoxicity evaluation toward Raphidocelis subcapitata and Daphnia magna , we identified three Flavobacterium -antagonizing strains with favorable preliminary safety profiles: Pseudomonas palmensis BG17, Rhodococcus qingshengii IW15, and Janthinobacterium sp. CB21. Cell-free supernatants of these isolates suppressed F. psychrophilum growth in vitro , with concentration-dependent effects for CB21 and IW15, and across the tested supernatant dilution range for BG17. Growth of antagonists in 50 μM and 200 μM FeCl 3 reduced pathogen inhibition by BG17 across all supernatant concentrations. Its iron-free supernatant absorbed near 405 nm and fluoresced at 440-445 nm, while direct FeCl 3 addition shifted both signals, and growth of the antagonist in extra iron reduced them. Together with an NRPS cluster of low similarity to a characterized pyoverdine biosynthetic gene cluster (BGC) and a positive CAS assay, these findings are consistent with an iron-responsive fluorescent chelator in BG17. The effect of iron on the inhibition caused by IW15 supernatant differed depending on the iron concentration tested, suggesting a more complex iron-responsive phenotype rather than a simple concentration-dependent effect. Inhibition by CB21 supernatant was not significantly affected by iron under the tested conditions, and its genome did not encode a dedicated siderophore BGC. These aquaculture-native isolates inhibit F. psychrophilum in vitro through apparently distinct mechanisms and warrant further evaluation as biocontrol candidates. IMPORTANCE Worldwide production of intensively farmed salmonids in aquaculture represents a valuable source of high-quality protein but is challenged by significant losses caused by bacterial pathogens, such as Flavobacterium psychrophilum . On a global scale, outbreaks are treated with antibiotics, leading to the development of antimicrobial resistance, while farm effluents can spread resistant bacteria into surrounding freshwater ecosystems, even reaching human pathogens with clinical relevance. Safer biocontrol alternatives are necessary, and probiotics have gained interest as a promising option. Here, we describe three native bacterial strains from a rainbow trout farming environment that through apparently distinct mechanisms inhibit the tested F. psychrophilum strain in vitro . The strains were selected via combined genomic safety and ecotoxicity screening on non-target eukaryotic organisms. By integrating functional, genomic safety, and environmental criteria early in the in vitro screening process, this study advances a One Health approach to develop sustainable disease management alternatives for aquaculture.
10.3390/d18120735: A globally recognized biodiversity hotspot, the Dniester Estuary supports an extremely rich and valuable ichthyofauna of high conservation status and commercial interest. This matrix of wetlands plays a crucial role in preserving the diversity of fish in the Dniester River basin and the northwestern Black Sea, serving as a key ecological buffer, refuge, foraging ground, and spawning place enabling smooth migratory transitions for many species. Human-induced climate change is driving a sea-level rise within the Black Sea, a phenomenon that is likely to critically disrupt the aquatic and semi-aquatic ecosystems and related fish diversity of the Dniester Estuary, its adjacent low-lying floodplains, and the neighboring marine coasts, directly threatening the fish fauna. In this sea-level rise risk assessment, 53 fish species were studied (Gobiidae, 18; Cobitidae, 8; Percidae, 7; Clupeidae, 5; Mugilidae, 3; Syngnathidae, 3; Gasterosteidae, 2; and one species each for Siluridae, Esocidae, Umbridae, Lotidae, Atherinidae, Centrarchidae, and Pleuronectidae). As a result of sea-level rise, three fish species will be strongly negatively impacted (Misgurnus fossilis, Umbra krameria, and Zingel streber), five will be moderately negatively impacted (Cobitis taenia, Lota lota, Sander lucioperca, Neogobius gymnotrachelus, and Alosa pontica), three will be weakly moderately negative impacted (Sabanejewia baltica, Silurus glanis, and Esox lucius), four will be neutrally impacted (Benthophilus brauneri, Clupeonella cultriventris, Syngnathus argentatus, and Nerophis teres), ten will be neutrally to positively impacted (Pungitius platygaster, Gasterosteus aculeatus, Lepomis gibbosus, Percarina demidoffii, Neogobius melanostomus, Engraulis encrasicolus, Liza haematochelius, L. aurata, L. saliens, and Platichthys flesus), and one will be positively influenced (Atherina pontica).
10.1017/s0030605325102378: Abstract The fishing cat Prionailurus viverrinus in Southeast Asia is threatened by habitat destruction and poaching. In Cambodia, despite the availability of suitable habitat in extensive wetlands, evidence of the species’ presence is scarce. This study presents the results of surveys for fishing cats at four wetland sites, a review of all records of presence and an assessment of the extent of predicted suitable habitat in Cambodia. We also report on threats to fishing cat survival and a population estimate to inform the species’ categorization on the IUCN Red List. Camera-trap surveys showed a decline in frequency of captures during 2017-2023. More recent records from 2021-2023 confirmed a breeding population in the mangrove wetlands of south-west Cambodia. There were no records of presence on the Tonle Sap Lake floodplain in central Cambodia (2021-2022) or along the Mekong River (2022), apart from a single photographic record south-east of Tonle Sap Lake in 2022. The presence of wetlands and high levels of precipitation were predictors of fishing cat presence, and 17% of Cambodia’s wetlands are predicted to offer suitable habitat. We identified 19 protected areas as priority sites for conservation action and population monitoring. High priority sites (c. 5% of Cambodia was identified as highly suitable habitat) are located along the coast and moderately suitable areas (c. 12.5% of Cambodia) on the Tonle Sap floodplain. Poaching and deforestation are the main threats to fishing cats in Cambodia. We extrapolated the size of the fishing cat population from available data and estimated 34-67 individuals in Cambodia, which is low and warrants urgent and effective conservation action.
10.1080/10888705.2026.2760878: Aquatic animal welfare is increasingly recognised as essential to sustainable aquaculture in Latin America and the Caribbean (LAC). This study identified the principal welfare challenges perceived by scientists, Competent National Authority staff, and industry professionals during a three-day online workshop. Latent Dirichlet Allocation was used to analyse responses concerning nutrition, environment, health, and behaviour across developmental stages, production systems, transport, slaughter, and species-specific issues. Major concerns included animal-based assessments, feeding strategies, and sanitary conditions. Across developmental stages, participants emphasised feed quality, stress, cannibalism, sanitation, and spawning behaviour. Production-system challenges included water quality, stocking density, predator exposure, and facilities supporting natural behaviours. Participants also highlighted limited veterinary capacity and inadequate behavioural assessment tools. Transport and slaughter priorities included capacity building, protocol standardisation, and reducing stress and suffering. Species-specific concerns focused on nutrition, behaviour, and disease diagnosis. Overall, stakeholders recognised substantial gaps in theoretical knowledge and practical capacity. Priorities included nutrition, stress reduction, water management, environmental-impact mitigation, husbandry, personnel training, and comprehensive guidance to strengthen welfare assessment and implementation across species, life stages, and aquaculture production contexts throughout the LAC aquaculture sector.
10.3390/aquacj6040064: Aquaculture is increasingly recognised as a key sector for achieving global development goals, including improving nutrition, ending hunger, poverty reduction, and economic growth. This paper presents a framework for building a climate-resilient aquaculture value chain, using Kenya as a case study. Drawing on data collected through workshops, interviews and field observations, the study identifies the four key stages of the aquaculture value chain most affected by climate change: feed production, fish production, transportation and distribution, and post-harvest processing. It also maps relevant stakeholders and outlines specific adaptation pathways such as ecosystem-based approaches, policy reforms, and technical innovations that can be co-produced to enhance resilience at each stage. The framework emphasises the importance of multi-stakeholder collaboration and highlights the need for inclusive approaches that address gender and socio-economic inequalities within the sector. Findings suggest that, despite existing institutional and infrastructural challenges, there is a strong appetite among stakeholders in Kenya for collective action. 10.9734/jsrr/2026/v32i114774: Integrated fish-livestock farming offers a means of recycling livestock waste within pond-based aquaculture, potentially reducing dependence on purchased inputs. This study evaluated fish production, water quality and economic outcomes under four farming systems in Kolli Hills, Namakkal district, Tamil Nadu. 10.3389/faquc.2026.1992667: Offshore aquaculture is widely recognized as the next frontier for animal production. Several candidate species for offshore aquaculture development have been identified for the United States (U.S.), with striped bass ( Morone saxatilis ) emerging as one of the leading contenders. Marine spatial planning methods use robust tools to identify suitable space for emerging industries but often focus on minimizing risks and conflicts rather than identifying the most suitable locations for production. While some areas on the West Coast experience several days at suitable temperatures, they generally do not reach the optimal thermal range required for striped bass aquaculture. In contrast, three subregions along the Atlantic and Gulf coasts were identified as having the highest potential for offshore striped bass aquaculture: North Carolina, the Florida Atlantic coast, and the Northern Gulf. As ocean temperatures rise, these select regions will largely stay within suitable ranges but experience less time within optimal temperatures by mid-century.
10.1111/jwas.70173: Abstract Aquaculture has been identified as a viable approach to address the socio-ecological challenges facing wild-capture fisheries. However, its success is not merely a technocratic matter of deploying new technology; it depends on communities' acceptance and active participation. This is especially important for communities deeply connected to wild-capture fisheries, where aquaculture may be perceived as disrupting their identity and well-being. Framing plays an important role in community acceptance, as the ways in which aquaculture's benefits are presented can shape levels of public support. We examined community acceptance of aquaculture by comparing framings around food security, environmental benefits, and economic development and by identifying the factors that shape support within each. Using a structured questionnaire administered to 948 North Carolina residents, we found that community acceptance differed significantly depending on how the benefits of aquaculture were framed. Support for aquaculture was highest when framed in terms of economic benefits and lowest when framed in terms of ecological benefits. The predictors of acceptance varied across framings. However, the perceived need for aquaculture was the only factor that consistently influenced support across all outcomes. These findings highlight that aquaculture's legitimacy and acceptance depend on the alignment between emphasized benefits and residents' individual values, climate attitudes, and perceived local priorities. More broadly, they suggest that communication strategies for aquaculture development may be more effective when tailored to the values and concerns most salient to the intended audience and that governance processes attentive to community expectations may help build broader support.
10.1111/1462-2920.70476: ABSTRACT While the expansion of macroalgae on coral reefs is a global concern, the spatial scales and mechanisms through which macroalgae inhibit coral recruitment processes and the role of epilithic bacteria in coral settlement remain inadequately understood. Using tiles preconditioned at three distances of two algal species in both up and down-current directions, we show that macroalgae shape early epilithic bacterial assemblages, with strong effects 1 cm downstream of both algae. When exposing the tiles to larvae of two coral species in ex situ settlement experiments, the coral Acropora pulchra showed reduced larval settlement on cryptic surfaces of tiles conditioned 1 cm up and downstream of the alga Dictyota bartayresiana , whereas the coral Pocillopora acuta showed the opposite pattern. Specific bacterial taxa within the families Bdellovibrionaceae, Pirellulaceae, Flavobacteriaceae and Rhodobacteraceae were associated with P. acuta settlement with differences across algal species. When tiles with coral spat were returned to their initial positions on the reef, spat survival was consistently reduced closer to, and particularly 1 cm downstream of, D. bartayresiana . These results demonstrate that macroalgae influence coral settlement and post-settlement survival at centimetre scales through distance- and flow-dependent effects and indicate that these effects may be mediated by epilithic bacterial assemblages.
10.3389/fmars.2026.1976839: Introduction Coastal urbanization and land-use changes have increased terrigenous sediment inputs into tropical marine ecosystems, altering benthic habitat structure. While broad functional-group models are commonly applied to assess sedimentation impacts on coral reefs, species-level responses remain poorly understood. To evaluate the influence of local sedimentation regimes on macroalgal community structure, species composition and sediment deposition rates were monitored across five sampling periods in 2014 at two fringing reefs with contrasting environmental exposures (Caleta de Chon and Zacatoso) in the Mexican Tropical Pacific. Methods Sedimentation rates were partitioned into fine and coarse fractions, and macroalgal diversity and assemblage composition were evaluated using taxonomic identification to the species level. Results Macroalgal species diversity ( H’ ) exhibited significant spatial contrasts during May ( t = 3.55, df = 10.87, p = 0.0046) and November ( t = 3.34, df = 25.85, p = 0.0025), with Caleta de Chon consistently supporting higher diversity and species richness than Zacatoso. Multivariate community composition differed significantly between reefs (one-way PERMANOVA, F = 2.495, p = 0.0074), but showed no significant temporal variation ( F = 0.9148, p = 0.6571). Two-way PERMANOVA revealed a strong main temporal effect on deposition rates (F4,59 = 18.35, p = 0.0001) and a significant site-by-time interaction ( F 4,59 = 2.69, p = 0.0252), despite no main effect of reef location ( F 1,59 = 1.87, p = 0.1673). Both reefs experienced a synchronous total sedimentation peak in May (0.031 g m -2 d -1 at Caleta de Chon vs. 0.034 g m -2 d -1 at Zacatoso); however, deposition at Caleta de Chon was dominated by fine silts (0.022 g m -2 d -1 ), whereas Zacatoso was driven by a coarse sediment pulse (0.0209 g m -2 d -1 ). Discussion These findings demonstrate that local geomorphology and hydrodynamic energy filter sediment grain-size fractions, shaping distinct macroalgal assemblage structures at local spatial scales despite shared regional weather drivers. Evaluating species-level composition alongside sediment grain-size fractions provides high diagnostic resolution to disentangle coastal watershed runoff from wave-driven bedload transport, establishing a critical baseline to anticipate benthic community shifts under accelerating coastal development
10.1111/jfd.70327: ABSTRACT Streptococcus agalactiae is one of the most serious diseases in Nile tilapia aquaculture. The total bacterial counts in the liver of FF + OTC-treated fish were significantly lower than those of the control group (1.05 and 5.15 × 107 CFU/ g , respectively). 10.3390/fishes11120690: Piscidins are fish-exclusive antimicrobial peptides (AMPs) with broad-spectrum and immunomodulatory activity. Piscidin paralogues with divergent expression are widespread in fish, but how their transcription is regulated remains unknown. Mapping their cDNAs onto the published genome assembly yielded over 30-kb sequences covering the genes and their flanking regions. Interestingly, these piscidin genes form a tandem array in a syntenic cluster on chromosome 12 (ecPis3-ecPis1-ecPis2-ecPis4). This arrangement is conserved among five groupers examined by micro-collinearity. Predicted transcription factor (TF) binding repertoires differed among the promoters, and KEGG enrichment results were interpreted with a focus on immune system and signal transduction pathways. Dual-luciferase assays indicated paralogue-specific control: MAFA and MAFBb activated ecPis1 and ecPis2 promoters, whereas MAFF and MAFK reduced their activity; ESR1 activated ecPis4 promoter and ZBTB26-like reduced that of ecPis3. 10.3390/fishes11120691: Acrossocheilus longipinnis (Wu, 1939) is a species endemic to China and distributed in the Pearl River basin. The genome is 16,597 bp in length and contains 37 genes and one control region, with an A + T content of 55.95%, showing a pronounced AT bias. The 13 PCGs span 11,410 bp in total; COX1 starts with GTG, whereas the remaining 12 PCGs start with ATG, and some genes end with the incomplete stop codons T- or TA-. A total of 3619 codons were identified, with leucine codons being the most abundant and CUA having the highest usage frequency. Of the 22 tRNAs, all except trnS1, which lacks the DHU arm, fold into the canonical cloverleaf structure. The Ka/Ks values of the 13 PCGs ranged from 0.02 to 0.19 and were all lower than 1, indicating that these genes have experienced strong purifying selection during evolution; ND6 had the highest Ka/Ks value and COX1 the lowest. While the whole-mitochondrial-genome tree exhibited topological conflicts likely due to alignment ambiguities in the non-coding regions, the strictly aligned 13 PCGs provided a more robust matrilineal signal.
10.3390/fishes11120693: Aeromonas veronii is a prevalent opportunistic pathogen that causes severe disease and economic losses in freshwater aquaculture. In this study, two A. veronii strains, designated Ly-Av-1 and Ly-Av-2, were isolated from diseased large-scale loach (Paramisgurnus dabryanus) exhibiting different clinical symptoms. Hemolytic activity on blood agar, virulence gene profiles and antimicrobial susceptibility of the isolates were determined. Following artificial infection of loaches, serum activities of AKP, ACP, ALT, AST, SOD, CAT, GSH-Px and MDA content were measured. Meanwhile, the expression of oxidative stress-related genes and immune-related genes in the liver, spleen, kidney and skin was also evaluated. The results showed that infection with both A. veronii strains induced hepatic injury and upregulated the expression of immune genes in the spleen. Strain Ly-Av-1 exhibited hemolytic activity in vitro and caused skin swelling, ulceration and marginal hemorrhage in infected P. dabryanus. Compared with Ly-Av-2, Ly-Av-1 had a lower LD50 and harbored virulence genes hlyA, alt and lip. Oxidative stress injury and elevated expression of inflammatory factors were detected in loaches infected with Ly-Av-1. In contrast, Ly-Av-2, in which the hlyA gene was not detected, induced skin swelling and ulceration without skin hemorrhage. These results indicate that differences in virulence-gene repertoires drive divergent host oxidative stress and immune outcomes during A. veronii infection. 10.3390/fishes11120689: Artificial propagation of chub mackerel (Scomber japonicus) has recently been achieved in China, making ocular health an emerging concern for farmed stocks. Adipose eyelid opacification, distinct from the ophthalmia reported in Japan, remains poorly characterized, and its structural and molecular basis and potential link to mortality are unresolved. In a farm survey of 300 early-life live fish, 21 (7%) exhibited this phenotype; technicians reported that affected fish appeared more likely to die, although survival and growth were not systematically quantified. We compared transparent (HG) and opacified (WG) eyelids using histology, optical measurements, transcriptomics, proteomics, and RT-qPCR, with three biological replicates per group. Opacified tissues showed structural disorganization, higher relative opacity signals (600 nm: 30.79 ± 9.05 in HG vs. 84.20 ± 4.94 in WG, mean ± SD), and pigment-like aggregates. Proteomics revealed decreased abundance of keratins (e.g., KRT8, KRT15) and ECM-associated proteins (e.g., COL12A1A, EMILIN1A), but increased abundance of the cell-adhesion protein CDH2 and stress-response chaperones (e.g., HSPD1, HSP90AB1) in WG. Transcriptomic data, treated as exploratory due to technical constraints, suggested alterations in structural and inflammatory pathways (e.g., lum, l1cam, arpc1a/b), which were partially supported by RT-qPCR. Exploratory bacterial profiling described genus-level differences involving Vibrio and Photobacterium without establishing infection. These findings provide candidate molecular targets and baseline information for further investigation of adipose eyelid opacification in cultured chub mackerel.
10.3390/fishes11120692: Quasipaa spinosa, the Chinese spiny frog, is a commercially important amphibian for which captive production commonly relies on live mealworms (Tenebrio molitor), while some farms have adopted formulated feeds. We conducted a farm-based observational survey comparing two existing adult populations at a commercial farm, one maintained on live mealworms (JA) and the other on formulated feed (JB). Thirty frogs per population were assessed for body weight and linear morphological traits, and six frogs per population were further examined for intestinal morphology, digestive enzyme and antioxidant indices, and 16S rRNA-based gut microbiota. Frogs from JB were larger at sampling, and intestinal length was greater, whereas eight intestinal histomorphological indices were broadly comparable. Trypsin, α-amylase, lipase, CAT, SOD, MDA, and T-AOC did not differ detectably, while GSH-Px activity was higher in JB. Gut microbial alpha diversity showed no detectable differences, whereas exploratory Bray-Curtis-based analyses suggested metric-dependent differences in microbial community composition. JA samples showed a higher relative representation of several lactic acid bacteria-related genera, whereas JB samples exhibited greater relative abundances of Cetobacterium and Terrisporobacter, genera that have been previously associated with vitamin B12 metabolism and amino-acid fermentation, respectively. Overall, these observations document an established commercial population maintained on formulated feed and identify morphological, physiological, and microbial patterns that warrant further evaluation in replicated studies.
10.3389/fmars.2026.1939537: Introduction The study was conducted along the eastern Adriatic coast to assess whether otolith elemental signatures can differentiate nursery types of gilthead seabream ( Sparus aurata ) and support inference of age-class-3 fish nursery origin. Methods A total of 143 specimens were collected from 11 sites, including 76 juveniles sampled between May and June 2021 and 67 age-class-3 fish sampled between December 2023 and April 2024. Adult specimens were selected from a larger dataset assembled for ongoing studies of Sparus aurata . Age had been estimated by reading annual growth increments in the otoliths, and only specimens assigned to age class 3 were included in the present study. Otolith-based age estimates were therefore used as a specimen-selection criterion. Laser ablation inductively coupled plasma mass spectrometry (LA-ICP-MS) measurements of the otolith region corresponding to the juvenile nursery stage were used to derive the Q10 and Q90 concentration descriptors for Sr, Na, and Mg.K-means clustering identified two chemically distinct clusters, with the optimal number of clusters determined by a silhouette analysis. Cluster stability was determined using a combination of bootstrap resampling and Jaccard similarity index. Results Principal component analysis showed separation between clusters, primarily along PC1, which was mainly associated with Sr Q10, Sr Q90 and Na Q10. Cluster assignments corresponded closely with nursery type classifications: Nursery Type N 1 was predominantly associated with Cluster 1, whereas Nursery Type N 2 showed greater site-specific variability and mixed cluster composition. 92.86% of N1 individuals were assigned to Cluster 1, compared with 47.06% of N2 individuals assigned to Cluster 2. All three PC1-associated parameters differ significantly between clusters and nursery types. Sr-related variables were higher in Cluster 2 and N 2 , whereas mean Na and Na Q10 were higher in Cluster 1 and N 1 , indicating distinct otolith chemical profiles among groups. Distributional descriptors, particularly Q10 and Q90, provided stronger discrimination than mean values alone. When age-class-3 fish specimens were included, the two-cluster structure was largely retained, although some boundary individuals showed classification uncertainty. Based on the juvenile otolith region in age-class-3 fish otoliths, A 1 age-class-3 fish were mainly associated with Cluster 1 (66.67%), which resembled N 1 , whereas A 2 sub-adults more often belonged to Cluster 2 (64.86%), which suggest differing nursery contributions to the age-class-3 fish sampling areas, alongside substantial overlap in otolith chemical profiles. Discussion These results indicate that otolith elemental signatures retain ecologically meaningful information and may support inference of nursery origin, with potential application in targeted conservation and management of S. aurata stocks.
10.3389/fmars.2026.1938640: Seagrass recovery depends on aligning scientific research, community leadership, governance, and locally relevant priorities. The diverse ecological and social functions of seagrass position it as a useful ‘boundary object’: a shared reference point through which different actors can collaborate without requiring identical understandings. This Community Case Study examines this role through a collaborative programme of seagrass research and stewardship in Sanday, Orkney, UK, developed with Sanday Development Trust. Sanday supports approximately 21 ha of Zostera marina meadows alongside diverse marine habitats and cultural practices, while facing increasing coastal erosion associated with climate change. Since 2022, participatory mapping, ecological research, reciprocal capacity-building, educational co-design, cultural practice, and policy dialogue have connected seagrass stewardship with wider priorities for coastal and island resilience. Local knowledge helped identify previously undocumented seagrass meadows and was translated through ecological research into georeferenced habitat evidence subsequently incorporated into government datasets and regional marine planning. Reciprocal training and field support have expanded monitoring capability, while educational co-design enabled scientific understandings of seagrass to be reinterpreted through pupils’ preferred approaches to learning and incorporated into locally relevant lesson plans. Creative practice translated relatively inaccessible submerged ecology into locally meaningful cultural forms, while collaboration with Sanday Development Trust increasingly connected seagrass research with multi-habitat restoration, coastal erosion, adaptation, and wider island resilience planning. Across these activities, seagrass was understood and valued differently by residents, researchers, educators, community organisations, cultural actors, and planners, while remaining a recognisable shared reference point through which knowledge, meanings, and priorities could be translated and coordinated. Collaboration did not imply consensus or equal authority between actors, but enabled different forms of expertise and institutional responsibility to interact around a common ecological object. This case demonstrates how seagrass can support place-based collaboration across different social worlds, embedding habitat recovery within wider social-ecological systems and community priorities.
10.3389/fmars.2026.2015479: To investigate zooplankton size structure and its environmental drivers, a survey was conducted off the Shandong Peninsula in May 2025 using ZooScan, d-RDA, and structural equation models (SEMs). Normalized biovolume size spectrum (NBVS) parameters and environmental traits exhibited pronounced spatial heterogeneity. The terrestrially influenced Bohai Sea-characterized by higher temperature, shallower depth, lower salinity, and elevated TSS, nutrient, and Chl-a levels-displayed steep NBVS slopes (-2.58 to -0.60) and lower mean equivalent spherical diameter (Mean ESD) and plankton particle size diversity index (PSDI). Conversely, the deeper, higher-salinity Yellow Sea maintained flatter slopes (-1.40 to -0.10) and significantly higher Mean ESD and PSDI ( p < 0.05). d-RDA showed environmental variables explained 21.7% of size-structure variance ( p = 0.001, Adj. R 2 = 0.217), reflecting a gradient from nearshore terrestrial influences to offshore oceanographic conditions. SEMs results further revealed regional differences in the environmental association pathways of the NBVS slope between the Bohai and Yellow Seas. The Bohai Sea operated under a “resource-driven” regime, where Chl-a accumulation acted as the dominant driver steepening NBVS slopes; whereas the Yellow Sea exhibited an “environment-driven” pattern directly constrained by water temperature and depth. These findings demonstrate that NBVS metrics can serve as sensitive indicators for coastal ecological health monitoring.
10.3389/fmars.2026.1984103: Mass mortality events affecting marine bivalves can have important ecological and socioeconomic consequences, yet their underlying causes often remain poorly understood. The Noah’s ark shell ( Arca noae ) is an ecologically and commercially valuable Mediterranean bivalve, and in July 2022, approximately 90% of individuals in natural populations from the Ebro Delta (northwestern Mediterranean Sea) were affected by a severe mortality event. To investigate potential factors contributing to this event, a mortality-affected site was compared with a nearby site where no mortality was observed, integrating environmental, microbiological, histopathological, and experimental evidence. A total of 166 bacterial isolates were recovered, with Acinetobacter johnsonii and Enterobacter sp. exclusively detected in samples from the mortality-affected site. Experimental challenges with one representative isolate of each bacterial taxon showed that both isolates significantly reduced host survival, resulting in cumulative mortalities of 81-85%, compared with 26% in controls, indicating their potential to contribute to host mortality under the experimental conditions tested. Samples from the mortality-affected site showed marked differences in microbiome composition, including reduced alpha diversity and differences in community structure, together with higher relative abundances of Acinetobacter , Enterobacter , and Stenotrophomonas . Histopathological examination revealed more severe lesions in the digestive gland and gills, including hemocytic infiltration, epithelial sloughing, and necrosis. Environmental analyses revealed significant differences in temperature, salinity, dissolved oxygen, and chlorophyll- a between sites, suggesting that environmental conditions may have contributed to host susceptibility. Together, these findings support a multifactorial mortality scenario in which environmental conditions, host alterations, and differences in the microbiome may have interacted to contribute to mortality in A. noae . This integrated evidence highlights the complexity of mortality events in this species and provides a basis for future surveillance and health management of natural populations.
10.3389/fmars.2026.1981790: The toxigenic marine dinoflagellate Ostreopsis cf. ovata and accompanying periphytic diatoms were studied over two annual cycles on a reef platform at Llavaneres, Catalonia, Spain. In each year, as the Ostreopsis bloom peaked, a large centric diatom began to appear and became dominant as the Ostreopsis declined. Previous records at Llavaneres and elsewhere along Catalan and Mediterranean coast, and also on the Atlantic coast of the Basque country, similarly document a temporal association between the later phases of Ostreopsis blooms and the abundance of a large centric diatom. The diatom at Llavaneres and at Donostia was identified as Actinocyclus cf. subtilis and examination of historical materials revealed close agreement between the Llavaneres specimens and some of the earliest records of A. subtilis , in brown mucilaginous growths on rocks in the UK. Elsewhere, large centric diatoms associated with Ostreopsis in the benthos have sometimes been identified as the planktonic genus Coscinodiscus , but this may be because the pseudonodulus characteristic of Actinocyclus cannot be detected in living or uncleaned cells. The association between Ostreopsis and Actinocyclus is often physically close, with healthy Actinocyclus growing alongside Ostreopsis in a common mucilaginous matrix. Our findings are significant in (1) demonstrating an in situ shift in dominance from Ostreopsis to Actinocyclus at a number of Mediterranean and NE Atlantic sites, consistent with (2) a possible tolerance of Actinocyclus to any allelochemicals produced by Ostreopsis ; (3) providing clear documentation of A. cf. subtilis , including recognition of living cells, LM and SEM characterization, and an rbcL based phylogeny; and (4) highlighting a temporal association that suggests Actinocyclus could be explored further as a potential indicator of Ostreopsis bloom decline.
10.3389/fmars.2026.1976619: Introduction In Southeast Asia, 58.6% of elasmobranch fish species are threatened with extinction. The primary threat driver is their targeted and incidental commercial fishing. In Singapore 84.6% of all native elasmobranch species are threatened with extinction, even though there exist no significant commercial fisheries within her territorial waters. Extensive marine urbanization may have contributed to the vulnerability of these populations, although ecological and distributional data remain limited. Methods Using publicly-available records, we characterize elasmobranch diversity and distribution in data-poor Singapore using 977 verified and georeferenced observations over a 25-year period (2000-2024). Results Our findings show that elasmobranch fishes occurred within key coastal marine habitats, underscoring the urgent need to conserve these areas. Discussion We discuss the potential impacts of urbanization, recreational fishing, and abandoned, lost, or otherwise discarded fishing gear (ALDFG) on these threatened taxa. This study demonstrates how long-term data can establish a baseline understanding of Singapore’s wild elasmobranch species and provides a foundation for future ecological research and conservation planning.
10.1007/s10750-026-06481-9: The applicability of species-specific droplet digital PCR (ddPCR) was evaluated for environmental DNA (eDNA) detection of two invasive alien species in the Danube River Basin (DRB): round goby (Neogobius melanostomus) and spiny-cheek crayfish (Faxonius limosus). Available species-specific primers and probes targeting the cytochrome c oxidase subunit I gene were re-assessed in silico and validated in vitro using genomic DNA from specimens caught within the DRB. Analytical sensitivity was assessed by establishing the limit of blank, detection, and quantification, alongside a double-threshold approach for low-level F. limosus detections. Field validation revealed consistently detectable and quantifiable eDNA signals for N. melanostomus, whereas F. limosus was detected only at low levels. Microcosm experiments demonstrated substantially higher eDNA shedding by N. melanostomus and increased F. limosus eDNA signals during molting and increased activity. In addition, higher eDNA signals were observed in DNA extracts obtained from glass microfiber (GF/C) filters compared to Sterivex filters. By integrating field and experimental data, this study highlights the utility and sensitivity of targeted ddPCR-based approach for detecting crayfish eDNA in large rivers, while simultaneously providing a comprehensive evaluation of ecological and species-specific parameters influencing observed eDNA detection patterns of N. melanostomus and F. limosus.
10.1111/eff.70077: ABSTRACT Juvenile cold-water fishes inhabiting seasonally warm rivers must balance tradeoffs among temperature, food availability and energetic costs, yet the riverscape features supporting production remain poorly understood. We combined spatially extensive surveys with temporally intensive growth and bioenergetics analyses to evaluate how juvenile redband trout ( Oncorhynchus mykiss newberrii ) rear within the seasonally warm Sprague River, Upper Klamath Basin, Oregon, USA. We sampled fish distribution across 130 km of mainstem and off-channel habitats using backpack electrofishing, boat electrofishing and snorkelling, then quantified growth and consumption dynamics within core rearing habitats. Juvenile redband trout were patchily distributed, with 60% of sites containing no trout and the top 10% of sites containing 53% of all individuals sampled. Peaks in abundance were associated with two contrasting landscape features: groundwater habitats and a warm, high-gradient canyon reach lacking detectable groundwater inputs. Off-channel groundwater habitats also supported high juvenile densities and rapid growth. Surprisingly, juvenile trout in the warm high-gradient reach also maintained positive summer growth despite temperatures exceeding 27°C. Bioenergetics modelling suggested fish in this habitat compensated for elevated metabolic costs through substantially higher food consumption. Our findings demonstrate that rare riverscape features can disproportionately support salmonid rearing in seasonally warm rivers. By linking spatial patterns of abundance with temporal patterns of growth and energetics, this study provides insight into how habitat heterogeneity may promote adaptive capacity and resilience of cold-water fishes in warming environments.
10.1186/s12915-026-02798-y: Changes in ploidy and genomic composition shape fertility by altering chromosome behavior during gametogenesis, providing a genetic basis for fertility control in agriculture. Recently, we identified a novel amphitriploid female in the Carassius complex with ameio-fusiongenesis, which produces unreduced eggs via ameiotic oogenesis and generates higher-ploidy offspring through egg-sperm fusion.
