We crossed this female with males of three distinct cyprinid species-congeneric amphidiploid C. auratus , distant amphidiploid Cyprinus carpio , and even more distant diploid Ancherythroculter nigrocauda -thereby generating two synthetic octaploids (S8n- Ca and S8n- Cc ) and one synthetic heptaploid (S7n- An ). In early ovaries before 100 days post-hatching (dph), oocytes in all three synthetic allopolyploids underwent apoptosis in association with improper synaptonemal complex assembly and incomplete double-strand break (DSB) repair associated with aneuploidy or failed homologous pairing. Interestingly, between 100 and 140 dph, a small proportion of oocytes initiated alternative pathways. Approximately 5.0% of S8n- Ca oocytes produced unreduced eggs via ameiotic or endoreplicated oogenesis pathways, rendering S8n- Ca females fertile. In contrast, only 0.9% (S8n- Cc ) and 0.7% (S7n- An ) of oocytes underwent endoreplication, yet only those in S8n- Cc developed into mature eggs. Consequently, S8n- Cc females were partially fertile, whereas S7n- An females were completely sterile. Notably, incomplete DSB repair did not compromise spermatocyte development; rather, these cells underwent extensive apoptosis from failed segregation at anaphase I, leading to azoospermia in all three synthetic allopolyploid males. This study reveals a mechanistic association between integrated paternal genomes and sex-specific fertility outcomes, providing a theoretical foundation for generating sterile polyploids in aquatic animal breeding.
10.1177/02611929261507293: Micro-sized and nano-sized plastic particles (MNPs) are ubiquitous in aquatic environments. Fish may mistake them for food or ingest them accidentally during filter feeding. Some MNPs contain heavy metals that, when ingested, can subsequently leach into the digestive tract of the fish, posing health risks to the fish themselves and to animals higher up the food chain, including humans. This study aimed to assess the bioaccessibility of heavy metals leached from MNPs by using an in chemico digestion model. Plastic pellets were crushed and sieved into micro-sized and nano-sized particles. The stomach and intestine of the fish were simulated in vitro to reproduce the digestion process, in order to evaluate leaching capacity, bioaccessibility and the potential human health risk of the heavy metals. The results indicate that heavy metals in the MNPs exhibited varying bioaccessibility (with As in vitro assay could be used to investigate the bioaccessibility of heavy metals and thus avoid the use of fish in in vivo testing.
10.1007/s12011-026-05443-5: Iron is an essential trace element required for numerous physiological and biochemical processes in fish, including oxygen transport, energy metabolism, and antioxidant defence. In aquaculture systems, where natural mineral availability may be insufficient, dietary supplementation of iron plays a critical role in maintaining optimal growth and health. However, both deficiency and excess of iron can adversely affect fish performance, leading to anaemia or oxidative stress, respectively. The bioavailability of iron is influenced by its chemical form, dietary composition, and interactions with other nutrients. Recent advances in aquaculture nutrition have highlighted the potential of nano-scale iron supplementation to enhance iron absorption efficiency and reduce environmental losses. This review provides a comprehensive overview of iron metabolism, dietary requirements, sources, nutrient interactions, deficiency and toxicity effects, and environmental considerations in fish. Furthermore, emerging perspectives on the application of nanotechnology in iron nutrition are discussed, emphasizing the need for precise and sustainable feeding strategies.
10.12982/cmjs.2026.113: Intensive aquaculture systems are frequently affected by nutrient accumulation and harmful cyanobacterial blooms, creating a need for biological approaches capable of addressing both issues simultaneously. This study investigated the performance of the halotolerant yeast Saccharomyces cerevisiae NM2 for concurrent nutrient removal and the population response of Microcystis aeruginosa NA during co-cultivation in aquaculture wastewater at a salinity of 1.5%. In monoculture, S. cerevisiae NM2 achieved chemical oxygen demand (COD) removal efficiencies of 87.34-91.35% at initial COD concentrations of 100-750 mg/L within 24 h. Total nitrogen (TN) and total phosphorus (TP) removal efficiencies reached 64.12-71.21% and 96.80-97.68%, respectively, resulting in residual TP concentrations below 0.35 mg/L. In co-culture with M. aeruginosa NA, cyanobacterial abundance decreased by 86.3-97.6% over the 24-h experimental period. COD and TP removal efficiencies under co-culture conditions remained high, ranging from 91.08% to 93.94% and exceeding 97%, respectively, while TN removal efficiencies ranged from 50.41% to 70.40%. The mechanism underlying the decline in M. aeruginosa NA abundance was not resolved by the present experimental design and may involve nutrient-mediated effects, direct inhibitory activity, or other microbial interactions. These findings demonstrate effective nutrient removal by S. cerevisiae NM2 accompanied by a marked decrease in M. aeruginosa NA abundance under the tested co-culture conditions.
10.1111/raq.70232: ABSTRACT Viral disease constrains penaeid shrimp aquaculture by destabilizing production, animal welfare and aquatic food-system resilience. White spot syndrome virus (WSSV)-penaeid shrimp models provide the strongest mechanistic evidence for antiviral immunity, but they cannot serve as universal proxies for RNA viruses, decapod iridescent virus 1 (DIV1), crayfish, crabs or freshwater prawns. This review treats crustacean antiviral immunity as an evidence-weighted network rather than a catalog of immune genes, distinguishing study-level evidence for host defense from the separate maturity of proposed aquaculture applications. We integrate Toll/immune deficiency (IMD)-nuclear factor kappa B (NF-κB), stimulator of interferon genes (STING)-interferon regulatory factor (IRF)-Vago-Janus kinase/signal transducer and activator of transcription (JAK/STAT), RNA interference (RNAi), recognition-entry duality, cellular clearance, antimicrobial peptides, and prophenoloxidase (proPO)-linked defense into interacting signaling and innate immune networks. The central conclusion is that pathway biology becomes useful for practical aquaculture when it yields molecular markers and management interventions for validation against diseases and production outcomes rather than simply stronger immune activation.
10.3390/hydrobiology5040049: This study examined the contribution of drainage and collector ditches in the Syr Darya River basin to local and regional aquatic biodiversity by comparing fish and macroinvertebrate assemblages in these anthropogenic habitats with those in adjacent natural river sections. Assemblages were analyzed in relation to eight abiotic environmental variables, with particular attention to blackflies and fish. Ditches differed from adjacent river habitats in several environmental characteristics, most notably lower summer water temperatures and reduced turbidity, and supported distinct aquatic assemblages. Of the 46 animal taxa recorded, 11 were restricted to ditches, indicating that these habitats contributed a distinct component to regional biodiversity. Drainage and collector ditches also provided suitable habitats for Simuliidae larvae and supported local blackfly populations. In contrast, fish assemblages in both ditch types were dominated by non-native species, potentially reflecting environmental filtering and repeated immigration from established populations. Although ditches exhibited lower species richness than adjacent river sections, they supported several species not recorded in natural river habitats. Thus, anthropogenic ditches cannot replace natural rivers but may increase habitat heterogeneity and contribute to biodiversity conservation in highly modified landscapes. Extensive networks of irrigation canals and drainage collectors have been established throughout much of the Syr Darya River basin, substantially modifying natural freshwater habitats. This study investigated the contribution of two types of anthropogenic ditches-drainage and collector ditches-to local and regional fish and macroinvertebrate diversity by comparing their assemblages with those of adjacent natural river sections. The diversity and distribution of macroinvertebrates and fish were examined in relation to eight abiotic environmental variables, with particular attention to blackflies (Diptera: Simuliidae) and fish as ecologically and socioeconomically important components of regional aquatic ecosystems. Drainage and collector ditches differed from adjacent river habitats in several environmental characteristics, most notably lower summer water temperatures and reduced turbidity. These conditions were associated with distinct aquatic assemblages in the ditches. Of the 46 animal taxa recorded, 11 were restricted to ditches, indicating that these anthropogenic habitats supported a distinct ditch-associated component of the regional fauna. Drainage and collector ditches also provided suitable habitats for Simuliidae larvae and supported local blackfly populations. In contrast, fish assemblages in both types of ditches were dominated by non-native species. The occurrence and distribution of non-native fishes may reflect a combination of environmental filtering and repeated immigration from established populations, although the relative contribution of these mechanisms remains to be determined. Overall, the ditches exhibited lower species richness than adjacent river sections but contributed to regional biodiversity by supporting several species that were not recorded in natural river habitats. Thus, although anthropogenic ditches cannot be considered substitutes for natural river ecosystems, they increase habitat heterogeneity and provide additional aquatic habitats within highly modified landscapes. Their ecological significance should therefore be assessed not only in terms of species richness but also with regard to the composition, origin, ecological roles, and conservation status of the species they support.
10.70963/jm.v3i2.1073: Downstream processing activities are a strategic sector that increases the added value of fishery products and supports regional economic growth. One product with development potential is crispy nilem baby fish, which represents a strategic effort to increase the economic value of bycatch and address the fish’s tendency to spoil easily. This activity is carried out, among other places, by the Baby Fish Mr.O MSME in Rancapaku Village, Tasikmalaya Regency. This study assessed the value added generated from processing of crispy nilem baby fish in MSMEs Baby Fish Mr.O in one production. The type of research used in this study is quantitative data with a case study approach. The data collection technique is through interviews with tools in the form of questionnaires and observations. Data is obtained from primary and secondary data. The sample extraction technique is carried out by the purposive sampling method. The data analysis in this study uses the Hayami method. The results of the study show that based on the analysis of the Hayami method, the added value of processing crispy nilem baby fish in Baby Fish Mr.O MSMEs is IDR 234,798 per kilogram of raw materials with an added value ratio of 78.27%. The added value of this product is in the high category
10.1007/s10641-026-01935-4: Abstract Elasmobranchs are key components of marine trophic webs, functioning as top and mesopredators, but they are under considerable pressure from fishing activities and environmental degradation. Although the region was among the first Brazilian areas to be settled, the sharks and rays off the southern coast of Rio de Janeiro remain poorly known. This study aimed to assess the diversity of demersal elasmobranchs in a potentially relevant region of southeastern Brazil and to investigate the reproductive aspects of the most abundant species. Fourteen campaigns were carried out along the ocean side of Grande Island and the mouth of the Ilha Grande Bay using trawls and bottom longlines, between January 2006 and August 2007. The observed diversity was supplemented by a comprehensive literature review and recent records from citizen science databases. Twenty-one species were identified, with the most abundant comprising Atlantoraja cyclophora , Psammobatis extenta , Psammobatis rutrum , Rioraja agassizii , and Rhizoprionodon lalandii , with a substantial presence of juveniles. The L 50 values for A. cyclophora were 38 cm for females and 37.2 cm for males, 29.2 cm for females and 25.4 cm for males for R. agassizii , and 59.5 cm for male R. lalandii specimens. Results suggested a year-round reproductive activity for Arhynchobatidae, as females with eggs in the uterus or displaying vitellogenic activity were captured throughout the entire study period. The study highlights the need for conservation efforts in the region’s inner coastal shelf waters, given their potentially significant ecological role for elasmobranchs.
10.1080/02724634.2026.2744129: A single fossil referable to the putative ephippid (batfish) †Eoplatax sp. is reported from the Eocene (Lutetian) Habib Rahi Formation of northwest Pakistan, where it is associated with a modest undescribed marine teleostean fauna. The specimen is incompletely preserved and lacks many of the cranial features used to diagnose †Eoplatax, but postcranial characters described here support its attribution to the genus. Additional traits distinguishing †Eoplatax from Platax are reviewed. Extinct taxa traditionally aligned with ephippids have never been formally investigated alongside extant species. We provide a critical review of the putative ephippids represented by skeletal fossils in order to facilitate future work. Apart from the new specimen of †Eoplatax reported here, all of these examples come from the Paleogene record of Europe. This †Eoplatax from eastern Tethys represents the first record of the genus outside the celebrated Bolca assemblage of the western Tethyan region, and hints that other nearshore teleostean lineages may have had wide geographic ranges at this time. Investigation of fossils from deposits outside of Europe and central Asia, even incomplete material like the specimen of †Eoplatax presented here, is essential for constraining biogeographic hypotheses of marine fish biogeography in the Cenozoic.
10.1139/cjfas-2026-0046: Understanding how ecologically similar species coexist is central to ecology, particularly in environments where interspecific competition is high. We investigated niche partitioning between two sympatric batoid species, white skate (Rostroraja alba) and thornback ray (Raja clavata), in a coastal marine protected area (the Professor Luiz Saldanha Marine Park, Portugal) using a combination of acoustic telemetry and DNA metabarcoding. The acoustic telemetry results revealed substantial spatial and behavioural overlap between species, including similar diel patterns and habitat preferences, with no evidence of fine-scale spatial segregation. In contrast, metabarcoding analyses of cloacal swabs indicated significant dietary differentiation. Rostroraja alba exhibited a higher diversity and number of exclusive prey taxa compared to R. clavata, suggesting broader or more opportunistic feeding strategies. These findings indicate that trophic niche partitioning, rather than spatial or temporal segregation, supports the coexistence of these ecologically similar skates. This study highlights the value of integrating spatial ecology with molecular diet analysis to better understand mechanisms of niche differentiation and species coexistence in marine predators.
10.1139/cjfas-2025-0404: As salmonid marine survival declines and the causes of marine mortality remain uncertain, supplementation programs are increasingly adopting strategies that bypass this life stage. Smolt-to-adult supplementation (SAS) programs collect migrating smolts, rear them to maturity in captivity, and release them to spawn in the wild. Despite ongoing debate regarding the risks and benefits of SAS and other stocking approaches, empirical evaluations remain limited. We evaluated an Atlantic Salmon SAS program operating concurrently with a captive-bred juvenile release program on the Tobique River, New Brunswick, Canada. Three cohorts of potential spawners and five years of returning adults were sampled. Parentage analysis was used to determine spawning success, reproductive success, and mating patterns. SAS fish spawned successfully in the river and mated with other SAS adults, sea-run salmon, and unsampled spawners, likely precocial male parr. However, SAS adults exhibited lower reproductive success than both sea-run and broodstock-origin spawners, while broodstock-origin fish had the highest lifetime reproductive success. Consequently, SAS adults contributed fewer returning adult recruits and had a reduced demographic impact on the population.
10.1111/raq.70233: ABSTRACT Dissolved oxygen (DO) affects respiration, feeding, growth and welfare in aquaculture. DO forecasting can provide early warning of hypoxia and inform aeration decisions. Most aquaculture forecasts use time series from fixed monitoring locations; these describe temporal variation but contain limited information on biological oxygen demand, management activity and spatial distribution. This review traces the transition from single-point time-series prediction to multimodal DO forecasting. Environmental and operational variables capture external forcing and interventions associated with DO dynamics. Biological, behavioural and physiological observations provide information on oxygen demand and animal responses, whereas spatial and hydroacoustic observations characterise fish distribution and biomass across locations and depths. The review covers spatiotemporal alignment, missing-value reconstruction, multimodal fusion, and temporal, spatiotemporal, multimodal and hybrid forecasting models. Applications include hypoxia warning, DO-field forecasting and reconstruction, and forecast-informed oxygen management. Across the literature, DO and physicochemical measurements form the observational basis and are supplemented by biological, spatial and operational information selected for each forecasting task. Asynchronous observations, missing data and variable sensor reliability complicate multimodal fusion, while differing forecast horizons and evaluation settings affect comparisons across studies. Field deployment is further affected by sensor drift, biofouling and differences among production sites. Priorities for future research include quality-aware and mechanism-data fusion, transferable models evaluated under comparable horizons and event definitions, and prospective studies linking prediction error to warning lead time, spatial risk and management outcomes. In brief, this review aims to help researchers and practitioners understand multimodal DO forecasting and its potential to guide oxygen management in aquaculture.
10.3390/fishes11120687: This study investigated the growth performance, gut microbiota, and intestinal histology of juvenile Nile tilapia (Oreochromis niloticus) fed a functional additive blend containing sodium butyrate, dehydrated hydrolyzed yeast, zinc proteinate, and a fermentation product of Lactobacillus acidophilus. Three doses (0.30, 0.60, and 2.40 g kg-1) were added to a basal diet, and treatments were randomly assigned to 24 experimental units, with six replicates per treatment. Fish were fed a restricted ration twice daily for 55 days. Dietary supplementation significantly improved the feed conversion ratio and protein retention and reduced voluntary feed intake and nitrogen loss. Fish supplemented with 0.30 and 0.60 g kg-1 had a greater intestinal absorptive area. At 0.60 g kg-1, muscular layer thickness increased compared with the control. Diet significantly affected intestinal microbial community structure, with more pronounced taxonomic changes at 2.40 g kg-1. Spearman correlations showed that higher daily weight gain was associated with lower feed conversion ratio (r = -0.845), while greater intestinal absorptive area was associated with lower voluntary feed intake (r = -0.526). Overall, the most consistent results were at 0.30 and 0.60 g kg-1, indicating that these inclusion levels improved nutrient utilization and gut health parameters in juvenile Nile tilapia.
10.1007/s10750-026-06485-5: Among Neotropical cichlids the tribe Heroini exhibits substantial ecological diversity and is one of the dominant fish groups across northern Neotropical riverscapes. The majority of studies on heroine cichlids have focused on macroevolutionary patterns but the role of geological and climatic factors shaping lineage diversification within the tribe remains poorly understood. Here we used ultraconserved elements (UCEs) to infer a taxonomically complete and geographically comprehensive phylogenomic framework of the early-diverging herichthyine sister genera Thorichthys and Trichromis and to comparatively investigate their evolutionary and biogeographic histories. All our phylogenomic hypotheses support the monophyly of both genera and two species subgroups within Thorichthys . Our results provide evidence of (a) unrecognized diversity within Trichromis salvini , (b) uncertainty in species boundaries in Thorichthys , and (c) the first report of ghost introgression in fishes of the northern Neotropics. Additionally, our results demonstrate the importance of the Papaloapan and Coatzacoalcos watersheds for fish diversification in the region. Finally, we show patterns consistent with ecological divergence during the evolution of this group, particularly among sympatric non-closely related species. Altogether, these patterns suggest that lineage diversification in northern Neotropical cichlids has been driven by the interaction of geological restructuring, climatic and sea-level oscillations, and heterogeneous ecological pressures.
10.1111/jfb.70725: Abstract We established hypoxia avoidance thresholds of three-spined stickleback ( Gasterosteus aculeatus ) using a customized choice-flume system. Stickleback is an opportunistic species, increasing in abundance in several aquatic systems. We show that sticklebacks avoid oxygen levels commonly reported in many coastal areas. When prey was available in severe hypoxia (10% O 2 sat), fish still spent 50.9% of the 30-min feeding period in the hypoxic side, compared with 78.5% in the prey side under normoxia. These findings provide a prey-dependent estimate of hypoxia sensitivity in an abundant northern-temperate coastal fish and highlight the need to test whether laboratory thresholds predict field distributions.
10.1111/jfb.70746: Abstract Stock assessments for Albacore ( Thunnus alalunga ) in the North Pacific Ocean use an integrated, sex-specific model based on the hypothesis that growth and longevity are sexually dimorphic. However, the paucity of sex-specific data available to model somatic growth and understand spatial population structure was a continual source of uncertainty among past studies. We engaged in a geographically expansive sampling effort to obtain recent age, length and sex data from fisheries sources across its North Pacific range and provide an updated growth model and regional estimates of sex ratios more representative of the entire stock of North Pacific albacore. With a more complete sample distribution by sex, a combined sexes model was favoured over a sex-specific model based on both Akaike Information Criterion (AICc) and Bayesian Information Criterion (BIC). The von Bertalanffy growth parameters for combined sexes were L ∞ = 124.4 cm in fork length ( L F ), K = 0.168 years -1 and t 0 = -2.100 years. Regional (west, central and east Pacific Ocean), fishery-dependent, sample sex ratios ranged from 1.2 to 1.6 males per female for size classes up to 90 cm L F . Individuals 100 cm L F and larger were predominantly males, but large females were collected for all size classes, and males were larger than females in only one age class. In contrast with previous growth studies, our results support the use of a single model to describe growth and longevity of both male and female North Pacific albacore. The convergence of sex-specific growth curves associated with a more complete sample distribution combined with studies from other albacore populations suggests that male-skewed sex ratios among adult North Pacific albacore are likely due to sex-specific migration patterns, habitat preferences, or behaviours that impact their vulnerability to capture.
10.1111/jfb.70748: Abstract Eelgrass ( Zostera marina ) beds form essential ecosystems that provide significant ecosystem services through carbon fixation and as nurseries for aquatic living resources. The period during which vegetation is in decline or has disappeared in annual eelgrass beds is longer than in perennial eelgrass beds. There have been no comparative studies of fish production in eelgrass beds with the different life cycles, although quantitative evaluation of fish production within habitats is an essential process for assessing the contribution of each habitat to fisheries resources. We conducted field surveys at two eelgrass beds (annual eelgrass in 2023-2024 and perennial eelgrass in 2008-2009) in temperate coastal waters of the western North Pacific to evaluate how the difference in eelgrass life cycle affects seasonal change and annual amount of fish production. Fish production was estimated by monthly seines that enabled species-specific estimates of biomass increase. The results showed that monthly fish production in the perennial eelgrass bed remained at higher levels for a longer period than in the annual eelgrass bed, and annual fish production in the perennial eelgrass bed was approximately twice that in the annual eelgrass bed. Because the increase in sea water temperature and changes in other environmental conditions under global warming are expected to shift eelgrass towards an annual life cycle, this could affect ecosystem services of eelgrass bed through changes in fish community structure and production.
10.1111/eff.70054: ABSTRACT Stream flows are widely regarded as a master variable affecting fish assemblages, with extreme events (e.g., floods, droughts) reorganising assemblages. Although assemblage turnover (temporal beta diversity) is common following hydrologic extremes, we have limited knowledge on how hydrologic extremes influence assemblage turnover across a broad spatial extent. In this study, we analysed time-series counts of stream fish assemblages at 34 sites in the conterminous US to characterise the relationship between assemblage turnover with high- and low-flow anomalies. We found that flow anomalies were equally important in explaining fish assemblage turnover when analysed across study sites. One-year lag effects of flow extremes were equally important to current-year effects. Temporal changes in relative abundance were a stronger factor of fish assemblage turnover than assemblage composition (i.e., species loss and gain). Species with the greatest contributions to assemblage turnover tended to be fluvial species that were locally abundant. Our study showed that neither high nor low flows influence stream fish assemblage turnover consistently across sites, suggesting context dependence. Further research with additional sites across ecoregions could identify factors determining this context dependency, which will help stream fish management under climate-change-induced hydrologic uncertainty and increasing human demand for water.
10.1111/fme.70134: ABSTRACT Freshwater ecosystems in the Eastern Himalayan Region of India-a global biodiversity hotspot-are threatened by invasive alien fish species perhaps facilitated by exotic aquaculture, the aquarium trade, climate change, and inadequate regulation. The invasion of alien species disrupts native biodiversity, causes ecological imbalances, and threatens livelihoods dependent on freshwater resources. To address this, the present study develops an integrated management framework by synthesizing and adapting global biosecurity protocols, policy tools, and community-led conservation. The framework integrates three pillars: (1) advanced biosecurity, with real-time monitoring and predictive modeling for early detection; (2) strengthened, context-sensitive policies to regulate high-risk species trade and aquaculture while respecting local economies; and (3) community empowerment through stewardship programs using traditional knowledge, sustainable livelihoods, and awareness. Recognizing the region's unique geological history and the convergence of two biodiversity hotspots in Northeast India, the framework's strength lies in its tailored design, which explicitly leverages local communities and their traditional practices to provide culturally grounded, sustainable solutions. By fostering regional collaboration, using technology, and engaging communities, this approach aims to disrupt invasion pathways, protect biodiversity, and enhance ecosystem resilience, thereby contributing to global conservation goals.
10.1002/jaa2.70061: ABSTRACT A four-component stochastic frontier model is applied separately to nine broadly classified species group panels of U.S. aquaculture farms covering the years 2007 to 2017 to identify both time-varying and persistent inefficiencies for catfish, trout, “other” food fish, bait fish, ornamental fish, sport fish, crustaceans, mollusks, and “other” aquaculture products. We find considerable efficiency gaps in aquaculture production driven primarily by growers' persistent inefficiencies; average overall technical efficiency ranges from 43.8% to 53.7% for “other” aquaculture products and trout, respectively. This finding suggests that increased extension efforts promoting best planning practices for potential entrants can significantly improve U.S. aquaculture efficiency.
10.1111/fog.70095: ABSTRACT Phytoplankton primary production is essential to coastal food webs. However, the roles of different nutrient sources in semienclosed bays characterized by strong seasonal variability in physical conditions and nutrient availability are not well understood. We investigated seasonal variations in phytoplankton biomass and primary productivity over 2 years (June 2021-November 2023) at a shellfish aquaculture site in Miyazu Bay, Japan, where nutrients are supplied via offshore seawater intrusion and river discharge as well as submarine groundwater discharge (SGD). Vertically integrated chlorophyll a (Chl-a) and electron transport rate-based primary production were highest in winter, coinciding with elevated dissolved inorganic nutrient concentrations associated with offshore water inputs. However, Chl-a-specific productivity and photosynthetic activity declined in winter due to reduced solar radiation, indicating that phytoplankton biomass accumulated under nutrient-rich conditions despite light limitation. Photosynthetically active radiation (PAR) within the water column was governed primarily by surface PAR rather than by the light attenuation coefficient, which was low and showed no seasonality. In contrast, Chl-a-specific productivity and photosynthetic activity peaked in summer, when surface nutrient concentrations were low but solar radiation was high. Geochemical tracers ( 222 Rn and 224 Ra) revealed continuous inputs of nutrient-rich groundwater near the seabed, suggesting that SGD may supplement nutrient availability during nutrient-depleted summer conditions. Size-fractionated analyses revealed that small phytoplankton (< 20 μm) dominated biomass and production throughout the year. These results also highlight SGD as a relatively persistent nutrient pathway that may supplement nutrient availability under light-rich but nutrient-poor summer conditions.
10.12688/f1000research.194150.1: Abstract* Fishery products are prone to quality deterioration during post-harvest handling and distribution. Therefore, the development of a sustainable cold chain requires the integration of facility planning, distribution efficiency, coastal zone management, and socio-ecological considerations. This study aims to synthesize these approaches and identify gaps in their integration. A systematic review was conducted through a literature search in the Scopus database, with reporting guided by PRISMA 2020. The initial search yielded 396 records; 222 records were retained after applying the publication year restriction of 2016-2026. Screening for document type, language, and access resulted in 134 records for title and abstract evaluation. A total of 37 publications proceeded to the eligibility assessment stage, and 12 publications were reported in a qualitative-thematic synthesis based on four research questions. The synthesis identified four main themes: location-allocation optimization and low-emission distribution; coastal spatial-ecological planning; facility accessibility and socioeconomic resilience; and carbon traceability and accountability. The results show that technical, ecological, and social approaches make complementary contributions, but their integration into a single fisheries cold chain planning model has not been comprehensively demonstrated in the reviewed literature. This study proposes a Coastal Cold Chain Integration Triad Framework that links spatial-ecological suitability, facility location-allocation optimization, and socio-ecological resilience and supply chain integrity. This framework provides a conceptual basis for research and planning in sustainable fisheries logistics, with a need for further empirical testing.
10.31961/eltikom.v10i2.2125: Current government aid programs in the fisheries sector often rely on reactive and uniform approaches, which may result in inefficient resource allocation. This study proposes an integrated dual-model machine learning framework to support more targeted fisheries aid allocation. The framework addresses two policy needs: predicting future vulnerability risk among capture fishers and estimating the success potential of aquaculture farmers. Data were obtained from the Integrated Fishery Reporting Application, comprising 625 aquaculture farmer records and 437 fisher records across 28 sub-districts in Lebak Regency, Banten, Indonesia. A Random Forest classifier was employed to classify fisher vulnerability into three categories: Low, Mid, and High Risk, while a Gradient Boosting Machine (GBM) regression model was used to predict survival rate as a proxy for farmer success potential. The optimized Random Forest model achieved a weighted F1-score of 0.8862, with recall values of 0.9268 for Mid Risk and 0.8889 for High Risk. The GBM model achieved an R-squared (R²) of 0.7585 and an RMSE of 6.0033 on the test data. These results indicate the potential of the framework to provide quantitative support for risk identification and aid prioritization. However, the findings are limited to data from a single regency and have not been evaluated through direct field implementation or policy intervention. Therefore, the framework should be considered an empirically evaluated decision-support approach rather than a fully validated policy tool.
10.3390/ani16233721: The Mekong Delta of Vietnam is one of Southeast Asia’s most important food-producing regions, supporting intensive rice cultivation, globally significant aquaculture, and diverse inland and rice-field fisheries that contribute to food security, rural livelihoods, and ecosystem functioning. However, hydraulic engineering, agricultural intensification, aquaculture expansion, urbanization, upstream river development, and climate-related pressures have progressively altered the hydrological and ecological processes sustaining these interconnected systems. This review synthesizes evidence on the transformation of rice-field fisheries and aquatic animal production in the Lower Mekong Basin, with particular emphasis on the Mekong Delta, and evaluates how effectively pollution governance addresses cumulative pressures on aquatic ecosystems. Peer-reviewed studies, official statistics, policy and legal documents, Mekong River Commission reports, and international institutional publications were assessed through a systematic critical review combining evidence mapping with structured narrative synthesis. The synthesis reveals a marked transition from hydrologically connected, multispecies production landscapes toward increasingly specialized rice and aquaculture systems. In the Mekong Delta region, recorded inland wild-fish catch declined from approximately 165,000 tonnes in 1995 to 30,000 tonnes in 2024, while aquaculture production increased more than eightfold, from approximately 78,000 to 650,000 tonnes, and rice production more than doubled, from 3.5 to 7.6 million tonnes. These contrasting trends coincided with high-dyke development, reduced floodplain connectivity, altered sediment and flow regimes, habitat modification, and greater agrochemical dependence. Major pollution pressures include nutrient and organic enrichment, pesticides, pharmaceuticals, domestic and industrial wastewater, micro-plastics, and acid-sulfate-soil drainage. Nevertheless, fishery decline cannot be attributed to pollution alone, because hydropower development, migration barriers, fishing pressure, habitat fragmentation, altered flood pulses, sediment deficits, and interact across spatial and temporal scales. Although Vietnam has established increasingly comprehensive fisheries, environment, water-resource, regional-planning, and climate-adaptation frameworks, implementation remains fragmented. Priority actions include integrated basin-to-field monitoring, cumulative-risk assessment, pollution prevention at source, stronger discharge controls, restoration of seasonal floodplain connectivity, protection of aquatic refuges, community co-management, and wider adoption of context-appropriate floating-rice, rice-fish, and rice-shrimp systems in this Delta region.
10.1111/jfb.70743: Abstract Traditional fisheries stock assessments incorporate life history data (e.g., mortality, growth, maturity), indices of abundance, and catch data into models to determine stock status and estimate biological reference points. However, obtaining these data in an accurate and timely manner can be challenging. While genetic techniques have been used for over 50 years to identify independent stocks, recent genomic innovations now allow for the generation of multiple stock assessment data inputs. Specifically, DNA extracted from non-lethally sampled tissue (e.g., fin clips) can be analyzed to monitor population structure and levels of connectivity, to estimate absolute abundance, to assess the age composition of landed or discarded catch, and to estimate sex ratios. Through standardized, adaptable, and minimally invasive methods to collect data necessary for robust stock assessments, genomic tools have the potential to provide a relatively comprehensive and cost-effective approach for long-term monitoring. The enhanced integration of next-generation genomic data into stock assessments will improve the accuracy and efficiency of fisheries assessment and management, ultimately supporting the sustainable use of marine resources.
10.1007/s12601-026-00319-0: Trawl size selectivity constitutes a critical link between fisheries science, fishing technology, and fisheries governance. This study comparatively examines the development of scientific knowledge on trawl size selectivity and the evolution of corresponding fisheries regulations in Türkiye, with particular attention to the degree of correspondence between these two trajectories. A four-stage methodological framework was applied. First, the global literature on trawl selectivity was examined through a bibliometric analysis of 1940 publications indexed in the Web of Science Core Collection between 1980 and 2026. Network analyses including keyword co-occurrence, co-authorship, citation analysis, and bibliographic coupling were conducted using VOSviewer software to identify the structural characteristics of the field. Second, publication trends were evaluated using forecasting approaches, including ARIMA, ETS, Holt-Winters, Theta, Naive, and Polynomial Regression models. Third, a systematic screening was conducted using the Turkish Council of Higher Education National Thesis Center, where 29 postgraduate theses addressing trawl size selectivity were identified. Fourth, fisheries communiqués were analyzed to examine the evolution of trawl selectivity regulations in Türkiye. The results indicate that Türkiye possesses substantial scientific research capacity on trawl size selectivity, reflected in international scientific publications and in postgraduate research. Forecasting analyses further suggest that scientific production on trawl selectivity will continue to increase through 2030, indicating sustained international interest in selective fishing technologies and bycatch reduction measures. However, codend mesh-size regulations in Turkish bottom trawl fisheries have remained largely unchanged since 2007. These findings indicate a persistent mismatch between the expanding scientific knowledge base on trawl selectivity and the limited evolution of corresponding regulatory provisions in Türkiye. The study highlights the importance of strengthening science-policy interactions and promoting evidence-based fisheries governance to improve the adaptive management of trawl fisheries.
10.32815/jpm.v7i2.3170: Purpose: This community engagement activity aimed to introduce Smart Costing based on Activity-Based Costing (ABC) to the Fish-Processing MSME Group in Domas Village, Pontang District, Serang Regency, and to improve participants’ understanding of financial recordkeeping and production cost calculation. Method: The activity took place on 22 October 2026 and included educational sessions and practical exercises on calculating production costs. Evaluation was qualitative, based on the implementation information provided by the community engagement team. Numerical pre-test and post-test scores and the exact number of individual participants were not available. Practical Applications: The activity introduced participants to more structured production-cost calculation. Follow-up collaboration is planned to support more orderly financial records, consistent production-cost calculations, and business development. Conclusion: The activity was reported to have run smoothly, with a reported change in participants’ understanding before and after the education. Since detailed evaluation records were unavailable, the magnitude of the change cannot be quantified. Continued mentoring is proposed to support application of the learning in daily business practices.
10.1007/s12562-026-02044-y: Social isolation can induce stress responses in group-living animals, with consequences for growth, behavior, and health. In social fish species, whether and how these effects are modulated by food availability, and whether they can be reversed by subsequent return to group rearing, remain poorly understood. Using mirror carp (Cyprinus carpio var. specularis) as a model, we investigated the interactive effects of social conditions (isolation-rearing vs group-rearing, including a transition from isolation to group-rearing) and food availability (low: one satiation meal every 2 days; high: two satiation meals per day) on growth, behavioral traits, stress (cortisol), immunity (immunoglobulin M, lysozyme), and oxidative stress (superoxide dismutase) over a 6-week experiment comprising two 3-week phases. High food availability consistently promoted greater growth, while the effect of social conditions on growth depended on food availability and developmental stage. Among behavioral traits, activity was influenced by social conditions, boldness by food availability, and sociability remained stable. Physiologically, social isolation was associated with elevated serum cortisol levels irrespective of food availability, reflecting enhanced acute stress responsiveness, and the elevated cortisol response observed in isolated fish was not evident after return to group rearing. Immune parameters (IgM and lysozyme) were suppressed by social isolation, while food availability enhanced IgM and SOD activity; however, post-hoc comparisons did not provide direct statistical support for recovery of IgM or lysozyme after return to group rearing, and the reversibility of these effects therefore remains uncertain. By simultaneously assessing growth, behavior, and multiple physiological systems, this study provides novel insights into the adaptive capacity of social fish species facing changes in both social environment and resource abundance.
10.3390/microplastics5040238: Contaminants in commercially important fish provide relevant information on environmental exposure in coastal urban systems. This study investigated materials detected in the gastrointestinal tracts of croaker (Micropogonias furnieri) and horse mackerel (Trachurus trachurus) marketed in Santos, Brazil, and Maputo, Mozambique, integrating microscopy combined with Raman spectroscopy (µ-Raman), frequency analysis, and correspondence analysis with market categories and market-associated socioeconomic profiles. µ-Raman analysis included 68 spectral acquisitions, yielding 124 component assignments, including carbonaceous materials, synthetic polymers, cellulosic materials, pigments, dyes, and other chemical signatures. Carbon and graphite were the most frequent components, while polyethylene terephthalate (PET) and polyester-related materials predominated among synthetic polymers. Both study areas showed comparable spectral-occurrence patterns, particularly for PET, graphite, and cellulosic materials. Global chi-square tests showed no statistically significant dependence between material occurrence and either market categories or socioeconomic profiles. However, adjusted standardized residuals and correspondence analysis revealed localized distributional patterns involving specific materials and market categories, which should be interpreted as exploratory rather than causal relationships. Integrating µ-Raman spectroscopy and multivariate analysis provides a useful framework for characterizing chemically diverse materials associated with gastrointestinal exposure in commercially important fish. Nevertheless, their occurrence in gastrointestinal tissues provides evidence of environmental exposure and may be relevant to ecological risk, which requires dedicated toxicological assessment. Because we analyzed only gastrointestinal tissues, the findings do not demonstrate contamination of edible muscle tissues, human dietary exposure, or health risk.
10.1186/s44365-026-00051-9: Aquaculture and inland capture fisheries both contribute substantially to food security, yet market acceptance is frequently constrained by consumer perceptions favoring wild-caught fish. This study evaluated the comparative proximate composition, sensory profiles, and consumer preferences for three commercially important Indian Major Carps ( Labeo rohita , Catla catla , and Cirrhinus mrigala ) sourced from wild-capture and pond-aquaculture systems to provide empirical evidence for product quality management. Thirty adult carps ( N = 30; n = 5 biological replicates per species per source) were analyzed for proximate composition (crude protein, crude fat, ash, and moisture) using standard analytical protocols and evaluated via two-way factorial ANOVA. Sensory attributes (color, flavor, juiciness, tenderness, oiliness, and overall acceptability) were assessed by 15 trained assessors (8 M:7 F) using a double-blind, randomized 9-point Hedonic scale and analyzed via non-parametric tests (Kruskal-Wallis H and Mann-Whitney U). A cross-sectional survey of 200 respondents (100 common consumers and 100 fishers) evaluated market preferences using Pearson’s Chi-Square (χ²) tests of independence. Two-way ANOVA revealed significant main effects of production source and species, along with a significant interaction for crude protein ( p = 0.001) and crude fat ( p < 0.001). Farmed carps exhibited pronounced lipid accumulation compared to wild fish, whereas wild carps deposited significantly higher protein and ash. Non-parametric sensory evaluation showed that wild-caught fish achieved significantly higher mean ranks across all attributes ( p < 0.05), with wild L. rohita scoring highest in flavor (8.46 ± 0.64) and overall acceptability (8.20 ± 0.95). Survey analysis indicated a predominant consumer preference for wild fish (61%) and identified L. rohita as the most preferred table species across both cohorts (χ² = 11.449, p = 0.010). Fishers reported significantly higher taste discrimination capacity than consumers (χ² = 6.490, p = 0.011). Wild-caught carps exhibited superior sensory palatability and leaner muscle profiles than farmed counterparts. These findings indicate that commercial aquaculture must optimize dietary formulations, minimize excessive lipid deposition, and manage pond water quality to bridge the sensory quality gap and enhance consumer acceptance of cultured carps.
10.56557/upjoz/2026/v47i225956: Aquaculture is central to aquatic-food supply, yet expansion can intensify pressures associated with feed ingredients, energy consumption, nutrient discharge, disease, biodiversity and unequal access to technology. Contemporary innovation encompasses recirculating aquaculture systems, biofloc and integrated multi-trophic production, precision sensing and artificial intelligence, alternative feeds, molecular health tools, and environmentally informed siting. Their sustainability implications cannot be established from technological novelty or production efficiency alone. This critical narrative review evaluates these approaches across biological performance, resource accounting, commercial feasibility, welfare, environmental effects and governance. Peer-reviewed literature and authoritative institutional evidence published principally from 2015 to 12 September 2026 were examined, alongside influential earlier work. The synthesis finds comparatively strong mechanistic evidence for controlled water treatment, nutrient transformation, selective breeding and established vaccination programmes, but greater uncertainty about their net benefits across complete production chains. Recirculation can reduce water withdrawals and permit effluent capture while increasing dependence on reliable electricity and treatment infrastructure. Biofloc and extractive co-culture can retain or recover nutrients, although their effects depend on suspended solids, microbial stability, species compatibility, harvesting and system boundaries. Digital methods improve observation and predictive capability, yet farm-scale prospective validation, transferability and independent cost-benefit assessments remain limited. Novel feed ingredients may ease pressure on forage fish without necessarily reducing land use, processing energy or nutrient competition. Evidence on seaweed-based carbon benefits and broad ecosystem services is particularly context dependent. The review proposes a decision framework in which technologies are compared against a realistic baseline using life-cycle impacts, nutrient budgets, health and welfare outcomes, economic resilience and distributive effects. Priority research involves multi-cycle commercial comparisons, interoperable monitoring, causal field evaluation and integrated environmental-economic appraisal. Sustainable aquaculture is therefore best advanced through context-specific combinations of technologies, rather than a universal ranking of ‘smart’ solutions.
10.32815/jpm.v7i2.3098: Purpose: Rural Village-Owned Enterprises (BUMDes) operating aquaculture units often face severe financial vulnerabilities and loss of Village Native Income (PADes) due to recurring night-time fish poaching and asset theft. This study evaluates and optimizes the existing CCTV infrastructure at BUMDes Marga Jaya, East Lampung, through a participatory community empowerment framework. Method: Executed under a 40-day Thematic Community Service (KKN-T) program by ITS NU Lampung, this project combined descriptive qualitative case study methods with a 4-stage community engagement strategy involving socialization, participatory technical auditing, hands-on training for four primary BUMDes operators/guards, and SOP formalization. Practical Applications: The program successfully upgraded network configurations, eliminated blind spots, conducted mobile app training, established bi-weekly maintenance SOPs, and integrated off-grid UPS/solar planning approved through village development deliberations. Conclusion: Combining optimized real-time CCTV technology with intensive community capacity building achieved zero theft incidents, enhanced internal labor discipline, and established a scalable model demonstrating how higher education partnerships bridge the digital divide for rural enterprise sustainability.
10.59496/20261ah5: The increasing demand for sustainable aquaculture has accelerated the search for probiotic microorganisms capable of improving fish health and reducing dependence on antibiotics. This study aimed to isolate, identify, and characterize potential probiotic bacteria from an integrated aquaponic system used for Nile tilapia (Oreochromis niloticus) production. Bacterial isolates obtained from aquaponic water samples were identified using matrix-assisted laser desorption/ionization time-of-flight mass spectrometry (MALDI-TOF MS), and their probiotic potential was evaluated through assessment of antagonistic activity against fish pathogens, hemolytic activity, antibiotic susceptibility, biofilm formation, pH tolerance, bile salt tolerance, and extracellular enzyme production. Four bacterial species, namely Bacillus mycoides, Bacillus marisflavi, Bacillus thuringiensis, and Lactococcus lactis, were identified. Among these isolates, B. thuringiensis exhibited the most promising probiotic characteristics, showing strong antibacterial activity against Lactococcus garvieae with an inhibition zone of 2.32 ± 0.012 cm, while no inhibitory effect was observed against Aeromonas hydrophila or Aeromonas caviae. The isolate displayed γ-hemolytic (non-hemolytic) activity was susceptible to all tested antibiotics except intermediate susceptibility to kanamycin and showed no biofilm formation. In addition, B. thuringiensis demonstrated optimal growth at pH 5.0 (P
10.1021/acs.est.6c09109: Abstract Marine plastic pollution is an increasing environmental concern, yet aquaculture’s contribution remains poorly quantified despite its rapid expansion and reliance on plastic infrastructure. Limited data on plastic stocks, flows, losses, and end-of-life (EOL) management constrain effective mitigation and circularity strategies. This study presents a system-wide assessment of plastic use and management in Norway’s sea-based Atlantic salmon aquaculture industry. A static Material Flow Analysis (MFA), informed by data from equipment manufacturers, suppliers, operators, and waste-management stakeholders, quantifies plastic stocks and flows across equipment deployment, use, repair, replacement, environmental losses, and end-of-life treatment. The results indicate annual marine plastic losses of approximately 2737 t, corresponding to 1.2-1.7 kg per tonne of salmon produced. Feed pipes, walkway components, and consumable ropes dominate leakage. Approximately 37,400 t of end-of-life plastics are collected annually, with 42% directed to incineration with energy recovery, 22% landfilled, and limited recovery through recycling. These findings highlight substantial opportunities to strengthen collection, recycling, and resource recovery. This first comprehensive national-scale assessment establishes a quantitative baseline for monitoring and policy development. It demonstrates MFA’s utility for identifying leakage hotspots and supporting Extended Producer Responsibility (EPR) and circular economy strategies to reduce plastic pollution from aquaculture.
10.3390/agronomy16232356: Aquaculture ponds are an important anthropogenic source of CH4, and rice-fish co-culture has been proposed as a mitigation strategy; but the performance of different rice varieties in mitigating the CH4 emission from the ponds and the morphological traits of low-emission varieties remain unclear. A two-year (2024-2025) field experiment was conducted with three replicate ponds per treatment, each pond containing one plot of each variety; the plot served as the experimental unit. The six rice varieties were then compared for their effect on CH4 emission from aquaculture ponds. The results showed that co-culturing with different rice varieties significantly reduced CH4 emissions by 24.2-43.9% and 25.1-41.8% respectively in 2024 and 2025, compared with fish monoculture. Co-culturing with different rice varieties showed varying effects on CH4 emissions, and the rice variety ZGY1578 (Zhegengyou 1578) consistently showed the lowest CH4 emissions among the six varieties across both years. Accumulated CH4 emissions showed a negative correlation with the abundance of pmoA in the sediment and the radial oxygen loss (ROL) rate of rice roots and a positive correlation with plant-mediated CH4 emission, indicating that the variation among rice varieties was associated with methanotrophic abundance, root oxygen release and plant-mediated transport. Random forest analysis showed the highest variable importance of root number for predicting pmoA abundance, and root weight and root length were positively associated with ROL. Tiller number positively affected plant-mediated CH4 emission, whereas root number and root weight decreased it. Rice varieties with well-developed root systems showed strong rhizospheric CH4 oxidation and low plant-mediated CH4 emission, while excessive tillering promoted plant-mediated CH4 emission. High ROL, dense root systems, and moderate tillering were associated with low-emission rice varieties. These findings provide a basis for breeding low-emission rice varieties to reduce CH4 emission from aquaculture ponds by constructing rice-fish co-culture systems.
10.1093/mmy/myag132: Abstract Sporothrix brasiliensis is an emerging zoonotic fungal pathogen that has transformed sporotrichosis in Brazil from a sapronotic ‘gardener’s disease’ into a major zoonotic epidemic in South America. Here, ITS metabarcoding of 989 fish from coastal southern Brazil detected S. brasiliensis-compatible reads in 67.3% of pooled samples, and culture recovered viable isolates from selected samples. Genome typing placed fish-and bird-derived isolates within S. brasiliensis clinical Brazilian lineages, implicating aquatic-coastal interfaces in the ecology of this expanding pathogen.
10.1007/s11160-026-10116-6: Mesoscale fronts are ubiquitous oceanographic features that shape pelagic habitats through complex biophysical interactions, yet quantitative frontal indicators capturing front-induced biological hotspot and ecological barrier effects remain rarely incorporated into habitat models. We combined a satellite-based front-detection algorithm with a machine-learning approach to develop a “front-accounted habitat model” that integrates a suite of satellite-derived frontal indicators into conventional habitat modelling (only accounting for background environmental conditions). Using the neon flying squid, a commercially and ecologically important fishery stock in the western North Pacific, as a case study, the front-accounted habitat models increased $${\text{R}}^{2}$$ from 0.33 to 0.42-0.52 with relative increases of 27.5-58.4% and significantly reduced prediction errors by 2.3-15.3% relative to the conventional habitat models. Historical reconstructions of suitable habitat (areas with catches > 3 t) linked recent catch declines to habitat contraction and northward shifts, potentially associated with the post-2017 northward shift of intensified Western Oyashio Extension fronts that may have restricted productive subarctic water transport into the fishing grounds. During 1998-2023, the reconstructed habitat centroid shifted northward at 18.7 km decade-1, compared with 34.5 km decade-1 for the conventional model, highlighting the potential role of fronts in modulating habitat shifts under climate variability. These findings inform international squid management and offer a transferable framework for integrating frontal indicators into habitat models to improve habitat prediction and ecological interpretation.
10.3390/ani16233718: Fermented Pangasius by-products may replace conventional feed ingredients, but such substitutions alter several dietary nutrients simultaneously. We compared laying performance, egg quality, yolk cholesterol, selected fatty acids, and hematology in 150 Hisex Brown hens allocated to 30 cages (five replicate cages per diet) during a 60-day trial. Diets comprised a basal control (P0), four formulations containing 0.5-2.0% fermented Pangasius by-product extract with sugar-palm starch as partial replacement for soybean meal and fish meal (P1-P4), and a pigment-reference diet (P5). Cage-level outcomes were assessed by one-way ANOVA and Tukey comparisons. Hen-day egg production differed among diets (p = 0.0053): P3 (79.76%) and P4 (80.36%) exceeded P0 (61.91%). Feed conversion did not differ significantly (p = 0.294). Mean yolk cholesterol was 1384.1 mg/100 g dry matter in P0 and 995.6 mg/100 g in P4. The final worksheet identified EPA, DHA, linoleic acid, and oleic acid as measured; ALA and arachidonic acid were estimated and excluded from measured outcomes. Derived group omega totals and yolk n-6: n-3 ratios were withdrawn. Because the substitution changed multiple diet components, findings describe complete-diet associations, not an isolated ingredient effect or an optimal inclusion level.
10.1007/s11160-026-10115-7: Derelict gillnets have received increasing attention worldwide due to ghost fishing and marine plastic pollution. Biodegradable gillnets have been proposed as a promising technical approach to mitigate these impacts, but their fishing performance must be fully evaluated before practical application in commercial fisheries. In this study, we systematically assessed the performance of biodegradable polylactic acid (PLA) gillnets relative to conventional polyamide (PA) gillnets in a mixed-species fishery in the Yellow Sea of China, by evaluating length-dependent catch efficiency, capture mode probability, capture-mode-specific catch efficiency, catch composition, and catch value. Overall, PLA gillnets showed significantly lower catch efficiency than PA gillnets for target species, with length-integrated catch ratios of 71.83% for silver croaker (Pennahia argentata), 73.13% for flower croaker (Nibea albiflora), and 60.34% for swimming crab (Portunus trituberculatus). For the two fish species, gilling and wedging were the dominant capture modes, whereas all swimming crabs were captured by entangling. Mode-specific analysis showed that reductions in catch efficiency of PLA gillnets were smaller under gilling and wedging than under snagging and entangling, indicating the important role of capture mode in influencing fishing performance. Catch composition was broadly similar between PLA and PA gillnets; however, the gross catch value of PLA gillnets was approximately two-thirds of that of PA gillnets, mainly due to reduced catches of high-value target species, particularly swimming crab. These results demonstrated that PLA gillnets did not achieve equivalent catch performance under the tested configuration and conditions. However, broader spatiotemporal testing should be made before concluding on their catch performance.
10.1111/jfb.70724: Abstract The deep-sea catsharks in the genus Apristurus (Pentanchidae) constitute one of the most species-rich yet least resolved elasmobranch lineages. Herein, we utilised a systematic literature search to synthesise current knowledge on their diversity, morphology, phylogeny, distribution, ecology, reproduction and threats, and outline priorities for research aligned with the UN Decade of Ocean Science. The genus currently comprises 43 described extant species and three extinct taxa. Morphologically, Apristurus species share cephalic dorso-ventral compression, broad spatulate snouts and diagnostic labial-furrow states; meristics (including vertebral counts) and egg-capsule morphology provide additional taxonomic signal. Morphological ratios and fin shapes are also valuable for identification. Phylogenetic evidence generally supports monophyly of the genus and recovery of three species groups ( brunneus, spongiceps, longicephalus ), although some recent morphology-led hypotheses warrant further genomic testing. Apristurus is circumglobal (excluding polar seas and the Mediterranean), occupies depths ca. 24-2652 m and functions primarily as a generalist mesopredator, with region- and species-specific trophic specialisation. Reproductive ecology is oviparous; egg capsules commonly aggregate on structurally complex substrates (e.g., sponges and corals) where local hydrodynamics likely enhance embryonic ventilation. Fossil egg cases at cold seeps indicate long-standing associations with complex deep-sea habitats. Major threats to the genus arise from deep-sea trawl bycatch and emerging seabed industries. Threats are exacerbated by genus life-history traits (prolonged development, low fecundity) which imply high sensitivity, though many species remain listed as Least Concern owing to a paucity of data due to the depths at which the genus lives. Key research gaps identified include the need for a robust, integrative taxonomy; publicly accessible genetic reference libraries; in situ behavioural and life-history observations; quantification of bycatch and post-release mortality; and assessment of climate and mining impacts on nursery habitats. We provide a consolidated baseline of information to assist with accelerated discovery, identification and conservation of Apristurus across its global range.
10.3390/fishes11120686: Mandarin fish (Siniperca chuatsi) refuse artificial diets, but some individuals can be domesticated. To identify candidate molecular pathways and preliminary genomic loci associated with feed domestication difficulty, we compared easily domesticable (group T) and difficult-to-domesticate (group W) mandarin fish using brain transcriptome sequencing (n = 15 per group) and whole-genome resequencing (n = 30 per group). Transcriptome analysis identified 761 differentially expressed genes (DEGs), with down-regulated genes predominating in group T. Gene set enrichment analysis (GSEA) revealed nominally significant positive enrichment of neurotransmitter transporter activity, sodium symporter activity, and Wnt signaling in group T, while cytokine-cytokine receptor interaction was down-regulated. Weighted gene co-expression network analysis (WGCNA) identified the MEtan module as negatively correlated with growth-performance traits associated with domestication outcome and enriched in nucleosome, chromatin, and protein-DNA complex. Resequencing yielded 2,650,994 high-quality single nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs), with intergroup differential SNPs annotated to 14,956 genes. Multi-omics integration prioritized 32 candidate genes across neural signaling/transport, chromatin/nucleosome, immune/inflammation, steroid/lipid metabolism, and cell structure/other; core candidates included slc1a5, gpr84, olfml2bb, and histone family genes. Notably, SNPs in gpr84 and olfml2bb showed nominal differences between groups. These findings suggest that enhanced neurotransmitter recycling and synaptic plasticity, lower neuroimmune activation, and chromatin regulation are associated with feed domestication success, providing preliminary candidate loci that require validation in larger, independent populations and should not yet be regarded as established markers for marker-assisted selection in easily domesticable mandarin fish.
10.3390/fishes11120685: Growth rate represents a core economic trait that determines both aquaculture production performance and market value of the foxface rabbitfish (Siganus vulpinus). However, the molecular mechanisms underlying growth variation in this species remain largely uncharacterized. In this study, full-sibling S. vulpinus individuals reared under identical controlled conditions were stratified into a rapid-growth (RG) and a slow-growth (SG) group based on growth performance, and skeletal muscle transcriptome sequencing was conducted to identify growth-related candidate genes. A total of 24,036 expressed genes were detected across both groups, with 13,663 genes co-expressed in the two groups. Differential expression analysis revealed 707 differentially expressed genes (DEGs), including 329 upregulated and 378 downregulated genes in the RG group relative to the SG group. GO and KEGG enrichment analyses showed that these DEGs were primarily enriched in biological processes associated with energy metabolism, protein turnover, amino acid metabolism, cytoskeletal organization, and muscle structural maintenance. Notably, the glycolysis/gluconeogenesis pathway was significantly overrepresented, implying that carbohydrate metabolism and ATP provision are key contributors to muscle growth variation in S. vulpinus. Within the DEG set, S. vulpinus Eno3 was significantly upregulated in the RG group and identified as a core gene implicated in the glycolysis/gluconeogenesis pathway. Bioinformatic characterization demonstrated that S. vulpinus Eno3 harbors a 1305 bp open reading frame (ORF) encoding 435 amino acids, and possesses the canonical conserved structural features of the enolase protein family. Phylogenetic analysis, conserved motif identification, functional domain annotation, and multiple sequence alignment collectively confirmed that S. vulpinus Eno3 is evolutionarily conserved and likely functions as a β-enolase isoform involved in glycolytic regulation. These findings indicate that S. vulpinus Eno3 may contribute to rapid muscle growth by modulating glycolytic flux, ATP generation, and metabolic intermediate availability. Collectively, this study provides valuable candidate gene resources and a theoretical foundation for deciphering the molecular mechanisms underlying growth variation, and supports the future development of molecular breeding programs for S. vulpinus.
10.3390/fishes11120684: Abandoned, lost, or otherwise discarded fishing gear (ALDFG) poses persistent environmental and management challenges. This study evaluated six direct gillnet marking methods and four gear-accounting units for South Korea’s fishing gear deposit system. The marking-type assessment combined previously derived AHP weights, preferences from 145 fishers and eight gear companies, and detachment observations from 1856 markings on nine net panels. At a common two-cycle endpoint, the textile double-sided tape fiber label ranked first (0.829), followed by the ultrasonic-welded (0.823) and gel-type tape labels (0.817). Using each gillnet’s last available observation changed the leading method to ultrasonic welding (0.718), while excluding swimming crab observations changed it to the gel-type label. For marking units, net-panel ranked first under equal expert-stakeholder weighting, whereas expert AHP alone favored weight. The results identify context-specific candidates for further field testing, not universally superior technologies or evidence of deposit-system effectiveness.
10.3390/fishes11120683: Aromatase (Cyp19a1), which converts testosterone to 17β-estradiol, plays a critical role in ovarian differentiation in teleosts. However, the transcriptional mechanisms regulating cyp19a1 during gonadal sex differentiation in Japanese eel (Anguilla japonica) remain unclear. We investigated the effects of Adrenal 4 binding protein/Steroidogenic factor 1 (Ad4bp/Sf-1) and Forkhead box L2 (Foxl2) and Foxl3 paralogs, and follicle-stimulating hormone (Fsh) signaling on cyp19a1 transcription using luciferase reporter assays in HEK293T and JTC-35 cells. Ad4bp/Sf-1, Foxl2a, or Fsh signaling alone did not activate the full-length (-5292/+38) cyp19a1 5′-flanking region, whereas combinations of these factors increased transcriptional activity. The simultaneous presence of Ad4bp/Sf-1, Foxl2a, and Fsh signaling produced the highest transcriptional activity in HEK293T cells. Co-transfection of Foxl2b with Foxl2a tended to reduce relative luciferase luminescence compared with Foxl2a alone, whereas Foxl3a and Foxl3b showed transcriptional activation potential under the experimental conditions used. Foxl3a, in particular, exhibited markedly high transcriptional activity in both cell lines despite the testis-biased expression of foxl3a and foxl3b in vivo. Deletion analysis showed that factor-dependent activation was markedly reduced by deletion to -847/+38 and abolished when the -847/+38 region was removed. Putative Ad4bp/Sf-1 and Foxl2 binding sites and a cAMP-responsive element were identified within this proximal region, suggesting that it may contribute to transcriptional responses to multiple regulatory factors. These findings provide insights into the potential combinatorial regulation of the Japanese eel cyp19a1 promoter and the distinct transcriptional regulatory properties of Foxl2 and Foxl3 paralogs under heterologous reporter assay conditions.
10.3390/fishes11120682: Replacing fish oil (FO) in salmonid feeds alters long-chain polyunsaturated fatty acid (LC-PUFA) supply, but the combined effects on hepatic fatty acids, elongase expression and gut microbiota are poorly known when the lipid source is the only dietary variable. Juvenile rainbow trout (Oncorhynchus mykiss) were fed for 60 days on six low-fishmeal (10%) diets with FO, shrimp by-product oil (SH), camelina oil (CO), canola oil (CA), or blends SHCA (25% SH + 75% CA) and COCA (25% CO + 75% CA), with three tanks per diet. Hepatic fatty acids, elovl2 and elovl5 expression and distal intestinal microbiota were analyzed; growth and fillet lipid data from the same fish and tanks were reported separately. 10.1007/s10750-026-06484-6: The aim of this study was to evaluate whether bryophyte host identity and growth form influence epibryophytic diatom assemblages beyond the effect of environmental filtering in karst springs. We hypothesized that environmental variables would remain the primary drivers of community structure, while bryophyte-related effects would be detectable at finer taxonomic or functional levels. Epibryophytic diatom assemblages from karst springs in the Apuseni Mountains (Romania) were analysed using taxonomic, diversity and functional approaches. Oven-dried material from whole bryophyte tufts was processed to obtain cleaned diatom samples. Bryophyte identity accounted for part of the compositional variation, but no consistent effects were detected when analyses were restricted to adequately replicated hosts or when permutations were constrained within springs. Similarly, bryophyte growth form did not significantly influence diatom community composition or ecological guild structure. However, environmental variables significantly structured diatom assemblages at the spring level, with water temperature and canopy cover emerging as the main predictors. Assemblages were consistently dominated by low-profile guild taxa, suggesting adaptation to hydrodynamic stress and continuously flowing conditions. Overall, the results indicate that environmental filtering represents the primary driver of epibryophytic diatoms in karst springs, whereas bryophyte host identity exerts a limited detectable influence under relatively homogeneous carbonate conditions.
10.1007/s10750-026-06466-8: Environmental DNA (eDNA) is a sensitive tool to detect rare and elusive species, including both endangered species and invasive alien species (IAS) at early stages of colonization. We aimed to i) design and test a quantitative PCR eDNA protocol for the detection of 22 freshwater species of conservation concern belonging to five phyla, ii) identify environmental factors influencing species detection, and iii) assess the cost-effectiveness of eDNA-based monitoring versus traditional survey methods. Target species included 14 endangered species listed in the Habitats Directive 92/43/EEC and eight IAS listed under the EU Regulation 1143/2014 potentially occurring in Central Italy. Thirteen assays were newly developed. Water samples were collected at 53 sampling sites. Relationships between eDNA species detection and 25 fine- and large-scale environmental variables were explored through principal component analysis. We detected 18 of the 22 target species, with highest detection rates for fish, amphibians, molluscs, and mammals. For four species, detection was significantly associated with environmental factors. Compared with traditional methods, eDNA monitoring was faster ( < 46% of time), more cost-effective ( < 88% of costs), and more accurate ( + 49 new occurrences). Our results demonstrate the high potential of qPCR-based eDNA for large-scale freshwater biodiversity monitoring.
10.17977/2580-2402.1277: The escalation of production capacity within the aquaculture sector triggers an accumulation of solid waste that degrades water quality, a condition establishing fundamental operational constraints for conventional mechanical filtration systems in recirculating aquaculture systems. Hydrocyclone separators emerge as a promising economically viable technological alternative; however, investigations regarding their specific optimization for managing fishery particulates with low density margins remain profoundly limited. This computational investigation implements a computational fluid dynamics framework, coupling the Reynolds stress model with the discrete phase model, to quantify the separation performance of a modified hydrocyclone design across ten variations of inlet flow rates. Through validation against benchmark data, the simulation outputs reveal that the degree of vortex maturity is absolutely governed by the fluid injection velocity. The minimum flow rate proves inadequate to construct a coherent forced vortex core, whereas the maximum flow condition conversely generates a dual peak Rankine vortex structure manifesting spatial asymmetry. In stark contrast to fundamental theoretical probabilities, the cumulative separation efficacy exhibits a negative correlation with increasing flow rates, characterized by an efficiency degradation from 72% to 64%. This physical reality confirms that an inlet momentum exceeding the optimal threshold escalates local turbulence and reduces particle retention duration, which in turn comprehensively disrupts the effectiveness of the centrifugal separation mechanism.
10.71317/kjard.2.11.2026.1099: The northern Arabian Sea along Pakistan's 1,001 km coastline represents a biologically productive yet increasingly threatened marine ecosystem, supporting over 500 cataloged fish species of substantial commercial and ecological importance.
