Escalating anthropogenic pressures, including overfishing, illegal, unreported, and unregulated (IUU) fishing, habitat degradation, and the intensifying Arabian Sea Oxygen Minimum Zone (OMZ), have severely altered fish community structures and precipitated declines in key commercial stocks. Traditional monitoring approaches, reliant on catch landings, net trawling, and morphological taxonomy, are constrained by phenotypic plasticity, cryptic speciation, specimen damage, and an inability to identify early life stages or processed products. This review synthesizes the transformative potential of two complementary molecular technologies environmental DNA (eDNA) metabarcoding and population genomics for biodiversity assessment and sustainable fisheries management along the Pakistan coast. eDNA metabarcoding enables non-invasive, high-throughput, multi-taxa community profiling through mitochondrial markers (COI, Cyt b, 12S/16S rRNA), facilitating detection of elusive, endangered, and cryptic species, including remnant sawfish populations and coral-associated assemblages in Astola Island MPA. Population genomics, leveraging SNPs and mitochondrial sequencing, resolves stock boundaries, genetic diversity, and demographic histories, revealing distinct Evolutionary Significant Units in silver pomfret (Pampus argenteus) and genetic connectivity patterns in Spanish mackerel (Scomberomorus commerson). Integrated applications extend to seafood traceability via DNA-based QR codes, IUU fishing detection, and Blue Economy policy alignment with SDG 14. Key challenges include eDNA degradation under high temperatures, PCR bias, incomplete regional reference databases, and infrastructural capacity gaps. Strategic multi-institutional partnerships and sustained investment are essential for operational implementation, offering a paradigm shift toward resilient, evidence-based fisheries governance in Pakistan.
10.1111/jfd.70328: ABSTRACT Hyperostosis in wild fishes remains poorly documented and quantitative information on its size-related onset and anatomical distribution in Oligoplites palometa (Cuvier, 1832) is limited. We quantified hyperostosis prevalence and described its skeletal distribution across size classes in O. palometa from two estuarine systems on the coast of Rio de Janeiro, Brazil (Guanabara Bay and Sepetiba Bay). A total of 31 specimens ranging from 45 to 510 mm TL were examined by radiography, followed by excision and morphometric analysis of the unaffected and affected bones. Hyperostosis was observed in all examined individuals ≥ 315 mm TL, whereas none was detected in specimens ≤ 82 mm. No individuals between 82 and 315 mm total length (TL) were available, limiting the assessment of the onset and progression of hyperostosis within this size range. Hyperostoses were detected in the cranium, cleithrum, dorsal pterygiophores and anal pterygiophores, with the cleithrum showing the highest prevalence (80.64%), followed by dorsal pterygiophores (77.41%), anal pterygiophores (67.7%) and cranium (61.29%). These findings indicate a consistent size-related pattern of skeletal involvement, highlighting the importance of population size structure when evaluating hyperostosis in wild fish populations.
10.1111/jfd.70326: ABSTRACT Climate change is expected to increase seawater salinity, potentially altering the physiological responses of marine organisms. In salmonids, elevated salinity has been associated with outbreaks of infectious diseases; however, the mechanisms linking salinity with intestinal epithelial dysfunction and bacterial invasion remain poorly understood. This study evaluated the effects of increased sodium chloride concentrations on the integrity of the rainbow trout intestinal epithelial cell line RTgutGC and its relationship with P. salmonis translocation. Cells cultured under control (8 g/L NaCl) or hyperosmotic conditions (16 and 20 g/L NaCl) were assessed for cytotoxicity, epithelial integrity, permeability, bacterial translocation, and gene expression. Hyperosmotic conditions significantly increased epithelial permeability and reduced barrier integrity, as evidenced by altered paracellular permeability to Dextran FITC and modulation of tight junction-related genes, including cld-3 and zo-1 . Salinity also induced the expression of osmoregulatory ( tsc22 and nka ) and immune-related genes ( il-1β and il-10 ), indicating activation of response to osmotic stress. Importantly, elevated salinity significantly enhanced the translocation of P. salmonis across the epithelial monolayer, whereas no bacterial translocation was detected under control conditions. Moreover, high salinity increased infection-associated cytotoxicity, mainly at 20 g/L NaCl. Together, these findings demonstrate that increased sodium chloride concentration compromises intestinal epithelial barrier function while promoting P. salmonis translocation. These results provide mechanistic evidence linking climate-driven changes in seawater salinity with increased epithelial susceptibility to bacterial pathogens and suggest that osmotic stress may represent an important environmental factor influencing the pathogenesis of piscirickettsiosis in salmonids.
10.1111/jfd.70325: ABSTRACT Tilapia lake virus is a major constraint to sustainable Nile tilapia ( Oreochromis niloticus ) production, yet effective antiviral interventions remain limited. We evaluated the antiviral potential of procyanidin against tilapia lake virus (TiLV) using complementary cell-based and in vivo challenge models involving 300 Nile tilapia. Procyanidin displayed a concentration-dependent safety profile, with a non-cytotoxic concentration of 0.0128 mg/mL in E-11 cells and an estimated LC 10 of 0.6528 mg/mL in fish. At the selected cellular concentration, procyanidin prevented virus-associated cytopathic effects and reduced TiLV RNA in culture supernatants to below the RT-qPCR detection limit. In vivo, procyanidin administration 24 h before or after viral challenge increased survival from 43.33% in untreated infected fish to 80.00% and 73.33%, respectively, corresponding to relative percent survival values of 64.44% and 52.22%. Treatment also reduced brain viral load by up to 3.12 log 10 units and was associated with qualitatively better-preserved brain and liver histoarchitecture. Hepatic transcriptional profiling revealed distinct treatment-associated expression patterns across inflammatory, innate immune recognition, antigen presentation, cellular immunity and antiviral interferon signalling pathways, with pre-treatment producing the strongest induction of several antiviral genes. Together, these findings identify procyanidin as a candidate antiviral compound against tilapia lake virus, with in vitro antiviral activity accompanied in vivo by improved survival, reduced brain viral load and treatment-associated changes in hepatic immune-gene expression, although the underlying protective mechanism remains to be established.
10.1163/15718085-20261060: Abstract The Chinese Fisheries Law was adopted in January 1986 and came into force on 1 July 1986. Four amendments and one revision have been made to the document since then. A revision in 2025 reflects China’s commitment to enhancing fisheries quality, efficiency, and green development. Initially, this article provides a brief overview of the Law, and then it evaluates some key changes in the revision of 2025. It concludes by pointing out some concerns that remain in the Law following the recent revision.
10.1111/1365-2656.70408: Abstract Spatial population synchrony, broadly defined as the correlated temporal dynamics of a population metric (e.g. abundance, biomass or growth rates) across sampled areas, is a central theme in ecology. Here, we investigated spatial synchrony in the abundance of 38 fish species from the Jirau Reservoir, a large impoundment in the Amazonian basin, over a decade. We combined cross-correlation at zero lag, tail dependence, synchrony networks, species traits and wavelets to investigate asymmetry, geography and the temporal structure of spatial synchrony. We found that 12 species exhibited significant river-wide synchrony, with no asymmetrical or spatial patterns of within-river synchrony. Water level synchrony, dispersal difficulty and density dependence explained little of the variation in within-river synchrony. However, wavelet analyses showed that the strength of river-wide synchrony varied across temporal scales, and some species also shifted in the dominant timescale of synchrony over time. Furthermore, key species traits such as migratory strategy, body size and trophic level were not significantly correlated with river-wide synchrony levels. These findings underscore the necessity of using multifaceted analytical approaches to understand and manage fish populations in human-altered aquatic ecosystems, where local factors may override broad-scale drivers.
10.1007/s11356-026-38367-7: Microplastics (MPs) are a serious global concern due to their potential risks to the environment, wildlife, and human health. The ingestion of MPs by organisms, such as marine invertebrates, can lead to their transfer through the trophic food chain, ultimately impacting human health. The present study investigates the quantity, shape, color, and polymer type of microplastics found in both the whole soft tissues and external surfaces of the spotted babylon (Babylonia areolata) collected in January (Northeast monsoon), April (transition period), and August (Southwest monsoon) 2024 from four sampling sites along the coast of Rayong Province, Thailand. The results revealed a total microplastic detection rate of 73.9% from the external body, with 1.14 ± 0.40 particles/individual, and 61.9% from the internal body contained at least one MP particle, with 1.01 ± 0.47 particles/individual. The overall MP contamination showed significant seasonal differences, with the highest contamination observed in August. The study also demonstrated a significant positive correlation between microplastic contamination and shellfish size. The most abundant MP shape was fiber, primarily in blue, followed by fragments and films. FT-IR analysis identified several plastic polymers, with the most common being PET, PES, and PP. Fibers were the predominant MP shape, followed by fragments and films, while PET, PES, and PP were the major polymer types identified by FT-IR. The predominance of PET-fibers suggests a potential contribution from textile-related sources. Nevertheless, MP levels in spotted babylon from Rayong Province were lower than those reported in previous studies. Our findings highlight the potential for MP transfer to humans through seafood consumption, raising concerns for food safety, and emphasize the need for regular monitoring of edible marine organisms and effective plastic waste management policies in the region.
10.63249/j-sh.v1i2.167: This study analyzes fishers' compliance with and perceptions of licensing documents at the Marine and Fisheries Resources Surveillance Office (PSDKP), Takalar Station, which operates within the working area of PSDKP Bitung. The objectives were: (1) to describe fishers' compliance with the procedures for issuing licensing documents and (2) to describe fishers' perceptions of licensing documents through an assessment of service quality. The study employed a descriptive design with a survey approach. A purposive sample of 30 adult fishers (aged 18-59 years) who were applying for or had previously applied for licenses was selected. The instrument was a four-point Likert-scale questionnaire. Compliance was measured using 20 statements representing 10 indicators of public service compliance assessment based on Ombudsman Regulation of the Republic of Indonesia Number 22 of 2016. Perceived service quality was measured using 16 statements representing the eight elements of the Service Quality Perception Survey (SPKP) (Constitutional Court of the Republic of Indonesia, 2023). Data were analyzed descriptively through frequency and percentage tabulation. The results show that fishers' compliance is very high; variation appeared only in the habit of reading written information on notice boards or service media (27 always; 3 rarely). Fishers' perceptions were also predominantly positive: information was easy to understand, requirements and procedures were clear, the service flow was easy to follow, completion time matched the estimate and was relatively short, facilities were comfortable and adequate, and officers were responsive in consultations and complaint handling. Regarding costs, all respondents considered the fees to be in accordance with regulations, yet seven respondents sometimes felt that the cost of processing was quite burdensome. It is concluded that licensing services at PSDKP Takalar are effective in fostering compliance and positive perceptions, with recommendations to strengthen the dissemination of written information and to mitigate indirect cost burdens so that services become more inclusive. These findings are relevant to improving licensing governance.
10.9734/ajrcos/2026/v19i11936: Fish diseases can compromise aquaculture production through reduced growth, deteriorating fish quality and increased mortality. Conventional disease identification often depends on time-consuming manual inspection. This study compared convolutional neural network (CNN) architectures containing two, three and four convolutional layers for classifying five fish disease categories and healthy fish. A dataset of 1,600 images was assembled from existing repositories and selected websites. The images were resized to 224 × 224 pixels and divided into training, validation and testing subsets at an 80:10:10 ratio. The models were trained for 100 epochs using a batch size of 32, with rotation and contrast augmentation applied to the training images. Model performance was assessed through classification accuracy, training and validation curves, and class-level evaluation measures. Across five executions, average test accuracies were 91.13%, 95.73% and 95.27% for the two-, three- and four-layer CNNs, respectively. The three-layer CNN showed comparatively stable training and validation behaviour, whereas the other architectures displayed less stable generalisation or indications of overfitting. Two additional baseline models were evaluated on the same dataset: fine-tuned VGG16 achieved 96.41% accuracy, and a VGG16-Random Forest hybrid achieved 93.56%. Among the three CNN architectures examined, the three-layer model provided the highest average accuracy and a favourable balance between classification performance and architectural depth on the dataset used.
10.1007/s41742-026-01301-3: One significant ecological concern regarding plastic pollution is the ability of microplastics (MPs) to adsorb and concentrate heavy metals in the marine environment. The sector-field inductively coupled plasma mass spectrometry (SF-ICP-MS) technique was applied to determine heavy metal concentrations in MPs from beach sediments, in fish muscle, and in the gastrointestinal tract (GIT) of fish from the Caspian Sea. First, metal determination in sediment and biological matrices was validated by analyzing the marine sediment certified reference material (IAEA-158) and DORM-4 fish protein certified reference material. For metals that pose greater risks to the marine environment and may come from multiple anthropogenic sources, the concentration factors (CF), namely, the heavy metal concentration ratio from MPs in sediment to sediment (CMPs/s), reach 3 (Cd), 7.7 (Pb), and 30 (Zn). The average amount of MPs was 55 items/kg, with the minimum and maximum values ranging from 14 to 155 items/kg. The same methodology was employed to quantify metals in MPs extracted from the fish gastrointestinal tract. The developed method holds promise as a potentially useful analytical tool for marine monitoring and precise assessment of MPs with regard to heavy metal contamination and impact on marine ecosystems.
10.63249/j-sh.v1i2.166: Fish Landing Bases (PPI) play a strategic role in supporting capture fisheries, improving fishers' livelihoods, and strengthening coastal economic development. This study aimed to analyze the implementation of the policy on the utilization of the Lonrae Fish Landing Base (PPI) in Bone Regency using the policy implementation framework proposed by Van Meter and Van Horn. A qualitative descriptive approach was employed through in-depth interviews, field observations, documentation, and secondary data analysis. Informants consisted of representatives from the Provincial Marine and Fisheries Office, the Bone Regency Fisheries Office, PPI management, fishers, and local community members. The findings indicate that the implementation of the policy has generally progressed in accordance with its intended objectives, particularly in improving fisheries services and supporting local economic activities. The policy benefits from clear objectives, positive implementer commitment, supportive social conditions, and relatively effective inter-agency coordination. However, its effectiveness is constrained by limited financial resources, insufficient human resources, inadequate supporting facilities, suboptimal communication with fishers, and operational management challenges. These constraints have prevented the full optimization of PPI functions, particularly regarding fish auction services, infrastructure utilization, and service delivery. Strengthening institutional coordination, increasing infrastructure investment, enhancing human resource capacity, improving stakeholder communication, and expanding operational budgets are therefore essential to maximize the role of Lonrae Fish Landing Base as a sustainable fisheries infrastructure that contributes to fisheries governance and the welfare of coastal communities.
10.6066/jtip.2026.37.3.271: Tuna processing industries generate a significant amount of by-products, including dark muscle and skin, which are potential sources of functional proteins such as fish protein hydrolysate (FPH) and gelatin. This study aimed to characterize FPH from tuna dark muscle and gelatin from tuna skin, while evaluating the effects of freeze-drying (FD) and oven-drying (OV) on their physicochemical and antioxidant properties. The results indicated that the yield and proximate composition of FPH-FD and FPH-OV did not differ significantly (p>0.05). In contrast, antioxidant activity showed a significant effect (p<0.05), with FPH-OV exhibiting a stronger radical-scavenging capacity than FPH-FD, as indicated by its lower IC50 value, namely 152.75 µg/mL and 647.68 µg/mL, respectively. Unlike FPH, the drying methods for gelatin significantly influenced moisture content, ash content, gel strength, and antioxidant activity (p<0.05). The freeze-dried gelatin had higher gel strength (399.7 g) than oven-dried gelatin (372.7 g), although both values exceeded the typical high-Bloom range of 200-300 g. Under the tested laboratory conditions, oven-drying at 60 °C produced FPH with yield and proximate composition comparable to those of freeze-drying and with higher antioxidant activity, whereas it increased moisture and ash contents of gelatin and reduced its gel strength.
10.1007/s44187-026-01368-z: Abstract Fish and fishery products are increasingly recognized as important components of healthy and sustainable diets, yet consumption remains low and seasonal in several inland European markets. This study examines motivational heterogeneity in fish and fishery product consumption in Hungary and explores its potential implications for freshwater aquaculture commercialization. The total sample comprised 576 respondents, of whom 463 reported consuming fish or fishery products. Exploratory factor analysis and Gaussian Mixture Modelling were conducted on the subsample of 314 fish-consuming respondents who provided complete valid responses to all motivational items. Exploratory factor analysis based on polychoric correlations identified two latent motivational dimensions: convenience and accessibility, and health and product characteristics. Gaussian Mixture Modelling distinguished three consumer segments: health-oriented, moderately practical consumers; low-motivation consumers; and convenience-dominated consumers. Taste and perceived health benefits emerged as the strongest general motivations, while convenience, accessibility and ready-to-cook formats contributed more strongly to differentiating between consumer profiles. The findings indicate that motivational heterogeneity may be relevant when considering the commercialization of freshwater aquaculture products in a low-consumption inland market. However, the survey measured motivations toward fish and fishery products in general rather than attitudes toward farmed fish specifically. Therefore, the aquaculture-related conclusions should be interpreted as sectoral implications rather than as direct empirical evidence of attitudes toward aquaculture. Interpreted in the light of previous literature, the identified consumer profiles suggest that transparent product information, trust-building and convenient product formats may support the development of more differentiated commercialization approaches for freshwater aquaculture value chains.
10.1007/s10499-026-02755-0: Mariculture is recognised as a sustainable livelihood in multi-use marine protected areas (MPAs). Surprisingly, specific carrying capacity (CC) models are unavailable in the literature to manage the development of mariculture. This study proposed a specific CC model for designating mariculture zoning in multi-use small-island MPAs, using a modified Modelling-Ongrowing fish farm-Monitoring (MOM) approach. The study was applied in the Anambas MPA to represent a common type of multi-use small-island MPA in most developing countries. To develop the model, three simulated finfish net cages were placed in different locations to collect field data and support model simulations. The results show that the three geographical areas within the MPA have CC limited by oxygen concentration, rather than by other variables. The levels of CC ranged from 49.93 to 119.9 kg/m3 in the wet season when using trash fish and from 7.14 to 116.41 kg/m3 in the dry season when using commercial feed. Because the CC model proposed here is based on the lowest MOM module values and farming seasons, the typical CC/holding density for finfish mariculture in the Anambas Archipelago MPA is 27.76 kg/m3 in the wet season and 7.14 kg/m3 in the dry season. These findings highlight that each location (mariculture zone) within an MPA has a distinct CC, influenced by fish farming practices and environmental characteristics. Therefore, mariculture development in MPAs should be limited through site-specific CCs based on established mariculture zones, with site selection and CC estimation for each site, taking into account the different feeds used, cultured fish species, and seasonality.
10.1007/s10641-026-01940-7: Surgeonfishes are a common group of fishes in coral reefs, and their spawning aggregations have been reported from various regions. This study aimed to examine the ecological characteristics of the aggregation of Ctenochaetus striatus in an Okinawan coral reef. These include (1) the lunar phase and tidal rhythm periodicities of aggregation formation and (2) the difference in fish density between inside and outside the aggregation site by using time-lapse still photography and underwater observations. The 87-day time-lapse still photography survey and time-series analysis using a correlogram revealed a significant semi-lunar rhythm in aggregation formation. Fish aggregations were generally observed during several consecutive days after the first quarter and last quarter moons, although some exceptions were observed. The aggregations were observed primarily during ebb tide in the neap and middle tide phases, but they were sometimes observed at high tide or during flood tide. The aggregations were observed for several hours, during which fish abundance increased rapidly before spawning and decreased rapidly afterward, respectively. The maximum fish density at the aggregation site (240 m2) was 1050 individuals (equivalent to 4.38 individuals per 1 m2). Since the fish density inside the aggregation site during spawning was 704.7-fold higher than that outside the aggregation site, and group spawning events were observed during when aggregation formed, the aggregation of C. striatus on this Okinawan coral reef can be regarded as a spawning aggregation.
10.1111/cobi.70425: Abstract Coastal fisheries are typically managed within bounds set by political jurisdictions of nations and their provinces. This approach often results in multiple states/provinces managing a single genetically distinct fish population autonomously and typically without coordination. In multispecies, decentralized, and data-poor fisheries, this can lead to inadequate assessments and fisheries overharvests. We developed an integrative risk indicator for interjurisdictional stocks (IRIIS) to assess the overexploitation risk to interjurisdictional populations. IRIIS incorporates species-specific vulnerability, distribution of genetically distinct populations with respect to jurisdictional boundaries, and differences in management practices across jurisdictions. As a case study, we used genetic tools and policy analysis to evaluate nine common target species spanning multiple jurisdictions along India's western coast. We showed that distinct populations of a species differed greatly in how they are managed by respective fisheries, and management disparities across jurisdictions can strongly influence the overexploitation risk for a population. IRIIS clearly identified these differences and helped determine specific fisheries policies that need reconciling across jurisdictions to reduce the risk of overexploitation. As a comprehensive management instrument, IRIIS is dynamic and sensitive to periodic revisions in fishery policy and could guide managers across jurisdictions in lowering the overexploitation risks to multispecies coastal fisheries.
10.3390/fishes11110679: Underwater fish disease detection is a vital visual perception task for health monitoring, disease early warning and precision breeding management in aquaculture. In complicated underwater environments, fish lesions suffer from faint boundaries and tiny sizes, while cross-scale fused features of detection models are contaminated by mixed degradation interference. To tackle the above issues, this paper proposes a YOLOv12-based detection method for fish lesions under complex underwater conditions. Firstly, an underwater spatial context receptive field module named CRB is designed. It expands the receptive range of shallow features through two-stage depthwise separable dilated convolution, establishes spatial correlations between local lesion responses and surrounding neighborhood structures and enhances the local structural representation of lesions with faint boundaries and small scales. Secondly, an underwater degradation-aware channel enhancement module DCE is presented. Degradation priors are constructed from image intensity, gradient and local contrast. Combined with mixed pooling to generate channel weights, the module recalibrates lesion-related responses and degradation interference responses after cross-scale feature fusion, so as to suppress the propagation of degradation noise within fused features. Lastly, the experiments are conducted on a self-built underwater largemouth bass lesion detection dataset. The experimental results show that the proposed model achieves Precision of 87.4%, Recall of 81.3%, F1-score of 84.2% and mAP@50 of 85.8%, which outperforms the baseline model by 3.3, 3.7, 3.5 and 3.6 percentage points, respectively. The proposed method serve as an effective visual perception solution for fish lesion detection in complex underwater environments.
10.1111/jfb.70740: Abstract Aquatic invasive species are among the top threats to freshwater fishes globally, causing declines in freshwater biodiversity and altering ecosystem functioning. Within Nova Scotia, Canada, invasive chain pickerel ( Esox niger ) and smallmouth bass ( Micropterus dolomieu ) have been found to reduce the abundance and diversity of native fishes. The invasive range of both species threatens and overlaps with the critical habitat of one of Canada's most endangered fishes, the Atlantic whitefish ( Coregonus huntsmani ). Here, we examine the seasonal space and depth use of adult chain pickerel and smallmouth bass using acoustic telemetry in Milipsigate Lake, Nova Scotia. High-resolution positions were calculated and analyzed using resource selection functions (RSFs) and generalized additive models (GAMs) to determine the relative space use and predicted depth of both species within the lake. Areas with the highest relative probability of use (>0.7) differed between species, and seasonal changes in space use were only significant for smallmouth bass ( p < 0.001). Chain pickerel had the highest relative probability of space use in shallow areas of Milipsigate Lake (<4 m), whereas areas with the highest relative probability of space use for smallmouth bass were concentrated around four distinct overwintering sites. Chain pickerel were predicted to occupy a narrow range (~2 m) of relatively shallow depths year-round. Smallmouth bass were predicted to occupy depths that were on average three times deeper than chain pickerel, including a broad range of depths from spring to fall (0-15 m) that contracted during the winter months (2-6 m). Here, we showed that the combined occupancy of the lake by both species is extensive, with limited overlap in space or depth use year-round. Ultimately, the methodologies and results presented in this study could help inform the development of management strategies for invasive freshwater fish species.
10.1007/s12520-026-02600-8: Abstract Euryhaline fish pose a challenge when interpreting the fishing habitats utilised in areas where both fresh and saline waters would have been accessible. One such example is the island of Gotland, central Baltic Sea, where archaeological fishbone assemblages often contain euryhaline fish species that could have originated from different habitats. To understand which waterbodies were used for fishing in the past, 87 Sr/ 86 Sr ratios of 41 fish teeth from the Mesolithic, Neolithic and Viking Age - Middle Ages were analysed using laser ablation-multi collector-inductively coupled plasma-mass spectrometry and correlated with a bioavailable baseline of water sources. We identify several shifts in the origin of euryhaline fish and discuss them in relation to environmental and cultural shifts. Using modern ecological knowledge, we discuss the likely habitat structures in the now drained lakes of Gotland. The results enhance our understanding of prehistoric and historic fishing practices and shed light on the broader socio-economic and environmental dynamics on the island of Gotland.
10.51317/wrehv191: The purpose of this study was to analyse the influence of effective communication on the sustainability of women’s small-scale fisheries in Homa Bay County, Kenya. The sustainability of women-led small-scale fisheries enterprises is often constrained by inadequate communication and information-sharing mechanisms, which limit women's ability to access timely market information, share enterprise-related challenges, participate in collective decision-making, and identify solutions to emerging operational constraints. These communication barriers stand to undermine enterprise resilience, compromise the quality and nutritional value of fish products, and ultimately threaten the livelihood security of fishers' households. The study is anchored on the Magic Bullet Theory (Hypodermic Needle Model). Applying the mixed-methods approach, the study analysed quantitative and qualitative data collected from a sample of 330 small-scale women fishers with a ninety-six per cent response rate. The results from both data sources were triangulated and became the basis of the study findings and conclusions. Fisher’s effective communication had a moderate and significant relationship with the sustainability of small-scale fisheries. The findings revealed that r=0.342, R2= 0.117, F (1,341) =45.597, at P=0.000<0.05, confirming that fishers' effective communication had a statistically significant contribution to the sustainability of small-scale fisheries. The coefficient of determination, R2= 0.117, indicates that fishers' effective communication activities explain 11.7 per cent of the variation in the sustainability of fisheries by women. The paper contributes to the literature on the role of effective communication in the sustainability of small-scale enterprises, poverty reduction among small-scale fishers, and nutritional value among families of women fishers. Furthermore, it adds to the importance of fishers engaging in a dialogue with the market and community.
10.1139/as-2026-0032: In this paper, we describe how Inuit traditional knowledge and western science have been mobilized over three decades to support the co-management of Arctic char (iqalukpik) (Salvelinus alpinus) fisheries in the waters near Ulukhaktok in the Inuvialuit Settlement Region (ISR), Canada. Fisheries within the ISR are co-managed under the provisions of the Inuvialuit Final Agreement, with support from the Inuvialuit-Canada Fisheries Joint Management Committee (FJMC) as the designated co-management board. In response to community concerns of declines in one of its most important subsistence fisheries, the FJMC worked with Inuit from Ulukhaktok to establish a community-based Working Group focused on Arctic char in the area in 1993. Through the efforts and leadership of the Ulukhaktok Char Working Group (UCWG), co-management partners have mobilized traditional knowledge and western science continually over the past three decades through opportunities for information-sharing both within the UCWG and the broader community, harvest data collection, fisheries monitoring, and additional community-driven research programs. These activities have informed the UCWG in the development, implementation, and ongoing annual reviews of its community Fishing Plan, which describes the current knowledge of the fishery and management measures that support conservation, sustainable use, and stewardship.
10.3897/aiep.56.213543: Elasmobranchs are ecologically and commercially important, but biological information remains limited for many species. This study investigated length-weight relationships (LWRs) of elasmobranchs caught as bycatch in a set-net fishery at Nishiki, Mie Prefecture, Japan, during 2018-2025. A total of 739 individuals representing 21 species were collected during 284 fishing operations, and 15 species with at least five individuals remaining after exclusion of damaged specimens and Cook’s distance outliers were analyzed. LWR parameters were estimated, for groups with at least ten specimens, in 13 species: Cephaloscyllium umbratile Jordan et Fowler, 1903; Sphyrna zygaena (Linnaeus, 1758); Hemitriakis japanica (Müller et Henle, 1839); Mustelus manazo Bleeker, 1854; Triakis scyllium Müller et Henle, 1839; Heterodontus japonicus Maclay et Macleay, 1884; Bathytoshia brevicaudata (Hutton, 1875); Hemitrygon akajei (Müller et Henle, 1841); Hemitrygon izuensis (Nishida et Nakaya, 1988); Gymnura japonica (Temminck et Schlegel, 1850); Myliobatis tobijei Bleeker, 1854; Urolophus aurantiacus Müller et Henle, 1841; and Okamejei schmidti (Ishiyama, 1958). Of the 15 species analyzed, 11 are classified as threatened on the IUCN Red List and two Near Threatened. For batoids, both disc width (DW) and total length (TL) were evaluated, and DW gave higher coefficients of determination than TL in all six ray species with sufficient data. Sex-combined LWR exponents ( b ) ranged from 1.659 to 4.168. BIC-based model selection indicated sex-specific intercepts with a common slope for four species-measurement combinations. These LWRs provide baseline biometric information for biomass estimation, bycatch assessment, and fisheries management.
10.3354/aei00543: This study investigated the spatiotemporal distribution, ecological risks, and health hazards of antibiotics in aquaculture environments of the Karst Plateau, southern China. In total, 37 antibiotics were detected in water and sediment, and 34 in fish muscle, with sulfonamides and quinolones predominating. Significant seasonal variations (p < 0.05) occurred: sulfonamides and macrolides peaked in autumn, while quinolones and tetracyclines prevailed in winter. Spatially, Guanling was a contamination hotspot with highest sulfonamides in autumn and quinolones in winter; Ziyun showed strong seasonal contrasts, and Kaiyang had the lowest levels but unique fish markers (Chlortetracycline, Anisomycin, Sulfadiazine, Enoxacin). Water chemistry was Ca 2+ -Mg 2+ -SO 4 2- type, and antibiotic sources correlated with agricultural and domestic discharges. Sediments accumulated 8 antibiotics (Trimethoprim, Sulfacetamide, Cinoxacin, Enoxacin, Enrofloxacin, Flumequine, Ofloxacin, Oxolinic acid), warranting resistance gene monitoring. Most quinolones posed moderate-to-high ecological risks in water and sediment, while fish antibiotics presented low health risks. This study provides baseline data and supports One Health management in karst plateau aquaculture.
10.56201/ijccp.v10.no1.2024.pg116.132: Monitoring of contamination level in Lake Geriyo was coordinated by evaluating the concentrations of metals (Zn, Cu, Pb, & Cd) in sediment and fish samples of the lake in two seasons. The order of the concentrations of the metals in the sediment were Zn > Cu > Pb > Cd. The results showed that the metals exhibited lower values than sediment quality guideline (SQG). Thus, Lake Geriyo sediment can be categorized as unpolluted. Metal levels were within the set limit of TEL, PEL, ERL, and ERM which indicated that the sediment did not pose any danger to local fauna and flora. Zn and Cd were below the background values (Hakanson, 1980) nevertheless Pb and Cu exceeded. Metal Bioaccumulation were determined in the liver, gills and flesh from benthic and pelagic fish species obtained from the lake. The levels of the heavy metals differ remarkably amid fish species and organs. Flesh have the lowest concentration of all the metals. Liver was the choose organ for Zn, Cu and Pb accumulations. Cd nevertheless exhibited higher concentration in the gills. The metals bio concentration in fish flesh were acceptable by the international legislation limits for Cu, Zn, and Cd but however Pb go beyond in Clarias and Tilapia for wet season and Heterotis both seasons , consequently risky for human consumption and a danger to public health. These levels might be likely due to anthropogenic inputs as there is no industrial activity around the lake.
10.1007/s10499-026-02754-1: The green transformation of aquaculture involves not only adjustments in production inputs and pollution control practices but also changes in farm management. Using survey data from 311 freshwater aquaculture operators across 18 provinces in China, this study examines the relationship between green technology adoption and management performance, with particular attention to technology pathways and labor endowment. The results show that green technology adoption is positively and conditionally associated with management performance after controlling for operator characteristics, farm resources, and observable regional conditions. Process input and end-of-pipe green technologies show some differentiated association patterns across management performance dimensions: end-of-pipe technologies have relatively higher point estimates for innovation and development, business decision-making, and social contribution, whereas process input technologies show a relatively stronger association with risk control performance. Labor endowment also plays a differential moderating role. Higher labor endowment, reflected in labor quantity and labor quality, significantly strengthens the positive association between process input technologies and management performance, while no comparable labor complementarity is observed for end-of-pipe technologies. Further analyses indicate pathway differences across production modes and between digitally enabled and non-digital management performance. These findings suggest that the managerial value of green technologies depends not only on adoption itself but also on technology pathways and implementation capacity. Policy should therefore strengthen the fit between technology types and labor capacity through production training, stable labor allocation, and regional technical services to support sustained implementation and the green transformation of aquaculture.
10.1007/s10499-026-02759-w: Aquaculture intensification increases pressure on water quality, disease control, contaminant surveillance, and environmental safety. This scoping review maps nano-enabled remediation, monitoring, biosecurity, and ecotoxicological evidence alongside material recovery and practical validation. A Scopus search on 16 June 2026 identified 695 records; the evidence inventory comprises 57 unique English-language original research articles. Overlapping domains include remediation (14 articles), monitoring (15), biosecurity (17), antifouling (3) and ecotoxicology (17), with one natural-particle fate study. Reported settings comprise laboratory proof of concept (29), real-matrix bench testing (17), controlled stocked-system interventions (9), and a semi-field net test (1); the observational study is not assigned an intervention-maturity category. Six articles report reuse or regeneration, and one reports operational energy demand; these findings do not establish general economic viability. Performance depends on the tested material, matrix and endpoint, and high removal percentages require matched controls. Verification used full texts for 32 articles and indexed abstracts for 25. Unretained search-field settings, individual exclusion decisions, single-author screening, and incomplete source-level information constrain reproducibility and prevalence estimates. Laboratory sensitivity and short-term efficacy cannot establish environmental safety or commercial readiness. Translation requires verified residual exposure, chronic and early-life-stage testing, comparative life-cycle assessment and use-specific regulatory review.
10.1007/s10499-026-02756-z: Nigeria, Sub-Saharan Africa’s largest aquaculture producer, faces a substantial fish supply deficit despite rapid sectoral growth, with annual import expenditures at USD 0.6-1 billion. This study synthesizes evidence from a systematic review of 74 peer-reviewed studies from Web of Science, ScienceDirect, and Google Scholar, plus FAO and government reports, to analyze fisheries and aquaculture trends (2000-2024) using CAGR and OLS regression in R. The search yielded 2436 records; 74 met inclusion criteria after PRISMA-guided screening. Nigeria’s aquaculture expanded at a CAGR of 10.09%, surpassing China’s 4.18%. Regression shows a strong temporal trend (+13,044 tonnes/year, R2 = 0.773, p 300,000 t in 2014-2015, aligning with policy milestones (2000, 2008, 2013, 2016, 2024). However, the post-2015 plateau and multicollinearity (VIF=12.74) preclude definitive causal attribution to policies. Persistent constraints include high feed costs, input dependence, weak infrastructure, limited finance, and climate vulnerabilities. A targeted search for China comparative literature yielded no eligible studies for direct comparison; therefore, transferable lessons were drawn from policy documents, FAO reports, and peer-reviewed literature on Chinese aquaculture. Compared with China’s diversified systems, Nigeria remains heavily reliant on inland catfish and tilapia, with underdeveloped mariculture. Sustainable transformation requires investments in breeding, domestic feed production, digital technologies, responsible mariculture, and data-driven spatial planning. Adapting these transferable lessons from China offers a pathway to improve productivity, reduce import dependence, strengthen food security, and accelerate Nigeria’s blue economy development.
10.3390/jmse14222209: Marine aquaculture wastes move among water, particles, sediments, and biomass. Evaluating system-wide benefits requires accounting for elemental stocks, discharge loads, and the fate of harvested biomass. This narrative review examines species-specific evidence for sea purslane (Sesuvium portulacastrum) and the polychaete Perinereis aibuhitensis, alongside evidence from other halophytes, macroalgae, and polychaetes. Sea purslane assimilates dissolved nitrogen and produces harvestable biomass. The polychaete consumes deposited particles and ventilates burrows. These activities can affect assimilation, organic matter mineralization, and particle movement. In one experiment, sediment nitrogen and phosphorus fractions changed. Final nutrient concentrations in the overlying water exceeded control values, and polychaete biomass fell. One field study documented natural co-occurrence. It manipulated only the plant and used one pond per condition. We found no independently replicated experiment that manipulated both species and could estimate their interaction. Combined performance may depend on whether plant uptake keeps pace with sediment release. Near-bottom oxygen levels and the fate of resuspended particles may also matter. We propose three testable predictions, compare in-pond and separate configurations, and illustrate how to evaluate interaction and approximate additivity. Further validation should account for carbon, nitrogen, and phosphorus within a common boundary and assess discharge peaks, harvest safety, seasonal stability, and operating costs.
10.1186/s12711-026-01094-1: Abstract Background Pooled DNA genotyping has gained increasing attention in recent decades due to its potential to substantially reduce genotyping costs and its applications in identifying trait-associated DNA markers and estimating parental contributions to pooled offspring samples. However, accurately estimating parental contributions from pooled offspring genotype data remains a major challenge in selective breeding. This study presents a novel approach based on a differential evolution (DE) algorithm to estimate individual parental contributions to pooled offspring samples and assesses its accuracy across a wide range of simulated scenarios. Results Parental contributions were estimated with up to 100% accuracy by genotyping both in-silico pooled offspring and individual parents across various conditions, including different parental combinations (20 males × 20 females, 8 males × 8 females, and 5 males × 5 females), SNP densities (10-3981 markers), and pool sizes (2-1000 individuals), with or without knowledge of parental sex. In a simulated progeny testing scenario involving five males and five females that produced six full-sib families with 200 offspring each, 1200 offspring were ranked by body weight and grouped into 10 in-silico pools based on fixed weight intervals. Parental contributions to each pool were accurately estimated, enabling reliable calculation of genetic merit, defined as the mean body weight of all offspring from each parent. Genetic merit estimates obtained from pooled genotyping showed a perfect correlation with those derived from individual genotyping, with a root mean squared error of 1.4 g relative to a mean offspring weight of 674 g. Only 10 in-silico pools were genotyped instead of 1200 individuals, substantially reducing genotyping effort. The method was implemented as an open-source R package, DNApooling , and validation using empirical genotyping data demonstrated reliable estimation of parental contributions and genetic merit under real-world conditions. Conclusions The method provides a robust, scalable, and cost-effective approach for estimating parental genetic merit through progeny testing, analysing mating patterns in mass-spawning species, and assessing genetic diversity within pooled samples. Its practical utility is particularly relevant to genetic evaluation in aquaculture breeding programs.
10.1007/s11356-026-38430-3: Recirculating aquaculture systems (RAS) are intensively designed aquaculture models that rely on various water treatment technologies to maintain optimal water quality, ensuring the production of safe, healthy, and high-quality aquatic products. This work presented the design, construction, and evaluation of an automated land-based RAS platform, with a total volume of 3.6 m3, and a 130-day breeding trial using rainbow trout (Oncorhynchus mykiss). During the trial, water quality parameters in the RAS culture tanks were monitored. Results showed that average concentrations of ammonia nitrogen (NH4+-N), total nitrogen (TN), total phosphorus (TP), chemical oxygen demand (COD), and suspended solids (SS) were 0.41 mg/L, 4.12 mg/L, 0.22 mg/L, 13.59 mg/L, and 4.91 mg/L, respectively, with dissolved oxygen (DO) maintained at approximately 10 mg/L and pH fluctuating between 6.5 and 8.0. During the first 40 days, the system exhibited excellent water treatment performance, after which some water quality parameters showed a gradual increase, though these changes did not negatively impact the welfare of rainbow trout. Fillet nutritional composition and texture characteristics were compared between rainbow trout reared in the RAS and those sampled from an independently operated traditional flow-through pond system. These systems were not established as simultaneous or equivalent experimental treatments; therefore, any observed differences should be interpreted as descriptive differences between independent culture systems rather than causal effects of the rearing system. Results showed that no significant differences (p > 0.05) were observed in the crude protein and crude fat content between the two aquaculture methods; however, the RAS-cultured fish had significantly higher moisture content (p < 0.05) and lower ash content (p < 0.05) than those raised in flowing ponds. Texture profile analysis (TPA) revealed that the hardness, adhesiveness, springiness, and chewiness of the fillets from RAS-cultured fish were significantly lower (p < 0.05) relative to those from flowing ponds. Overall, the results demonstrated the operational feasibility of evaluated automated land-based RAS for rainbow trout culture under the tested conditions during the 130-day trial. The system maintained water quality within the observed ranges, and no statistically significant differences were detected in the measured nutritional composition of fillets from RAS-reared fish and fish obtained from an independently operated flow-through pond. The findings provided a basis for further controlled evaluations of RAS performance relative to conventional aquaculture systems, such as fish welfare, system stability, production efficiency, environmental impacts, and economic feasibility.
10.1007/s11356-026-38382-8: The southern coast of Lombok Island, Indonesia, is home to ecologically significant environments, including mangroves, seagrass meadows, and coral reefs, which coexist with traditional seaweed and shellfish farming systems. Even though they are vital, there is a lack of comprehensive data regarding baseline environmental conditions. This study investigated the concentrations, spatio-temporal distributions, and ecological risks of petroleum hydrocarbons (PHCs) in 28 surface sediment samples collected from Awang, Paremas, and Seriwe Bays during the 2022 and 2023 southeast and northwest monsoon seasons. Each sample contained trace amounts of PHCs, ranging from 1.1 to 11 mg/kg dry weight; nevertheless, concentrations remained well below established ecotoxicological thresholds, indicating a low risk to benthic organisms. Furthermore, although the differences were not statistically significant, PHC concentrations were generally higher during the southeast monsoon than during the northwest monsoon, except in Paremas Bay. This study provides baseline information on bulk petroleum hydrocarbon contamination in the coastal sediments of southern Lombok Island, which can serve as an environmental quality marker for aquaculture-dominated coastal systems. Although ecological risks were low under current conditions, continued monitoring is recommended to detect potential future changes associated with increasing coastal and maritime activities.
10.1007/s10499-026-02758-x: This study evaluated the effects of salinity on growth, biochemical composition, sensory quality, and extract radical scavenging activity of the edible sea grape Caulerpa racemosa under controlled culture conditions. Thalli were cultivated for 43 days at 24, 27, 30, 33, or 36 ppt in three independent aquaria per treatment; the aquarium was the experimental unit (n = 3), and within-aquarium measurements were treated as subsamples. Compared with the 30-ppt reference treatment, thalli cultured at 27 ppt had greater absolute growth (141.11 ± 8.13 vs. 72.91 ± 6.73 g) and specific growth rate (3.12 ± 0.10 vs. 2.09 ± 0.13% day⁻1; p < 0.05). The 27-ppt treatment also produced the highest numerical overall sensory-acceptance score (4.43 ± 0.78 on a five-point scale), whereas the 36-ppt treatment produced the lowest numerical score (2.00 ± 0.57). Conversely, extracts prepared from aquarium-derived biomass cultured at 36 ppt showed greater DPPH radical scavenging activity than extracts from the 27-ppt treatment (21.63 ± 0.04 vs. 10.00 ± 0.04%; p < 0.05) and the lowest IC50 (234.94 ± 0.85 ppm). Under the conditions tested, 27 ppt was most suitable for fresh-biomass production, whereas 33-36 ppt increased extract radical scavenging activity but reduced biomass production and sensory acceptance.
10.1007/s40152-026-00537-1: This paper writes against productivist tendencies in ‘fish for food’ policies, showing how they - in contrast to their aims - challenge people’s access to healthy and nutritious food. Using Indonesia as a case, it argues that a historically shaped modernist agenda, fuelled by economic interests and paternalistic ideas of wellbeing, informs a ‘high-value fish bias’: a governance focus on aquatic foods intended for export or middle-class consumption, and/or products that are discursively framed as an outcome of technological innovation. The paper unpacks the high-value fish bias, giving clues as to why fish for food are governed the way they are. Using empirical data from the East Indonesian island of Sumba, it also describes the local effects of this bias on local small fish value chains, giving specificity to often generalised claims about small fish as a policy blind spot. The paper argues that well-meant local fisheries- and food-related policies cannot shake off their discursive roots. As a result, relatively well-functioning small fish value chains are rendered anachronistic and pushed to the margin, due to which small fish for food are underutilized in (local) policies.
10.1007/s11160-026-10110-y: Elucidating the response mechanisms of non-native populations following their introduction to different geographical locations provides a foundation for the prevention and management of invasive species. Using whole-genome resequencing data from 190 Carassius auratus individuals (92 diploids and 98 triploids) across native and non-native ranges, this study compared the genetic responses of two non-native populations introduced to the Golmud River and Lhasa River on the Qinghai-Tibet Plateau (QTP). The results showed that the two geographically distant populations likely originated from admixture of multiple native sources. Compared with their source populations, the two non-native diploid populations each formed independent genetic clusters and exhibited comparable levels of heterozygosity loss (16.63 and 19.91%), increases in nucleotide diversity (9.0 and 8.1%), and proportions of individuals showing inbreeding signals (33.3 and 30.0%). In contrast, the two non-native triploid populations, which reproduce via gynogenesis, showed no independent genetic clustering and maintained genetic diversity comparable to their sources. However, selective sweep analyses revealed limited overlap between the two non-native populations within each ploidy level, with only sharing one outlier region, two candidate genes and two enriched GO terms in diploids, and one outlier region and one candidate gene in triploids. These findings revealed similar patterns of genetic diversity changes but divergent selection-associated genes and functional signatures between geographically distant non-native C. auratus populations on the QTP in both diploids and triploids.
10.1007/s11160-026-10109-5: Abstract Fish ecologists and managers have an interest in estimating the efficacy of freshwater habitat restoration, comparing among restoration options and basins. This often boils down to the question: How many fish can this habitat support? The number of fish a habitat can support, termed capacity, has increasingly become the currency for comparing habitats, restoration options, management policies, and is the backbone of many life cycle models. Underlying this focus is the assumption that capacity is determined from a factor or factors that limit abundance, and that improving these factors will promote an increase in population abundance. Researchers have a number of methods to estimate capacity, each with different benefits and drawbacks that vary by situation. Broadly, these methods fall into five categories: habitat expansion -applying high percentile observed fish densities to estimates of habitat area or volume; stock-recruit -fitting statistical relationships to time series of paired adult and progeny abundance; quantile regression -fitting high percentile regressions to local estimates of fish abundance and habitat features; microhabitat-scale models -scaling up statistical microhabitat suitability or individual bioenergetic requirements to reach and population levels; and food web models -estimating the energy flow from the primary and secondary production in a stream environment up through food webs to fish. The appropriate method in each situation will be determined by the available data, what management questions are being evaluated, the urgency and cost of producing estimates, and the temporal and spatial scales of estimates required.
10.1080/23308249.2026.2748998: Cephalopods are emerging as important model organisms in diverse scientific fields, including neuroscience, behavior, ecology, and aquaculture, driving increased interest in their care under artificial environments such as laboratories, aquaria, and aquaculture facilities. With this rise in captive use comes a critical need for systematic, science-based approaches to cephalopod health management. In controlled settings, health outcomes are often shaped by interactions in the form of complex infections involving multiple etiological agents, such as bacteria, viruses, fungi, protozoan and metazoan parasites aggravated by environmental and husbandry factors. These interactions directly influence host susceptibility, pathogen transmission, and disease severity, underscoring the importance of pathogen identification and traceability for sustaining captive populations. Beyond disease control, maintenance of cephalopod welfare requires vigilant monitoring of clinical signs, accurate diagnostics, and timely intervention. These practices also enhance research reproducibility and ethical stewardship. This review synthesizes recent advances in cephalopod health, covering key areas such as pathogen-associated diseases, immunology, nutrition, and biosecurity measures relevant to aquaculture and research settings. By integrating insights across these domains, the aim is to contribute to understanding the main stressors as well as to describing specific methodologies for assessing and managing the health and welfare of cephalopods, critical pillars to sustainable aquaculture and the reliability of the scientific studies in which they play a vital role.
10.1111/fme.70133: ABSTRACT Estimates of outmigration timing of Atlantic salmon smolt ( Salmo salar ) have become crucial inputs for predictive models that quantify effects of anthropogenic impacts. Recent reviews indicate that choice of method may impact estimates of migration timing, demanding an evaluation of the various monitoring tools in tandem. Here, we compared the migration behavior of smolts tagged with PIT tags or acoustic telemetry tags with smolts monitored with river transects of underwater video systems in two rivers in western Norway for three consecutive migration seasons (2019-2021). Despite discrepancies in the quantiles of migration, the methods often observed many of the same local peaks in migration distributions. Choice of tagging location had the largest observed effect on the migration timing of tagged individuals, with smolts from upstream of lakes arriving to the fjord 13.4 days later on average. Smolt length and morphological smolt index had negligible effects on migration timing.
10.1111/jfb.70741: Abstract Two new species of the ‘ Mesonoemacheilus guentheri ’ group are described from the Western Ghats Hotspot, based on morphological and multi-locus molecular data (mitochondrial cytochrome oxidase subunit 1, cytochrome b and nuclear Recombination-Activating Gene 1 sequences). Mesonoemacheilus mannanorum , new species, from a headwater stream of the Periyar River, is distinguished by a unique colour pattern of three series of whitish blotches on a brown background, and 8-9 branched pectoral-fin rays. Mesonoemacheilus sabariensis , new species, from a headwater stream of the Pamba River, is distinguished by a unique colour pattern comprising midlateral series of regularly or irregularly set and shaped whitish blotches with a wide brown margin, and pointed, elongated nasal flap-bars. Mesonoemacheilus now comprises 11 species, all of which are endemic to the rivers draining the Western Ghats Biodiversity Hotspot.
10.3390/fishes11110680: This study compared biofloc technology (BFT) and recirculating aquaculture systems (RAS) for juvenile Piaractus brachypomus and tested whether responses depended on commercial feed. Fish (174.71 ± 2.80 g) received feeds labeled 24% or 32% crude protein (CP) for 90 days in a 2 × 2 factorial (three tanks per treatment). Water quality, growth, and physiological responses were analyzed by tank. Final weight (444.96 ± 37.37 vs. 444.19 ± 50.07 g, p = 0.9758) and survival (95.55% vs. 91.11%, p = 0.4082) did not differ between BFT and RAS. During days 45-90, fish fed 24% CP feed had greater weight gain (126.06 vs. 91.96 g, p = 0.0385) and specific growth rate (0.69 vs. 0.54% day-1, p = 0.0496). Higher apparent feed intake with 24% CP feed (3.86 vs. 2.14 g fish-1 day-1) may have contributed to this gain. Hepatic thiobarbituric acid-reactive substances (TBARS, nmol g-1 tissue) were higher in BFT than RAS (5.80 ± 1.27 vs. 3.39 ± 0.82, p = 0.0010) and with 32% CP feed (5.23 ± 1.84 vs. 3.96 ± 1.18, p = 0.0295). Both systems supported juvenile grow-out. Among the feeds tested, the 24% CP product combined greater growth with lower hepatic TBARS.
10.3390/fishes11110681: The present study optimized and evaluated a lower-cost SYBR Green qPCR assay for White Spot Syndrome Virus (WSSV) detection and applied it to wild Penaeus monodon and Penaeus indicus from coastal Mozambique. Primer sets targeting VP19, VP24, VP26, and VP28 were compared with VP24_I showing favourable analytical performance (efficiency, 95.0%; R2 = 0.9988), good inter-run precision, no detectable cross-amplification with Infectious Hypodermal and Hematopoietic Necrosis Virus (IHHNV) or Decapod Iridescent Virus 1 (DIV1), and sequence confirmation of WSSV amplicons. Its dilution endpoint was comparable to that of the commercial MAXDETECT qPCR kit under the conditions tested, while reagent costs were reduced by 85% (USD 1.88 versus USD 12.55 per reaction). The assay was applied to 330 shrimp, and these individual-level results were combined with previously generated one-step PCR results from 300 shrimp from the same survey. After adjustment for geographic region, detection method, and site-level clustering, P. indicus had higher odds of WSSV detection than P. monodon, although this difference was not statistically significant (OR = 1.60; 95% CI: 0.86-2.98; p = 0.139). A similar trend was observed when the qPCR and one-step PCR datasets were analyzed separately. VP24_I represents a promising lower-cost candidate assay for WSSV surveillance, while the observed species association should be interpreted cautiously.
10.3354/meps15379: Single-group approaches provide limited understanding of plankton organisation and variation between contrasting sampling periods in the Gulf of California. We integrated phytoplankton chemotaxonomic markers with zooplankton group-level and species-level data for eight focal taxa to compare assemblage structure between January and July 2007 and assess covariation with environmental conditions. This approach revealed features not detected when phytoplankton and zooplankton groups were examined independently. HPLC/CHEMTAX indicated that Chlorophytes, diatoms, and Prymnesiophytes dominated the January phytoplankton assemblage, whereas diatoms predominated in July, with substantial contributions from cyanobacteria and other nanophytoplankton under strong stratification. Zooplankton comprised 28 taxonomic groups and 215 species within the focal taxa, with higher abundance in January. Biomass was concentrated among the copepods Rhincalanus nasutus , Pleuromamma gracilis and Labidocera acuta and the euphausiids Nyctiphanes simplex and Hansarsia difficilis , which together accounted for 64.59% of the mean biomass represented by the 42 species evaluated. Canonical ordination separated January and July assemblages, identifying temperature, mixed-layer depth and accessory pigments as structuring gradients, although the first two axes explained only 19.6% of the variability. Despite marked January and July turnover in species composition and size spectra, species richness was similar between cruises, indicating changes in community structure without corresponding changes in regional diversity. Integrating pigment-derived phytoplankton contributions with species-level estimates of zooplankton abundance and biomass provides a framework for examining variation in plankton assemblage structure under contrasting environmental conditions and identifies taxa relevant to improving trophic models and estimates of secondary production in this productive tropical-subtropical ecosystem.
10.3354/meps15378: Global climate change, particularly ocean warming, can affect coastal benthic ecosystems worldwide. However, in the marine realm, little is known about how thermal variability may pre-select populations for their resilience to future warming. We conducted a pan-seasonal mesocosm experiment on the foundation macrophyte, the eelgrass Zostera marina . We contrasted specimens originating from coastal sandy habitats with variable microclimates (thermal history), both under natural temperature conditions and under a 3 °C warming scenario reflecting near-future conditions, for a total of 1.5 years. Warming reduced the number of leaves and shoots, as well as relative eelgrass height, and resulted in a 22-day earlier summer peak in biomass compared with ambient conditions. Individuals from the more variable microclimate tended to grow more under both ambient and future temperature conditions, with greater shoot and leaf numbers, and relative height than those from the less variable microclimate. Such individuals also exhibited greater response plasticity under both the natural conditions and the warming scenario. This experimental study enhances our general understanding of the negative impacts of global warming on seagrass ecosystems and shows that not only cooler microclimates (i.e., thermal refugia) can benefit a species, but that variable microclimates may also facilitate individuals with greater thermal tolerances. These findings are central for a better understanding and implementation of protection measures for ecosystem engineers, such as seagrass, under future climate conditions.
10.3354/meps15382: Seabird mass mortality events (MMEs) are acute episodes of unusually high mortality with potentially serious demographic impacts, projected to become more frequent or exacerbated under ongoing climate change. This review synthesises knowledge on the causes of seabird MMEs, focusing on how outcomes of MMEs were measured, their likely drivers, and the extent to which these drivers have been tested empirically. Seabird MMEs appear to be driven by climatic and human factors, predominantly ocean warming and severe storms, with food limitation consistently emerging as the main proximate mechanism linking environmental drivers to mortality. Many drivers are ultimately anthropogenic, either arising directly from human activities or through climate change increasing their frequency and intensity. Temporal trends in reported drivers reflect shifting pressures on seabirds, with fewer recent studies on MMEs driven by oils spills and more implicating marine heatwaves and severe storms. Critically, we reveal a lack of quantitative studies that statistically model the effects of potential drivers of MMEs, fundamentally limiting our mechanistic understanding of these events. We highlight key knowledge gaps, including understudied drivers of MMEs, and emphasise the need for more rigorous analytical approaches and better baseline data collection, both demographic monitoring at breeding colonies and from standardised beached bird surveys. This requires coordinated monitoring at national and international scales, ideally integrating data beyond carcass counts (e.g. necropsies, or diagnostic sampling). Such approaches are essential for developing a mechanistic understanding of MME drivers, assessing population-level consequences, and improving our ability to detect and predict this increasing pressure to globally threatened seabirds.
10.3354/meps15381: Rapid changes in fish species composition, distribution, and abundance because of global warming are emerging as important issues in Fukushima Prefecture, Japan. Such changes influence the ongoing recovery of the prefecture's fisheries, as fishing effort has gradually recovered year by year since the Great East Japan Earthquake in 2011. We analyzed bottom trawl fishery data collected from the prefecture, focusing on the recent increase in yellow goosefish Lophius litulon catches, to clarify changes in its distribution and the mechanism underlying the recent increase in abundance. A generalized additive model revealed significant effects of bottom depth and bottom temperature on the occurrence probability and catch per unit effort of L. litulon . We used a depth-temperature (D-T) diagram to examine the differences in L. litulon distribution during the periods 2006-2008 and 2019-2021. The recent increase in catch reflected both the expansion of their distribution and increased biomass. The expansion of the distribution was related to bottom temperature warming, which likely enabled the species to inhabit deeper waters (180-220 m) throughout the year. The increase in biomass was driven by increases in both body weight and population density. The increase was also likely promoted by the temporary reduction in fishing pressure after the 2011 disaster; a decline in competing carnivorous fish in recent years may also be a contributing factor. Prey abundance and distribution also differed between two periods, and these changes may have contributed to the expansion of the distribution and increase in biomass of L. litulon .
10.3389/fmars.2026.2006926: With the rapid expansion of coastal nuclear and coal-fired power plants, the environmental impacts of thermal discharge on adjacent marine ecosystems have become a major concern in environmental science. Unlike previous reviews focusing on a single biological group or isolated water-quality parameter, this review integrates physicochemical and biological responses, microbial functional ecology and the microbial loop, identifies candidate indicator taxa and functional traits, compares nuclear and coal-fired effluents, and synthesizes effects on seawater physicochemical properties, plankton community structure, and microbial diversity and function. We distinguish two impact pathways, which are direct entrainment/impingement within once-through cooling systems and in situ warming experienced by organisms in the discharged plume. Chlorination by-products, nutrient enrichment and discharge-modified hydrodynamics are considered because they confound field-derived signals; thus many field patterns are mixed-stressor responses and cannot be attributed to warming alone. Nuclear and coal-fired plants differ in effluent composition, in that nuclear once-through discharges during normal operation are dominated by heated seawater and biocide residues. Many field-observed patterns represent mixed-stressor responses and cannot be attributed to warming alone. Thermal discharge reduces dissolved oxygen and pH, accelerates nutrient cycling, increases pollutant bioavailability, and alters phytoplankton, zooplankton, and microbial communities, thereby affecting food-web stability and biogeochemical processes. The review also discusses current controversies and knowledge gaps. The main contribution of this review is to integrate seawater chemistry, plankton dynamics and microbial functional ecology within a single attribution framework, to identify candidate indicator taxa and functional traits. This synthesis provides a scientific basis for environmental monitoring, ecological risk assessment and adaptive management of thermal discharge in coastal marine ecosystems.
10.3389/fmars.2026.1907711: Calcifying macroalgae play critical roles in coral reef ecosystem functioning and carbonate dynamics. However, the metabolic responses underpinning several of their ecological functions remain poorly characterized, particularly in the Red Sea. To evaluate how macroalgal metabolism varies over time under naturally fluctuating conditions, we conducted in situ metabolic assays in the spring and fall over three years (2022-2024) using two ecologically important calcifying reef taxa: the green macroalga Halimeda opuntia and the crustose coralline alga Lithophyllum sp. We quantified rates of light and dark calcification, net photosynthesis, and respiration under natural light and temperature regimes in shallow nearshore habitats of the central Red Sea. Halimeda opuntia metabolism varied significantly across time points in both lagoonal and reef habitats, whereas Lithophyllum sp. showed more stable light calcification rates, though its dark calcification, respiration, and net photosynthesis varied. This variation did not follow a consistent seasonal pattern. Notably, light calcification rates in H. opuntia were more than twice those of Lithophyllum sp., consistent with their roles as fast-growing sediment producers versus slower-growing reef framework stabilizers, respectively. These results provide essential species-resolved in situ metabolic baselines for dominant calcifying macroalgae in the central Red Sea and highlight how divergent macroalgal functional groups contribute to carbonate production and reef stability in a region that regularly experiences environmental extremes.
10.1002/jat.70513: ABSTRACT Incomplete combustion of plastic waste is an emerging pathway for forming thermally transformed microplastics (MPs), whose physicochemical identity and ecotoxicological potential in aquatic vertebrates remain poorly understood, as available evidence has focused primarily on the toxicity of their leachates and extracts. Accordingly, we conducted an exploratory investigation of biochemical and behavioral profiles in juvenile Astyanax sp. exposed to MPs derived from the burning of expanded polystyrene (B-EPSMPs) and polyethylene terephthalate (B-PETMPs), integrating physicochemical characterization, behavioral responses, and biochemical biomarkers. Fish were allocated to Control, B-EPSMP, and B-PETMP groups, with 20 individuals maintained in one exposure aquarium per group for 10 days at a nominal B-MP concentration of 4 mg/L. Although the materials exhibited high morphometric similarity, Raman and UV-Vis analyses revealed distinct structural and spectroscopic profiles in the combustion-derived materials. No mortality was observed, but the exposed groups exhibited distinct sublethal response profiles. In the gastrointestinal tract, fish from both B-MP groups showed higher ROS and MDA levels and higher CAT and MPO-like activities relative to the Control group. Encephalic biochemical differences were more pronounced in the B-EPSMP group, including higher nitrite and dopamine levels, enhanced AChE activity, and lower BChE activity. Basal locomotor behavior remained largely preserved, whereas behavioral paradigms involving novelty and social interaction revealed differences among the observed groups. Fish from the B-EPSMP group exhibited greater locomotor reactivity to novelty and reduced interspecific social responsiveness toward Hyphessobrycon eques , whereas fish from the B-PETMP group mainly showed differences in novel-object exploration. Multiblock integration identified distinct biochemical-behavioral patterns among the sampled groups, with greater separation associated with the B-EPSMP group. Because each treatment was represented by a single exposure aquarium, these findings describe exploratory, tank-confounded associations rather than independently replicated treatment effects. Overall, the study provides preliminary evidence of distinct biological response patterns in fish exposed to fire-derived MPs and establishes a basis for future investigations using independently replicated exposure units.
10.1111/jfb.70742: Abstract Seasonal variation in fish parasite burden reflects the interplay between parasite transmission, environmental conditions and host characteristics, yet the relative contributions of these factors remain incompletely understood in many wild freshwater fishes. We investigated gill ectoparasitism in the Maghrebian Bleak ( Tropidophoxinellus callensis ), a freshwater fish endemic to Algeria and Tunisia, examining variation in parasite burden in relation to season, host age, physiological condition and dietary breadth. Three ectoparasite taxa were identified, Gyrodactylus barbi , Trichodina sp. and Dactylogyrus fraternus , providing the first characterisation of the gill ectoparasite assemblage of this species. Parasite burden peaked in summer, and season remained significantly associated with ectoparasitism after accounting for host characteristics, although much of the explained variation was shared among predictors. Parasite abundance increased with host age in unadjusted analyses, but the relationship reversed after accounting for hepatic condition and other predictors. Furthermore, parasite burden exhibited a nonlinear relationship with hepatic condition, reaching its highest values at intermediate hepatosomatic indices.
