Evidence is strongest for larviculture and juvenile rearing under controlled experimental conditions, whereas fattening and broodstock production are promising but require further commercial-scale validation. Despite these advances, further research is needed to validate the available findings across larger and commercial-scale systems, improve the reporting of engineering and operational parameters, and expand knowledge on carrying capacity, techno-economic performance, energy demand, long-term fish welfare, and genetic management. Overall, RAS represents a technically viable and promising strategy for tambaqui production. However, commercial expansion requires system-specific validation integrating biological performance, fish welfare, engineering efficiency, energy use, and economic viability.
10.1111/faf.70120: ABSTRACT One of the most pressing challenges confronting the scientific community today is understanding the consequences of global change on ecological communities and mitigating their impacts. Cleaning mutualisms are essential to the health and stability of coral reef ecosystems, influencing individual fitness, parasite dynamics, and community composition. However, these interactions are increasingly threatened by anthropogenic pressures. This review describes the behavioural diversity and ecology of dedicated cleaners, ranging from cognitively sophisticated wrasses and efficient, low-conflict gobies to visually signalling shrimps. We then review how the intricate interactions between cleaners and clients respond to environmental change, including chronic stressors (e.g., acidification), extreme events (e.g., marine heatwaves), and direct anthropogenic disturbances (e.g., underwater noise). Mounting evidence demonstrates that such stressors can disrupt cleaner and client dynamics, diminishing interaction motivation and quality, and altering underlying neurobiological mechanisms. Despite recent advances, significant gaps remain in our understanding of the long-term resilience and recovery of cleaning mutualisms across ecological, behavioural, cognitive and physiological pathways. As ocean climate-related drivers of change intensify and increasingly co-occur, it becomes urgent to investigate whether cleaners can continue to fulfil their ecological roles, or if reefs will face a future with compromised mutualistic services.
10.1111/fog.70092: ABSTRACT In continental shelf ecosystems, physical-biological coupling between hydrographic structures and bottom-up pathways can generate spatial gradients in prey availability and quality that may influence the lipid quality of small pelagic fish. The income-breeding Engraulis anchoita on the Northern Argentinean Continental Shelf (NACS) fuels reproduction through active feeding and makes tissue lipid quality closely linked to local oceanographic and dietary conditions. This study integrated stomach content and tissue-specific fatty acid (FA) analyses sampled in three zones of the NACS spawning ground under contrasting oceanographic conditions: Río de la Plata salinity front (RP), Mar del Plata shelf waters (MDP), and El Rincón thermohaline front (ER) during austral spring. Diet composition differed markedly among sampling zones, shifting from small euryhaline copepods in RP to almost exclusive consumption of the lipid-rich Calanoides carinatus in ER. These variations were accompanied by differences in tissue FA profiles: ER individuals showed the highest total lipid content, saturated FA, and polyunsaturated FA concentrations, while MDP muscle was dominated by monounsaturated FA, matching Calanidae copepod markers. The omega-3/omega-6 was highest in ER ovaries, indicating selective omega-3 enrichment. The DHA/EPA ratio decreased from RP to ER, reflecting a progressive shift toward diatom-based food webs at lower temperatures, while the EPA/ARA ratio increased from RP to ER in both tissues, suggesting that individuals inhabiting the productive ER frontal system were in a more advanced reproductive condition. Together, these results reveal spatial patterns in tissue lipid quality closely coupled to the physical heterogeneity of the NACS shelf, suggesting a potential bottom-up trophic pathway that may have implications upon anchovy egg viability, larval survival and fish conditions.
10.65770/unbx5666: Fish scales are a well-established source of type I collagen and represent a potential route for recovering higher-value materials from fish-processing by-products. However, fish-scale collagen is often treated as a single material even though processing can generate products with markedly different structures, functions, and levels of supporting evidence. This narrative review examines fish-scale-derived collagen across the source-processing-material form-property-application-evidence continuum, with emphasis on cosmetic, nutricosmetic, and biomedical uses. Four material categories are distinguished: purified collagen, collagen peptides or hydrolysates, collagen-containing composites, and retained whole-scale collagenous matrices. Available studies show that fish species, scale composition, demineralization, extraction, hydrolysis, and material modification influence collagen recovery, structural integrity, thermal behavior, fibril formation, and downstream performance. For skin-related applications, several controlled human studies support defined orally administered fish-scale collagen peptide preparations for selected hydration, elasticity, and wrinkle-related outcomes, whereas controlled human evidence for topical application remains limited. Biomedical evidence is most developed for wound-healing materials, while bone, oral, periodontal, and corneal applications have progressed through cell-based and animal studies. Many favorable outcomes, however, involve composite materials or retained scale matrices and cannot be attributed to collagen alone. Translation remains constrained by raw-material heterogeneity, inconsistent extraction and yield reporting, incomplete product-specific safety assessment, sterilization and manufacturing requirements, limited human biomedical evidence, and insufficient environmental and economic evaluation of scale-up. Fish-scale collagen should therefore be considered a family of application-dependent materials rather than a uniform alternative collagen source.
10.1007/s11457-026-09553-y: This research seeks to uncover spatial and temporal trends relating to the food contents of amphorae from Roman Gades, the modern Bay of Cádiz, from the second century BC through the second century AD. Earlier scholarship on amphorae from southern Spain has primarily focused on single sites and highlighted olive oil production. This research, however, uses a Microsoft Access database and Google Earth Pro to catalogue amphorae from 11 previous studies, produce detailed maps of their find spots, and analyze their dates, locations, and contexts to study the production and exports of the greater port area. Contextualizing individual amphora-find locations within the wider area, Roman economy, and ancient shorelines demonstrated evidence of a steady rise in the relative importance of fish products and of Puerto Real, one of the Bay’s neighborhoods, especially after the transition from the Roman Republic to the Roman Empire. Over time, the port increasingly specialized in fish products and separated the production of different commodities. Focusing on under-studied trade goods produced in the harbor’s immediate vicinity helps to fill a research gap created by the emphasis on olive oil and contributes to a more well-rounded understanding of Roman production and maritime trade in this area. More broadly, this study seeks to illustrate the potential for these types of amphora databases and maps to provide a more contextualized view of food production and transport, aid reconstructions of ancient food networks, and expand archaeology’s understanding of maritime trade.
10.1080/24705357.2026.2761577: Determining ecologically suitable water levels is fundamental to fish habitat conservation and ecologic regulation. The optimal water level thresholds for lacustrine fish in East Dongting Lake and their underlying driving factors remain poorly understood. This study focused on lacustrine fish and constructed a habitat suitability model based on depth and velocity suitability curves, then quantitatively analyzed the response of weighted usable area (WUA) to water level fluctuations. Results indicate that WUA exhibits a distinct bimodal variation with changing water level, and two optimal ecological water level ranges of 22.74-23.90 and 25.18-26.98 m are therefore recommended. Further analysis revealed that the bimodal character originates from the multi-stage sandbars topography across East Dongting Lake, where water depth acted as the key hydraulic factor limiting spawning habitat suitability. Shallow, slow-flowing habitats distributed over sandbar zones such as the northwest branching shoals, Wuguangzhou, Lu Lake, and Chaixiazhou are essential for maintaining high-quality spawning grounds of lacustrine fish. Relevant management strategies should be proposed to prioritize conservation efforts in these shoal habitats to protect the fishery resources in East Dongting Lake.
10.1007/s10529-026-03800-x: This study aims to address the urgent need for antibiotic alternatives in aquaculture by isolating and characterizing novel bacteriophages. The primary objective was to evaluate the efficacy of two newly identified phages, ST22 and ST231, in targeting the sulfate-reducing bacterium Desulfovibrio vulgaris and assessing their potential for environmental remediation and disease management. The researchers utilized Transmission Electron Microscopy (TEM) to determine morphological features and employed genomic sequencing to analyze the genetic profiles of both phages. Lytic activity was validated through lysis assays, while microcosm experiments were conducted to monitor the reduction of environmental pollutants, specifically H2S and NH3. Finally, in vivo trials with shrimp were performed to confirm biological safety and survival efficacy. Morphological analysis classified ST22 (genus Bruynoghevirus) and ST231 (genus Murrayvirus) as having double-stranded DNA genomes of 45,779 bp and 41,280 bp, respectively. Both phages exhibited potent lytic activity, significantly reducing D. vulgaris density and altering colony morphology. In microcosm settings, phage application effectively mitigated H2S and NH3 levels. Furthermore, a substantial increase in shrimp survival rates underscored their efficacy as safe biocontrol agents. Phages ST22 and ST231 represent promising candidates for sustainable disease management and environmental remediation in aquaculture. These findings validate the potential of phage therapy as a robust, eco-friendly alternative to traditional chemical treatments for bacterial pathogens.
10.1038/s41437-026-00900-2: Family-based aquaculture breeding programs deliver rapid genetic gains but inevitably accelerate inbreeding. Advanced mating strategies aim to manage this trade-off, yet the optimal emphasis on the rate of genetic gain ( $$\Delta G$$ ) versus the rate of inbreeding ( $$\Delta F$$ ) depends on the breeding horizon (the timeframe of consecutive breeding cycles), which existing strategies do not explicitly account for. We developed a look-ahead genomic mating strategy (LAGM) that holistically optimizes the gain-inbreeding balance across the entire breeding horizon. LAGM was benchmarked against genomic optimal contribution selection (GOCS), truncation selection (TC), and random selection in a simulated breeding program across varying horizons. Both LAGM and GOCS outperformed TC by 72.8-332.3% in conversion efficiency ( $$\Delta G/\Delta F$$ ), with the largest improvements observed at longer horizons, where severe inbreeding constrained the selection response. Constant constraints favoring inbreeding control tended to achieve higher conversion efficiency across horizons but substantially sacrificed $$\Delta G$$ . In contrast, across horizons, LAGM with a dynamic look-ahead window achieved conversion efficiency comparable to, or only slightly below (9.2-15.4%), that of the highest-efficiency GOCS (65°), while delivering 15.4-69% greater $$\Delta G$$ . Furthermore, in early breeding stages, by targeting solutions with high marginal returns and exploiting locus-resolved complementarity, LAGM achieved 4.4-58.6% higher $$\Delta G$$ than all GOCS strategies at matched inbreeding levels, even under fixed look-ahead windows-each of which approximately corresponded to a specific GOCS trade-off angle once the population structure had stabilized. Overall, LAGM offers a generalized look-ahead framework, grounded in classical quantitative genetics and modern mate selection, for balancing genetic gain and inbreeding.
10.1038/s41598-026-73653-x: Quorum sensing-driven biofilm formation is a key contributor to the persistence and multidrug resistance (MDR) of pathogenic bacteria, presenting a major challenge in combating infectious diseases. Probiotic quorum-quenching (QQ) bacteria represent a promising alternative to conventional antibiotics by suppressing quorum sensing-dependent virulence in MDR pathogens and simultaneously enhancing fish growth, immunity, and overall health. In this study, the probiotic and QQ attributes of Chromohalobacter sp. D23 were comprehensively investigated. The strain exhibited robust tolerance to gastrointestinal stress conditions, surviving bile salt (1.2%), phenol (0.75%), and acidic environments (pH 2.0-4.0). Additionally, it displayed pronounced antioxidant activity (> 69%), high auto-aggregation (72.0 ± 2.42%), and co-aggregation (> 73%) with fish pathogens, suggesting a high potential for gut colonization and pathogen exclusion. Genome mining also revealed presence of putative proteins involved in resistance to bile, phenol, acid, osmotic pressure along with adhesion and aggregation facilitating host gut colonization. Virtual screening of strain D23 also enabled to predict potential enzymes/proteins for biosynthesis of vitamins and amino acids. In spite of presence of very few antibiotic resistance genes, overall genome-wide analysis of the draft genome of strain D23 detected no putative virulence genes, plasmid, or transposable element-associated genes, suggesting a favorable safety profile. Whole-cell assay showed complete breakdown of synthetic N-acyl homoserine lactones (N-AHLs) as revealed by biosensor-based assay. Strain D23 also degraded natural N-AHLs of Aeromonas hydrophila within 12 h. Co-culture experiment revealed potent anti-biofilm activity against A. hydrophila ( p ≤ 0.0001). Genome mining identified putative metallo-beta lactamase enzyme (lactonase_D23) having conserved ‘ 66 HXHXDH 71 ’ motif. Molecular docking revealed moderate binding affinities of lactonase_D23 towards both C4-Homoserine lactone (C4-HSL) and C6-HSL, however, molecular dynamics simulations demonstrated that the C4-HSL-lactonase_D23 complex exhibited greater conformational stability, indicating highly persistent protein-ligand interaction. Later, in silico mutant enzymes exhibited higher binding affinity than wild-type lactonase_D23 to C4-HSL. This pioneer, integrated study suggests potentiality of strain D23 as safe, beneficial, autochthonous QQ probiotic candidate in aquaculture to improve overall fish health.
10.1186/s12864-026-13562-5: Trypanosoma carassii infects a range of fish species and is responsible for severe disease outbreaks in aquacultures. It is considered the causative agents of trypanosomiasis outbreaks in largemouth bass, tilapia, and blood parrot cichlids in South China. Here, we present a chromosome-level genome assembly of this trypanosome, combining long-read sequencing and Hi-C scaffolding to resolve 31 chromosomes of 42 Mb with a high level of completeness and structural continuity. Phylogenetic analysis identified T. carassii as a basal-branching lineage forming a sister clade to trypanosomes infecting terrestrial vertebrates. Hi-C mapping revealed 105 chromatin-folding domains, providing the first 3D genome architecture of T. carassii . Unlike the highly dynamic, antigenic subtelomeric regions of Trypanosoma brucei and T. cruzi , those of T. carassii have a remarkably stable architecture characterized by two variants of ∼3.9 kb conserved sequences, reflecting a static host-interaction strategy. The genome of T. carassii is gene-rich, carrying 11,366 protein-coding genes. A comprehensive prediction analysis identified 165 excretory/secretory proteins, 250 putative surface proteins, and 13 cytostome-cytopharynx complex components. These included GP63, cysteine peptidases, trans -sialidases, and a large number of T. carassii -specific hypothetical proteins, representing promising candidates for vaccine development, diagnostics, and chemotherapeutic targeting. As a basal-branching lineage of the genus Trypanosoma , this genomic resource provides a foundation for understanding piscine trypanosomiasis and informs about the evolution and fitness implications of retention of the cytostome-cytopharynx complex.
10.1111/jfb.70726: Abstract The Marbled Stargazer, Uranoscopus marmoratus, is redescribed based on five individuals collected from the southeastern Arabian Sea, India. This species is a poorly known fish which is distributed predominantly in the eastern Indian Ocean and belongs to the Uranoscopus japonicus species group. U. marmoratus is defined as having one pair of basipterygial processes; a simple posterior nostril and tubular anterior nostril; one internal supracleithral spine and one sharp humeral spine; 4-5 preopercular and 1 subopercular spines; no scales on the predorsal region; no supraocular cirri; 52-62 transverse rows of scales on the sides of the body; well-developed occipital lobes; occipital commissure with four posterior branches; head length 2.6-3.6 times in standard length; head large; head width 3.0-3.3 times in standard length; body depth 4.2-4.7 times in standard length; head depth 1.1-1.4 times its width; dorsal surface marbled, with pale spots on a brown background. Otolith morphological description of the fish was also provided for the first time. COI sequence generated herein represents the first genetic record of the species in GenBank, and Maximum-Likelihood (K2P) analysis recovered this species as a distinct lineage, offering additional support for its taxonomic distinctiveness.
10.1007/s12562-026-02054-w: The shorthead anchovy Encrasicholina heteroloba is a small pelagic species of significant economic and nutritional importance in Tanzania. However, reliable stock assessment remains challenging because of limited data. This study evaluated the status of E. heteroloba in Tanzania’s coastal waters. A total of 32,324 specimens were sampled between July 2023 and December 2024. Length-frequency data were cleaned, bootstrapped, and analyzed using electronic length-frequency analysis to estimate von Bertalanffy growth parameters and mortality coefficients, and stock biomass and abundance were estimated through virtual population analysis. Asymptotic length ( $${L}_{\infty }$$ ) was 8.42 cm total length, growth coefficient ( $$K$$ ) was 2.08 $${\text{y}\text{e}\text{a}\text{r}}^{-1}$$ , growth performance index ( $${\varnothing }{\prime}$$ ) was 2.19, current fishing mortality ( $${F}_{\text{c}\text{u}\text{r}\text{r}}$$ ) was 0.85 $${\text{y}\text{e}\text{a}\text{r}}^{-1}$$ , exploitation rate ( $${E}_{\text{c}\text{u}\text{r}\text{r}}$$ ) was 0.40, and length at first capture ( $${L}_{\text{c}\text{u}\text{r}\text{r}}$$ ) was 6.11 cm total length. Natural mortality ( $$M$$ ) was 1.25 $${\text{y}\text{e}\text{a}\text{r}}^{-1}$$ , and total mortality ( $$Z$$ ) was 2.10 $${\text{y}\text{e}\text{a}\text{r}}^{-1}$$ . Overall biomass and stock abundance were 70,725 metric tons and 4.37 × 1010 individuals, respectively. Biological reference points were $${F}_{0.1}$$ = 1.57 $${\text{y}\text{e}\text{a}\text{r}}^{-1}$$ , $${F}_{0.5}$$ = 1.06 $${\text{y}\text{e}\text{a}\text{r}}^{-1}$$ , and $${F}_{\text{m}\text{a}\text{x}}$$ = 3.34 $${\text{y}\text{e}\text{a}\text{r}}^{-1}$$ . The stock in this region is likely underexploited. These results support evidence-based fisheries management and contribute to sustainable utilization.
10.1108/jadee-03-2025-0120: Purpose This study examines stakeholder perceptions of the importance of 21 sustainability themes across 4 Vietnamese shrimp farming systems. It also assesses associations between respondent characteristics and a separate ranking of perceived system sustainability. Design/methodology/approach Using the Sustainability Assessment of Food and Agriculture Systems (SAFA) Guidelines, 94 respondents each rated 21 themes across 4 systems, yielding 84 ordinal ratings per respondent. Questionnaires were administered in person to 56 respondents and completed online by 38. Theme-specific Friedman tests accounted for repeated observations, with Benjamini-Hochberg adjustment across 21 omnibus tests and, separately, 126 paired Wilcoxon comparisons. Cumulative-link mixed models provided an ordinal sensitivity analysis. Ridge-penalised multinomial regression examined the separate ranking outcome. Findings Differences across systems were supported for 18 of the 21 themes after adjustment for multiple testing. Corporate ethics, rule of law and biodiversity showed no supported omnibus differences. Super-intensive farming generally received the highest ratings for the importance of addressing sustainability issues. These ratings concern perceived priorities rather than measured performance. First-rank counts were 27, 7, 5 and 55 for super-intensive, intensive, semi-intensive and extensive/improved extensive/integrated systems, respectively. Age and self-reported knowledge were positively associated with selected ranking contrasts. These associations provide secondary evidence because two outcome categories were small. Research limitations/implications The purposive sample comprised 52 consumers, 36 business stakeholders and 6 experts. Its size and composition limit generalisation. Survey mode, fixed question order, unmeasured familiarity with production systems, concentrated high ratings and seven uniform response profiles may have influenced the findings. Sparse ranking categories limit prediction and practical interpretation of the multinomial model. Social implications Promoting sustainable shrimp farming systems also aligns with MARD’s approved “Sustainable aquaculture development plan in the Mekong Delta to 2030” (Decision No. 3550/QÐ-BNN-TCTS, August 2021), which aims to develop regional aquaculture sustainably. Originality/value The study applies the SAFA themes to comparisons of shrimp farming systems rated by the same stakeholders. By distinguishing the importance assigned to individual issues from an overall sustainability ranking, it explains how these two forms of judgement contribute different evidence to sustainability assessment.
10.3389/fmars.2026.2012048: Improving the carbon emission efficiency of marine capture fisheries is important for the sustainable development of fisheries under climate change. Using 66 major marine fishing countries over 1995-2017 as the sample, we divided the countries into three groups by fishing structure: high-input predatory fish-dominated, mixed, and small pelagic and other finfish-dominated. We measured carbon emission efficiency with a slacks-based measure (SBM) model with undesirable outputs and a metafrontier approach, and decomposed the potential emission reduction into managerial inefficiency and the technology gap. The results show the following. (1) Carbon emission efficiency was generally low, with a mean metafrontier efficiency of 0.331, and the differences between groups were closely related to catch value. (2) The technology gap was concentrated in the high-input predatory fish-dominated group and the small pelagic and other finfish-dominated group, and its causes differed across countries: in Vietnam, Thailand and Malaysia it was associated with fuel-intensive fishing operations, whereas in Peru and Chile it stemmed from the low value of the catch. (3) The mean annual potential carbon emission reduction of the sample countries was 85.4 Mt CO 2 -eq, about 53% of their total emissions, and was concentrated in countries such as Indonesia, India and Vietnam. (4) Managerial inefficiency was the main source of the reduction potential, accounting for 69%. In the mixed group, almost all of the potential came from managerial inefficiency; in the high-input predatory fish-dominated group, the technology gap dominated; and in the small pelagic and other finfish-dominated group, both sources contributed. Countries should therefore choose different pathways according to the source of their reduction potential. For most countries, catching up with the best practice of similar countries could release most of the potential with existing technology, especially in countries where the potential is concentrated, such as Indonesia and India. Countries whose technology gap is accompanied by high fuel intensity should focus on promoting energy-saving fishing gear and propulsion technology, while countries that mainly land low-value catch should increase the value of their catch.
10.1139/cjfas-2026-0190: There has been considerable recent interest in applying portfolio theory to manage multispecies fisheries, analogous to the management of financial portfolios. It is demonstrated here that this analogy breaks down for several reasons. First, fisheries portfolio theory focuses on mitigating the uncertainty in short-term landings and revenue, which, unlike financial stocks, can usually be predicted to good precision. Meanwhile, it neglects the much more important risks of overfishing and stock depletion. Additionally, while portfolio theory reduces the volatility of the combined portfolio, it may call for highly varying landings of individual fisheries, which can cause considerable hardship. Finally, the control parameters (portfolio weightings) and random variables fundamental to portfolio theory have not been properly defined in the fisheries context, nor do such appropriate definitions seem to exist. Fisheries portfolio theory fails because it focuses on the wrong risk and it calculates this risk incorrectly. Additionally, it is based on an incorrect assumption that the actions of managers do not affect future fishery productivity.
10.3390/hydrobiology5040045: The increasing global demand for fish and fishery products has established fisheries and aquaculture as essential sectors for food security and economic development. However, the intensification of these activities may also increase exposure to biological hazards inherent to aquatic environments and production systems, raising concerns for food safety, occupational and public health. Among these hazards, pathogenic bacteria, associated with water, sediments, and aquatic organisms, are of particular concern. Environmental changes, including climate change and the expansion of aquaculture practices, may further promote the emergence and dissemination of these microorganisms. Within this context, Legionella spp. is recognized as a relevant waterborne pathogen due to its widespread occurrence in natural and artificial aquatic environments and its capacity to cause human disease, primarily through the inhalation of contaminated aerosols. Consequently, workers involved in aquaculture, fisheries, and fish-processing industries may represent a population potentially exposed to this microorganism. Although legionellosis is not considered a zoonosis associated with fish consumption, and no occupational cases linked to these sectors have been reported to date, the persistence of Legionella in aquatic environments highlights a plausible but insufficiently investigated exposure pathway. This narrative review synthesizes information from SciELO, Scopus, Google Scholar, and other relevant bibliographic sources on the biological and clinical characteristics of Legionella, available detection methods and prevention strategies. The aim is to examine the potential for occupational exposure within fish production systems and discuss its possible implications for worker health. By identifying hypothetical exposure scenarios and current knowledge gaps, this review seeks to support future research and contribute to the prevention and assessment of biological risks in the fisheries and aquaculture sectors, without assuming the existence of a demonstrated occupational hazard or an emerging public health problem.
10.3390/ani16223589: Mountain river networks are composed of a mainstem and multiple tributaries, where complex hydrological processes and habitat heterogeneity provide diverse niches for fishes. Previous studies have documented the fish fauna and diversity in the Dadu River basin, providing baseline information for regional fish conservation. However, differences in fish assemblage composition among river units and their relationships with water environmental conditions require further examination through continuous multi-year surveys. From 2023 to 2025, a three-year continuous survey of fish assemblages was conducted across 28 sampling sites in the mainstem and nine major tributaries of the Shimian reach in the middle Dadu River (upper Yangtze River basin), along with concurrent monitoring of water physicochemical parameters. A total of 54 fish species belonging to three orders and seven families were recorded, with Cyprinidae and Cobitidae being the dominant groups. Fish assemblages were mainly composed of rheophilic, benthic, and demersal-spawning species, reflecting the typical ecological characteristics of fishes in high-gradient river habitats. Fish assemblage composition remained generally stable over the three survey years but showed marked spatial differences among river units. NMDS ordination and PERMANOVA indicated that functional habitat types (mainstem, upstream and confluences) explained a significant proportion of variation in assemblage structure, whereas the effect of survey year was not significant, indicating that spatial differences across habitat types were more pronounced than interannual variation. Distinct fish assemblages were formed among the mainstem, confluences, and individual tributaries, with several natural tributaries supporting higher proportions of endemic and cold-water fishes. Water environmental analyses revealed evident hydrochemical gradients among river units, and redundancy analysis (RDA) showed that water temperature, dissolved oxygen, and nutrient concentrations were closely associated with the spatial distribution of fish assemblages. Building on previous surveys of fish fauna in the Dadu River basin, this study adds three years of fish assemblage data at the mainstem-tributary river network scale and further describes spatial differences in assemblage composition among river units and their relationships with water environmental conditions. These results provide baseline information for understanding the spatial distribution of fish assemblages in alpine canyon rivers and for fish biodiversity conservation and tributary habitat management in the Dadu River basin.
10.1038/s41598-026-79729-y: Toxic elements can be accumulated into human body through fish chain as fish is exposed to metals through water, sediment and contaminated feeds. Therefore, the study was conducted to determine the heavy metal content of fish species and their feeds, as well as the potential health risks associated with them. Forty-five fish samples were collected from fifteen fish farms whereas thirty feed samples were collected from three upalizas of Mymensingh district during June to August 2022. The collected samples were digested with an acid mixture, and concentrations of twelve heavy metals were measured by ICP-MS. Fe predominates over the other metals in almost all samples. All three fish species contained the higher concentration of Fe, Ni, Zn and Cr. The concentrations of Fe, Ni, Zn and Cr are 20.84, 9.4, 6.60, 1.86 mgkg -1 for Pangasius, 25.8, 13.82, 8.91 and 2.00 mgkg -1 for Rui and 27.58, 7.08, 7.92 and 2.09 mgkg -1 for Tilapia, respectively. The WHO/EU standard limits for Cr, Mn, Ni, and Pb were exceeded in feed samples from farmers and in commercial feeds. Tilapia fish species had a strong propensity to acquire As, Co, and Ni from farmer-supplied feeds and As and Se from commercial feeds as BFAF value was higher than 1. The degree of contamination across all species can be characterized as follows: Tilapia > Rui > Pangasius. The mean estimated daily intake of the heavy metals was lower than the recommended daily allowance. Except for Fe, the THQ values for fish species were less than 1. Conversely, HI in all species was higher than the allowable threshold of 1. Carcinogenic risks from Ni and Pb consumption were present in all fish species. Antibiotics, especially oxytetracycline and tetracycline, were detected in various fish samples. The results suggest that the authority should take appropriate precautions to ensure feed quality and prevent significant heavy metal exposure from farmed fish.
10.3389/fmars.2026.1941096: Introduction Post-harvest fish loss is an important concern in Somalia's fisheries sector, with potential implications for fish quality, livelihoods, food security, and market development. Methods A descriptive, cross-sectional mixed-methods survey was conducted with 94 fisheries stakeholders across four Somali fish markets: Mogadishu, Kismayo, Bosaso, and Berbera. Data were collected through questionnaires, semi-structured interviews, and field observations and analysed using descriptive statistics and thematic analysis. Results Respondents identified inadequate fish handling, limited preservation and cold-storage facilities, unreliable electricity, transportation difficulties, and weaknesses in quality control and enforcement as major challenges. They reported perceived effects on fish availability, market prices, consumer access, food security, income, business activities, and fish quality. Recommended mitigation measures included improved fish handling, timely icing, better cold-chain facilities, improved preservation technologies, training, stronger quality-control systems, and collaboration among stakeholders. Discussion The findings provide insights into stakeholder-perceived post-harvest challenges and potential mitigation strategies in Somali fisheries. However, the study did not directly measure physical fish losses, discarded quantities, or their economic value. The findings therefore represent stakeholder perceptions and reported experiences rather than measured losses or established causal effects.
10.1139/cjfas-2026-0083: Greenland halibut (Reinhardtius hippoglossoides) and witch flounder (Glyptocephalus cynoglossus) are fished in deep water (>500m) along the continental slope of eastern Canada, which is an area of oil and gas exploration. Virtually no information is available regarding the effects of noise on these species at this depth, however, some commercial fish harvesters believe that noise from seismic surveying displaces fish and causes reductions in catch. We used acoustic telemetry and a control-impact study design to test this hypothesis by measuring fish movement in response to weeks of industrial seismic survey noise. There were no large-scale displacements of tracked fish from the impacted area for either species. Greenland halibut movement, while in the study arrays, did not change with proximity to seismic activity. Witch flounder remained in the impact array longer than the control array and were more likely to remain stationary with increased seismic noise. Noise impact in this study revealed different behavioral effects, even within these two flatfish species, and suggests that effects on commercial catch rates will vary according to species.
10.3390/molecules31224099: The overuse of antibiotics in aquaculture has accelerated the emergence of drug-resistant bacteria and biofilm-associated infections, creating an urgent need for alternative antimicrobial agents. Zinc oxide nanoparticles (ZnO NPs) are promising candidates owing to their low toxicity and cost, but their intrinsic antibacterial activity is often inadequate. Herein, we report a series of copper-doped ZnO nanoparticles (Cu@ZnO NPs, 1-5 mol% Cu) synthesized via a facile solvothermal method. The 2% Cu@ZnO NPs, comprising well-dispersed spherical particles of approximately 200 nm with a highly positive surface charge (+20 mV), exhibited the strongest antibacterial activity, outperforming pristine and commercial ZnO, with a minimum inhibitory concentration (MIC) of 0.2 mg/mL and a minimum bactericidal concentration (MBC) of 1.0 mg/mL against both Escherichia coli and Staphylococcus aureus. Mechanistic studies suggested that bactericidal activity may arise from the synergy of electrostatic adsorption, membrane disruption accompanied by protein leakage, intracellular reactive oxygen species (ROS) generation, and sustained metal-ion release. The nanoparticles were shown to reduce biofilm formation by 80.96% and maintained 88.4% viability of L929 fibroblasts at 20 μg/mL, indicating good biocompatibility. In a zebrafish larvae infection model, 5.0 μg/mL of 2% Cu@ZnO increased the 72 h survival rate from 6.25% (Vibrio-challenged) to 65.0%. Cu@ZnO-loaded filter materials further demonstrated practical applicability for aquaculture water pretreatment. This work elucidates the structure-activity relationship of Cu-doped ZnO nanomaterials and offers a low-toxicity, filter-integrable alternative to antibiotics for sustainable aquaculture.
10.9734/ajfar/2026/v28i111188: Coastal water quality is affected by multiple pollution sources, and their contributions to receiving waters depend on pollutant generation, transport pathways, and delivery processes. This study developed a source-based assessment of pollutant loads in the Xuan Dai Bay area, Vietnam, using 2025 activity data for aquaculture, domestic wastewater, crop cultivation, livestock farming, and stormwater runoff. Annual loads of biochemical oxygen demand (BOD), chemical oxygen demand (COD), total nitrogen (TN) and total phosphorus (TP) were estimated using source-specific emission factors and delivery coefficients. Total generated loads were estimated at 3,945.54 tonnes per year (t yr⁻¹) of BOD, 10,711.35 t yr⁻¹ of COD, 1,447.66 t yr⁻¹ of TN, and 318.95 t yr⁻¹ of TP. After the proposed delivery factors were applied, the estimated loads reaching the bay were 1,577.79, 3,955.95, 716.31 and 193.73 t yr⁻¹, respectively. Aquaculture was the dominant source of estimated delivered TN and TP, contributing 70.44% and 82.12%, respectively, while livestock farming was an important source of organic loads. The results demonstrate that source rankings can change when pollutant transport is considered alongside generation. Although the estimates provide an initial basis for prioritizing pollution-control measures, uncertainty in emission factors and delivery coefficients limits their precision. Local validation and hydrodynamic assessment are needed to refine source attribution and support future assessments of environmental carrying capacity.
10.1007/s11802-026-6741-6: The rapid expansion of cage aquaculture raises concerns about its impacts on coastal sediment ecosystems. This study investigated the long-term effect of cage fish farming on the spatiotemporal dynamics, assembly mechanisms, and co-occurrence networks of benthic bacterial communities in Daya Bay, South China Sea. Surface sediments were collected every two months from a cage farm and non-aquaculture sites, and bacterial communities were characterized via high-throughput 16S rRNA gene sequencing. Alpha diversity did not differ significantly between farm and control sites, whereas community composition diverged markedly and was likely driven by aquaculture-derived nutrient enrichment. Sediment from the fish farm exhibited a reduced dominance of core phyla (Pseudomonadota, Acidobacteriota, Planctomycetota) and an enrichment of opportunistic heterotrophs (Bacteroidota, Bacillota, Spirochaetota) that was positively correlated with sedimentary biogenic elements, including total organic carbon (TOC), total nitrogen (TN), and total phosphorus (TP). Co-occurrence network analysis revealed that the farm-associated network had greater complexity, modularity, and stability and a significantly greater proportion of negative correlations, indicating intensified interspecific competition. Null model analysis of assembly processes showed that while deterministic homogeneous selection dominated both the farm and control sites, its contribution was substantially lower at the farm site (59.38% vs. 71.37%). Concurrently, the stochastic process of dispersal limitation increased from 1.73% to 14.20%. These findings demonstrate that cage fish farming restructures benthic bacterial communities and fundamentally alters their assembly rules by enhancing ecological barriers that restrict microbial dispersal. This mechanistic shift provides new insights into aquaculture’s ecological footprint in coastal ecosystems.
10.1007/s11802-026-6760-3: This study investigated the effects of fish species, simmering time, and deodorization methods on the nutrition and flavor of fish steak soups prepared from New Zealand hoki, Pacific cod, and Atlantic mackerel. Nutritional composition was analyzed via basic component measurement, while flavor profiles were evaluated using electronic tongue, free amino acid (FAA) assay, and GC-IMS coupled with ROAV analysis. Prolonged simmering raised protein, fat, and ash contents but reduced moisture in all samples. Fish Species imposed the strongest effect on taste profiles, followed by deodorization method, while simmering time showed the least influence. Both deodorization treatments improved flavor, with increased electronic tongue responses and FAA levels. GC-IMS detected 89 volatile compounds, mainly aldehydes, alcohols, and ketones. Extended heating increased fishy volatiles and decreased favorable ethyl acetate. While prolonged simmering enhances nutrient release, it simultaneously accelerates lipid oxidation and accumulates fishy off-odor volatiles. Applying sensory masking and yeast extract effectively mitigates these off-odors and boosts sweet and umami amino acids. Optimal simmering was 2 h for New Zealand hoki and Pacific cod soups, and 4 h for Atlantic mackerel soup. Sensory masking showed better deodorization, while yeast extract delivered stronger umami. These results support process optimization and sustainable valorization of fish by-products.
10.3389/fnbeh.2026.2016852: This research topic on Neurobiology and Behavior in Fish: Insights and Innovations in Frontiers in Behavioral Neuroscience brings together seven articles on four fish species including zebrafish (Danio rerio), Japanese medaka (Oryzias latipes), the mangrove rivulus (Kryptolebias marmoratus), and the blunt snout bream (Megalobrama amblycephala) with the goal of advancing our understanding of the fish nervous system and behavior through pharmacological, behavioral and genetic investigations.A major theme in this Research Topic is the use of behavioral neuroscience tests to infer neural function, both at baseline and after experimental manipulation. Shinkai et al. investigate the most widely used behavioral assay for testing anxiety-like behaviour in zebrafish -the novel tank dive test (https://doi.org/10.3389/fnbeh.2025.1624277). Fish are placed into a novel tank and vertical location is used as a proxy for anxiety-like behavior, with 'anxious' fish spending more time at the bottom. The authors use a logistic regression analysis on fish tracking data to greatly reduce false detections of freezing. Alteration of stress-like states is manipulated via restraint and darkness which reduces variability in the latency to enter the top half of the tank. However, a combination of darkness and restraint provoke abnormal escape responses. Shinkai et al. report behavioral alteration with test tank temperature and net chasing compared to funnel transfer, and no habituation after five consecutive days of testing.Guan et al. establish an in vitro model of olfactory epithelial cells from the blunt snout bream, Megalobrama amblycephala, reporting that collagenase digestion yields stable cultures with well-preserved ciliated neurons (https://doi.org/10.3389/fcell.2025.1587151). Scanning electron microscopy reveals olfactory neurospheres, while immunofluorescence and molecular assays confirm neuronal identity and olfactory receptor expression. Stimulation with an amino acid mixture or prostaglandin F2α increases pERK-labeled cells, indicating activation of olfactory signaling. RNA-seq analysis further identifies differentially expressed genes enriched in olfactory and reproductive pathways. Collectively, these findings provide a valuable platform for studying how fishes detect environmental odorants and integrate olfactory cues with reproductive physiology.Brain derived-neurotrophic factor (BDNF) is a conserved regulator of brain functioning, including synaptic plasticity and learning. In the study by Rovegno et al. variation of bdnf gene expression is investigated in the MIKK panel of 53 near-isolated medaka lines, revealing up to a 98% difference variation within the populations, (https://doi.org/10.3389/fnbeh.2026.1681619). Seasonal variability is present with higher bdnf in the summer and lower in the winter, but this is also reversed in some isogenic lines. There are no sex differences in the overall population but there are at the isogenic line level.In a second study on BDNF, Rovegno et al. test object recognition memory in a bdnf -/-line of zebrafish and compare them to wild-type siblings (bdnf +/+ ) (https://doi.org/10.3389/fnbeh.2026.1710671). Larvae (14 days post fertilization) undergo a novel object recognition procedure with visual stimuli (lines or crosses). There are no differences in the familiar, nor in novel object preference between the lines. However, using an absolute recognition index that takes into consideration a novel or familiar object preference, there is a significant decrease in preference in the bdnf -/-line.With psilocybin gaining popularity as a compound that may have clinical value, testing its effects in animal models is a first step in assessing its efficacy. Forsyth et al. report on the effects of psilocybin on social behaviour in the mangrove rivulus (https://doi.org/10.3389/fnbeh.2026.1767175). Testing in a dyadic pair of fish, psilocybin decreases the time spent moving and swimming bursts in the focal fish after stimulus fish exposure. Swimming bursts and increased activity in response to a conspecific are related to aggression in the rivulus. Thus, this suggests that psilocybin acts to decrease aggression related behaviours in this candidate model species.Severe tissue hypoxia, including hypoxia arising from cardiac dysfunction, increasingly emerges as a trigger of neurobehavioral change. Yet the effects of early-life hypoxia on anxiety-like behavior and behavioral disinhibition remain poorly understood. In the study by Vazquez-Roman and Burggren, acute, severe hypoxic exposure in zebrafish larvae reduces later exploratory behavior, especially diminished attraction to novel objects (https://doi.org/10.3389/fnbeh.2026.1717856). Inhibition of p38 MAPK (protein kinases that help cells respond to environmental stress and inflammation) rescues growth and prevents hypoxia-induced length restriction, but paradoxically intensifies anxiety-like thigmotaxis. These findings reveal that protective molecular interventions during hypoxia can carry unexpected neurobehavioral trade-offs.With the increasing use of larval zebrafish to test pharmacological compounds and toxicants, Hagen et al., examine the impact of three well known solvents used to deliver poorly soluble compounds (https://doi.org/10.3389/fnbeh.2025.1717998). Thirty-minute exposure to up to 1% DMSO has no detectable effect on locomotion, thigmotaxis, or startle responses (light, dark, and tap). Methanol and ethanol at 1%, however, increase locomotion, and ethanol also blunts the startle response to sudden darkness. For acute experiments requiring a solvent, their data favors use of DMSO.Collectively, the articles of this special issue advance on several fronts our understanding of the fish nervous system and behavior. To continue moving forward, we can prioritize the standardization of protocols (Shinkai et al., 2026) and solvent choice (Hagen et al., 2026), to promote reproducible pharmacological research in fish. Variation in individual, seasonal, and sex-dependent bdnf expression in medaka lines (Rovengo et al., 2026a), along with the role of BDNF in object recognition in zebrafish (Rovengo et al., 2026b), suggest that future research should collect data for both male and female fish, report the season and testing conditions, and use isogenic lines to tease apart genetic from environmental influences. The impact of hypoxia can have long lasting behavioral impacts, with p38 MAPK reversing some physiological damage, but producing later behavioral deficits (Vazquez & Burggren, 2026), demonstrating the complex relationship between physiology and neurobehavior and scarcity of 'silver bullets'. Using the mangrove rivulus to investigate the impact of psilocybin (Forsyth et al., 2026) highlights the value of using fish models other than the zebrafish for pharmacological challenges and pilot drug testing. Mechanistic screening can also take place in vitro with cultured olfactory epithelial cells (Guan et al., 2026) which offers a scalable platform for olfactory odorant research. Notably, neuroimaging, electrophysiology and optogenetics remain underrepresented, and we encourage future work to incorporate these approaches with behavioral paradigms to assess the mechanistic basis in which neural activity confers behavior.
10.1007/s11802-026-6773-y: Integrins are transmembrane receptors essential for cell adhesion and signaling, with known roles in growth regulation in vertebrates. However, the mechanisms employed by integrins to coordinate growth and environmental adaptation in bivalves remain unknown. The high-quality genome of Crassostrea gigas was referenced to identify 23 integrin genes, which included 8 α and 15 β subunits. Phylogenetic and structural analyses revealed lineage-specific expansion of the β subunits, suggesting functional diversification. Expression profiling across developmental stages, tissues, and selectively bred oyster lines revealed marked expression divergence associated with both growth performance and environmental adaptation. Notably, several integrin genes (e.g., Cg-ITGA1.2, Cg-ITGB1.2a, and Cg-ITGB1.4) were markedly upregulated in the fast-growing strain relative to the growth-depressed inbred line, implicating involvement in growth regulation. Conversely, overall integrin expression was higher in wild oysters than in the ‘Haida No. 1’ strain, suggesting that elevated integrin activity may confer environmental resilience rather than directly promote growth. Together, these findings reveal the evolutionary expansion and transcriptional divergence of the C. gigas family of integrins, highlighting dual roles in mediation of growth and environmental adaptability as a classical physiological trade-off. Functional studies are further warranted to elucidate the molecular mechanisms driving these patterns.
10.15517/29j0jp96: Introduction: Costa Rica hosts remarkable marine biodiversity, vital for conserving its marine and coastal ecosystems. However, marine macroalgae remains understudied, especially in the Área de Conservación Guanacaste (ACG). To address this, the BioMar-ACG Project began in 2015 as a collaboration between the government, academic institutions, and NGOs, aiming to document marine biodiversity using morphological and molecular tools, with local community involvement. The project has since expanded macroalgal collections, identified new species, corrected misidentifications, and revealed high regional endemism. Objective: To update the marine macroalgae inventory of the ACG using 2009-2024 collections from the BioMar-ACG Project and CIMAR-UCR previous projects, through morphological and molecular identification. Methods: Surveys were conducted at 35 coastal and island sites, from intertidal zones to 20 m depth, using snorkeling and SCUBA techniques. Sampling occurred during both upwelling and non-upwelling seasons to capture environmental variability. Macroalgae were manually collected, documented in situ, and preserved for morphological and molecular analyses. DNA was extracted using commercial kits, targeting six molecular markers (COX, ITS, psbA, rbcL, tufA, and UPA) for genetic identification. Final taxonomic identifications integrated molecular and morphological data. Results: A total of 562 specimens were analyzed, representing 101 species distributed among Rhodophyta (59 spp.), Heterokontophyta (22 spp.), and Chlorophyta (20 spp.). Thirty-one species were newly recorded for Costa Rica, 22 for the Pacific of Central America, and nine genera were documented for the first time in the region. Molecular analyses revealed nine potential new species to science. Conclusions: The BioMar-ACG Project substantially increased knowledge of the marine flora of Costa Rica’s northern Pacific, doubling the number of species previously reported for the ACG. The discovery of new genera and species, together with high genetic divergence within groups such as Ceramiales and Dictyotales, highlights the underestimated and cryptic nature of macroalgal diversity in the Eastern Tropical Pacific. These findings emphasize the need for continuous exploration, molecular re-evaluation of historical records, and inclusion of diverse habitats and depth gradients in future studies. The integration of morphological and molecular data, combined with community-based research, has proven an effective model for strengthening biodiversity documentation and marine conservation in Costa Rica.
10.1007/s12562-026-02052-y: This study investigated the effects of setting temperature and time on gel properties as well as flavor compound generation and release in rabbitfish (Siganus fuscescens) surimi suwari gel. To comprehensively evaluate the changes in suwari gel properties and flavor characteristics during surimi setting, various experimental techniques and analytical methods were used including gel breaking properties, water-holding capacity, molecular forces, total sulfhydryl content, gas chromatography-mass spectrometry (GC-MS) analysis, and correlation analysis. Results indicated that setting at 40 °C for 40 min yielded the highest breaking force. With regard to flavor profile, hexanal, 1-penten-3-ol, and 1-octen-3-ol were identified as the primary contributors during setting. The overall concentrations of flavor compounds showed an increasing trend with increasing setting temperature and time. Correlation analysis suggested that aldehyde volatilization was associated with gel physical properties, whereas alcohol volatilization showed a weak association with gel physical properties.
10.1007/s12562-026-02043-z: We evaluated whether illumination with specific light wavelengths improves prey capture efficiency in red sea bream Pagrus major larvae reared in tanks containing rotifers as prey. Specifically, we studied the role of UV vision in the feeding behavior of red sea bream larvae on prey rotifers. We compared the number of rotifers ingested by larvae using 5-, 10-, 15- and 20-day post-hatching (dph) individuals under different conditions. Ingestion rates and the number of ingested rotifers under monochromatic illumination were higher in UV and blue than in red and green. The number of ingested rotifers was significantly increased by mixing UV with red, green and white light. RNA sequencing of larval head tissues showed that UV-sensitive opsin genes (short-wavelength-sensitive opsin 1; sws1) were expressed at higher levels during early developmental stages and opsin gene expression profiles changed at 15 dph. Furthermore, measurement of the absorbance spectrum of rotifers indicated higher absorption in the UV wavelength range, implying that UV vision may increase contrast between translucent prey and the background. These results indicate that red sea bream larvae effectively use UV vision in feeding behavior during early developmental stages. It is suggested that application of UV light in larval rearing systems may improve growth and survival of larvae.
10.1093/bbb/zbag168: Abstract Fish are dietary sources of bioactive lipids, including long-chain n-3 polyunsaturated fatty acids; however, phosphatidylcholine (PC) molecular profiles across fish species and muscle types remain poorly characterized. We analyzed PC molecular species in skeletal muscle from eight fish species by LC-MS-based lipidomics and examined associations with swimming lifestyle and muscle type. PC fatty acyl composition and molecular profiles varied substantially among species, and principal component analysis separated three farmed species from five wild-caught marine species. An exploratory comparison among wild-caught species suggested that the two migratory Scomber species generally showed higher relative abundances of 18:0-, 20:4-, and 22:6-containing PC molecular species than the two demersal species. PC profiles also differed between white and red muscle, particularly for 16:0-, 18:0-, and 18:1-containing molecular species. These findings provide foundational data for future studies of factors shaping fish muscle PC composition.
10.2989/1814232x.2026.2662912: This study evaluated how coastal fishing affects sea turtles along the central Atlantic coast of Morocco, a globally significant biological region. Data were collected through structured interviews with fishers/captains, and a 15-month participatory monitoring programme involving selected captains. All participants operated within the Port of Agadir’s coastal fleet, which includes pelagic purse-seiners, demersal trawlers and demersal (bottom-set) longliners. To assess the 2021 sea turtle bycatch, data were gathered through structured interviews with 63 fishers, followed by participatory monitoring of 10 vessels from April 2022 to June 2023. Based on the participatory monitoring, we estimate that approximately 20 sea turtles were caught by demersal trawlers and pelagic purse-seiners during the study period. Sea turtle bycatch rates were slightly higher for demersal trawlers (mean 0.0221 captures/day) than for pelagic purse-seiners (mean 0.0144 captures/day). The only sea turtle species in the bycatch was the loggerhead turtle Caretta caretta, predominantly subadults. Based on the fisher survey, which also represented demersal longliners besides demersal trawlers and pelagic purse-seiners, we estimated ∼84 sea turtle captures occurred in 2021. Fishers perceived a decline in the loggerhead turtle population, and sea turtle captures were concentrated in spring and summer. Data from participatory monitoring with collaborating captains revealed notably high direct and potential mortality rates for loggerhead turtles in the region, emphasising the urgent need for conservation measures.
10.1080/15502287.2026.2759914: This paper reports the comprehensive flexural behaviour of biomimetic protective beams inspired by the hierarchical architecture of fish scales. The models measuring 150 mm × 20 mm × 10 mm, comprised of a 5 mm thick scale-tissue hybrid layer of overlapping Acrylonitrile Butadiene Styrene (ABS) scales embedded in a Thermoplastic Polyurethane (TPU) matrix, supported by a 5 mm soft tissue sub-layer. Scale geometries were derived from four fish species (i.e., Salmon, Bass, Tuna, and Corydoras), each exhibiting unique morphology and scale volume fractions ranging from ∼21% to ∼46%. A constant scale volume baseline (∼28% scale volume fraction) was used for comparative evaluation. The results showed that increasing scale volume fraction significantly improved energy absorption in the rigid scale phase while also moderately enhancing energy dissipation in the compliant tissue analogue. Reverse loading revealed that directional anchoring and curvature of the scales further contributed to stiffness gains, underscoring the importance of asymmetric morphology in load transfer. Among the tested configurations, designs with larger scale geometry (such as in Salmon) demonstrated superior mechanical performance due to improved continuous scale-tissue interaction and stress localisation within the stiff phase. At constant scale volume fractions, mechanical behaviour was also governed by geometric attributes such as scale length, curvature, and interlocking. Overall, the study highlights the characteristics of bio-inspired design for achieving flexible and mechanically efficient protective systems.
10.1111/raq.70228: ABSTRACT Infectious disease in aquaculture is shaped by interactions among pathogens, hosts and the surrounding environment. Temperature, salinity and other physicochemical conditions are established modifiers of several aquatic diseases, whereas environmental contaminants have been studied predominantly for their direct toxic effects. Whether contaminant exposure also alters subsequent infection has received much less integrated attention. We critically evaluate evidence linking environmental contaminants with viral, bacterial and parasitic infections in aquatic animals, while using established physicochemical stressors as a reference framework. Direct challenge studies show that pesticides, persistent organic contaminants, microplastics, mycotoxins and other pollutants can alter pathogen replication, infection severity or infection-associated mortality in specific host-pathogen systems. Several studies report altered infection outcomes after sublethal exposure despite limited or absent mortality, growth impairment or overt cytotoxicity before pathogen challenge. Pathogen challenge can therefore reveal functional effects of contaminant exposure that may be missed by conventional apical toxicity endpoints. However, the relationship is not uniform. Null, non-monotonic and occasionally protective effects have also been reported, and most direct evidence remains confined to laboratory studies in fish and shrimp. Evidence for transmission, commercial production systems, molluscs and parasitic diseases is comparatively scarce. Environmental contaminants should therefore be regarded as context-dependent modifiers of infectious-disease risk rather than universal causes of disease outbreaks. Where contaminant-associated susceptibility is demonstrated, disease control may need to address both the relevant contaminant exposure and the pathogen. This evidence supports exploring dual-function interventions that restore or mitigate contaminant-induced host dysfunction while directly inhibiting the pathogen.
10.1111/emr.70074: ABSTRACT Tropical oyster reefs are ecologically important ecosystems that support significant ecosystem services across coastal seascapes. Yet their current distribution and conservation needs remain poorly understood, limiting the effectiveness of management. In tropical Queensland, Australia, historical oyster reef declines and current threats have not been evaluated within a standardised risk-assessment framework. Here, we apply the IUCN Red List of Ecosystems (RLE) criteria to assess the conservation status of tropical eastern Australian Saccostrea (TEAS) reef ecosystems. We synthesised historical records, contemporary satellite imagery and field surveys to delineate TEAS reef ecosystem characteristics, define functional and collapsed states and quantify changes in distribution. Our analysis reveals a reduction in reef ecosystem occurrences since 1750, restricted contemporary distributions, pervasive environmental degradation driven by increased catchment modification and sediment loads and identifies ongoing climate change and declining water quality as continuing and persistent risks to their conservation. We conclude that TEAS reef ecosystems are Vulnerable to extinction under three of five criteria (A: reduction in geographic distribution, B: restricted geographic range and C: environmental degradation). Criterion D (disruption of biotic processes and interactions) and Criterion E (quantitative risk analysis) were Data Deficient and not assessed. Formal recognition of TEAS reefs within state and federal conservation frameworks, alongside integrated catchment management, climate-adaptive restoration approaches and improved species-level taxonomic resolution, is essential for safeguarding these ecosystems. This assessment establishes the first baseline conservation evaluation for tropical oyster reefs in the world and provides a foundation for future regional and international assessments.
10.3390/su182211535: Environmental governance in socio-ecological systems requires coordination among actors and institutions operating across different territorial and administrative scales. This study develops a multi-level environmental governance framework for recreational fisheries in the Toltén River Basin, southern Chile. A mixed-methods case study combined a socioeconomic survey of 188 stakeholders, semi-structured interviews with public-sector representatives, and participatory workshops conducted across the basin. Quantitative and qualitative evidence were integrated to identify governance challenges, territorial priorities, stakeholder roles, and opportunities for institutional coordination. The results identified resource-use pressures alongside institutional fragmentation, limited inter-municipal coordination, weak organisational capacity, and the limited availability of permanent mechanisms for collective action. Participatory mapping identified 61 priority areas for recreational fisheries and 74 conflict hotspots, highlighting the spatial extent of these challenges beyond municipal boundaries. Based on these findings, a governance framework was structured around municipal, river basin, and regional scales, linking local priorities with basin-scale coordination and regional planning. The framework builds on existing municipal and regional coordination mechanisms, while proposing basin-level coordination as a subsequent stage to strengthen cross-municipal articulation. The study illustrates how participatory processes can inform the development of place-based, multi-level governance arrangements for complex river basin systems and provides a case-based contribution to the study of recreational fisheries governance in territorially fragmented socio-ecological contexts.
10.52998/trjmms.2042258: Commercial marine fisheries face growing pressure to cut carbon emissions while struggling with fleet overcapacity and volatile fuel prices. This study examines the Turkish Black Sea fleet (6584 vessels across 34 ports) by combining vessel registry records, long-run catch and cost accounts, hull-resistance estimates, port-level spatial patterns, fleet efficiency comparisons, and policy simulations. Registry data show that installed engine power is heavily concentrated in industrial purse seiners and trawlers, with nearly half of trawlers and one-fifth of purse seiners exceeding gear-specific power-to-tonnage reference ranges. Theoretical resistance estimates indicate that wave-making drag accounts for most hull resistance during free-running transit (58-79%) but becomes negligible during low-speed towing and net setting. Across the coast, vessel engine intensity clusters regionally, whereas total installed power is concentrated in major fishing ports. Financial accounts for 2023 show that fuel absorbs roughly one-fifth of gross revenue, leaving a 29.5% net margin after capital costs and exposing operators to sharp margin compression when diesel prices rise, while efficiency comparisons point to moderate room for emission reductions across regional fleet segments. Against a realistic operational baseline of 366.98 kt CO2 yr-1 (784.92 kt yr-1 at theoretical full capacity), a hypothetical policy combining a 441 kW active-gear engine-power limit with the retirement of vessels over 35 years old cuts projected emissions by 29.3% (107.55 kt CO2 yr-1, or 166.95 kt against the upper bound). Even so, retiring older vessels on its own barely shifts surviving-fleet profitability unless lower fleet crowding is assumed to improve catch rates. Long-run multi-basin records further show that broader catch diversity is associated with steadier revenues in smaller fleets, a relationship that weakens as vessel numbers grow.
10.9734/jsrr/2026/v32i114726: Fisheries cooperatives are considered one of the most effective means of developing the fisheries sector and improving the living standards of poor fishermen. The current study maps research output on fisheries cooperatives during 1941-2023 using data retrieved from the Dimensions AI database, Google Scholar, and ResearchGate. A total of 310 publications were used for this investigation to evaluate the scientific productivity in the selected subject area. Thematic analysis was also used to review the global research landscape in fisheries cooperatives. Global publication shares, rankings and developments in research and bibliometric indices such as overall citations and average citation per paper were also analysed. In continent-specific publications, Asia ranked first (73.87%); in country-specific publications, Japan ranked first (26.13%), and within India, Kerala (20.59%) has the highest number. The journal Marine Policy (4.19%) carried the highest number of research papers. However, important gaps remain, particularly the under-representation of geographical regions. The thematic analysis revealed that studies predominantly focused on marine societies. Among all the studies, the principal areas of focus included the role of cooperatives and challenges (30.38%), socio-economic and financial analysis (29.75%), governance and management (26.58%), sustainability and conservation (7.59%), gender/women empowerment (3.48%), and technology integration (2.22%). Overall, this study highlights the importance of growth dynamics in fisheries cooperatives and identifies future research areas. These findings provide valuable insights for enhancing research efforts in this area, which may help improve the performance of these societies and support their development.
10.1088/2976-601x/aeb1d8: CORRIGENDUM: Managing expectations: implementing nutrition- sensitive fisheries and aquaculture (2026 Environ. Res.: Food Syst. 3 025008), Farmery, Anna K, Fullbrook, Liam, Allison, Edward H
10.37134/jadcm.vol1.2.1.2026: Fish sorting is an important aquaculture management practice for controlling size variation, feeding competition, and production efficiency. Conventional mechanical grading methods remain relevant because of their operational simplicity and relatively low technological requirements. However, labor demands, repeated fish handling, and variations in grading performance highlight opportunities for design improvement. This conceptual study critically synthesizes eight purposively selected publications published between 2016 and 2026 to examine developments in mechanical grading, electronic sensing, automation, machine vision, artificial intelligence, and digital connectivity. A focused narrative review was conducted using five analytical dimensions: functionality, usability, affordability, adaptability, and sustainability. Based on the literature synthesis, the Mechanical-Sensing-Automation-Intelligence-Connectivity (MSAIC) framework is proposed as a modular, problem-oriented approach to fish sorting equipment innovation. Catfish Sorter Pro, an existing manually operated mechanical grading prototype, is used to illustrate the potential application of the framework and opportunities for selective technological integration. The synthesis suggests that technological sophistication should not be considered independently of operational requirements, implementation costs, maintenance accessibility, and fish welfare. The proposed framework provides a conceptual basis for selecting technological capabilities according to specific design problems and resource constraints. However, neither the framework's practical effectiveness nor the performance of the proposed technological upgrades has been empirically established. Future research should validate the framework through comparative prototype testing, user-centered evaluation, economic assessment, and fish welfare monitoring.
10.3390/biology15222069: Thermal discharge from coastal nuclear power plants forms persistent temperature gradients in waters adjacent to outfalls, and is one of the typical anthropogenic disturbances in nearshore waters. However, whether fish community patterns under thermal discharge are consistent between water and sediment, and whether the two media provide complementary information, remain poorly understood. In October 2024, we collected water (n = 16) and sediment (n = 15) samples near the Hongyanhe Nuclear Power Plant, Liaodong Bay, and applied environmental DNA (eDNA) metabarcoding to compare fish community composition and spatial patterns across media in near- and far-field zones. A total of 32 fish taxa were identified: 2 only in water, 6 only in sediment, and 24 in both media. α-Diversity calculated from OTU abundance data did not differ significantly among the four medium-zone groups, mean Shannon index was numerically higher in far-field water (1.64) than in near-field water (1.07), and Simpson index showed a similar non-significant trend. Water community similarity declined with both geographic and environmental distances (distance-decay pattern), and indicator taxon analysis identified Acanthopagrus schlegelii and Lateolabrax maculatus as near-field water indicators and Sardinella zunasi and Thryssa kammalensis as far-field water indicators. Sediment communities showed high within-group dispersion and no distance-decay pattern. PERMANOVA revealed a significant medium × zone interaction, indicating that near-far-field differences in fish community composition depended on sample medium. Water community structure was associated with seawater temperature, nitrate concentration, and salinity, whereas sediment community structure showed no significant associations with the measured environmental variables. Overall, water and sediment eDNA provided partially complementary information on fish detection; combined water-sediment sampling is recommended to broaden monitoring coverage. This single-survey study provides baseline data for multi-medium fish eDNA monitoring to support future management of thermal-discharge impacts.
10.1007/s13353-026-01129-9: The efficacy of effective microorganism products in aquaculture covers multiple aspects that act directly on fish, such as improving resistance to fungal, bacterial, and viral infections, reproduction, feed efficiency, and overall growth performance, or indirectly through improved water quality. In this study, the application of two commercial water and two commercial food Effective Microorganism supplements was tested under recirculating aquaculture system conditions for their effect on the water and intestinal microbiome of common carp (Cyprinus carpio), as well as on carp growth performance. Neither the dynamics of alpha diversity nor the abundance of single genera followed a pattern related to the experimental setup defined by the supplementation. However, the effects of supplementation were clearly manifested by an increase in the final weight of the fish. The most consistent alteration was a significant increase in Lactococcus abundance in the intestinal microbiome compared to that in the control group, as observed in both experimental setups. We conclude that feed supplementation with Lactococcus enhances its intestinal abundance in fish and promotes improved growth performance, likely through mechanisms involving glucose absorption and metabolism, as demonstrated in previous studies.
10.3390/ijms272210154: Mussels are considered active biofilters that filter suspended and dissolved components of water and can be used in aquaculture. We studied the role of green mussels (Perna viridis) in filtering aquaculture effluent and its effects on gametogenesis and physiological processes. We established four experimental groups: G1, G2, G3, and G4. Groups G1 and G2 received fish-cultured wastewater and shrimp-cultured wastewater, respectively. Group G3 received low-nutrient seawater, whereas G4 served as a mussel-free control and received low-nutrient seawater under otherwise identical experimental conditions. The impact of biofiltration was evaluated by analyzing gonad morphology, gene expression, and physiological energetics. The results show a significant change in the gonadal structure, with low spermatozoa and spermatid content characterizing G1, and adipogranular cells becoming more prominent. G2 showed a comparatively high number of sperm cells, with spermatozoa becoming more prominent in the gonads. G3 is characterized by elevated sperm volume. CASA semen analysis showed low sperm counts and reduced motility and other kinematic parameters in G1 and G2. The Gonadosomatic Index (GSI) and Condition Index (CI) indicated better physiological condition in G2 and G3, with the highest survival rate in G2. Quantitative real-time PCR results revealed the expression of genes in the hepatopancreas, with high expression (p < 0.05) of Glutathione S-transferases (gst-o1), Heat shock protein 60 (hsp60), Heat shock protein 70 (hsp70), Nuclear factor erythroid 2-related factor 2 (NRF2), superoxide dismutase (SOD1), and a key sensor of oxidative and electrophilic stress-1 (KEAP1). Ammonia excretion was high in the G1 and G2 groups, and oxygen consumption was initially high in G1 and G2, later declining until the 21st day, while in G3 a stable trend was observed. Despite P. viridis’s positive role in bioremediation, aquaculture effluents negatively impact reproductive functions; moreover, P. viridis filtration augmented the decrease in nutrient content along with other abiotic components in the recirculating aquaculture in the G1 and G2 groups, confirming its role as a biofilter and helping with the reuse of aquaculture effluents.
10.3389/fcell.2026.1925369: Endoreplication is a conserved cell-cycle modification in which cells undergo repeated rounds of DNA replication without mitosis or cytokinesis, generating cellular polyploidy. This process contributes to cell growth, metabolic expansion, and developmental specialization across plants, invertebrates, and mammals. In teleost fish, whose genomes have been shaped by ancestral whole-genome duplications, endoreplication may have particular evolutionary significance. In hybrid fish systems characterized by genomic incompatibility, premeiotic endoreplication may serve as a meiotic rescue mechanism in some hybrid lineages that enables homologous chromosome pairing and circumvents hybrid sterility, as suggested by cytological evidence in female hybrid Clarias catfish ( Clarias macrocephalus × Clarias gariepinus ), where endoreplicated oocytes were observed in 12 of 372 pachytene cells (3.2%) and 45 of 142 diplotene cells (31.7%) from different females.
