This review synthesizes current knowledge on the molecular regulation of the endo-switch, for which suppression of Cyclin B/CDK1 and oscillatory Cyclin E/CDK2 activity are discussed as candidate regulatory features rather than an established Clarias mechanism, and discusses regulatory differences between pure endocycles and abortive endomitosis. We further evaluate approaches used to manipulate polyploidy in aquaculture, including physical shocks and chemical treatments used to induce polyploidy, while considering CRISPR/Cas9-based manipulation of CDK1 as an experimental functional approach rather than an established production method. Finally, we outline emerging multi-omics and artificial intelligence-based frameworks for predicting hybrid endoreplication potential and mitigating genomic instability, thereby bridging cell cycle regulation with precision aquaculture strategies. Collectively, these findings provide a mechanistic and applied framework that connects fundamental cell cycle mechanisms with the next-generation of polyploid-based aquaculture innovation.
10.1007/s40152-026-00534-4: Salmon aquaculture is a major contributor to coastal economies in Norway, yet the industry continues to face challenges related to local legitimacy and social acceptance. This study examines how voluntary corporate social responsibility (CSR) initiatives undertaken by salmon aquaculture companies are evaluated by local stakeholders and how these evaluations relate to social licence to operate (SLO). Drawing on 27 semi-structured interviews across three case companies in Arctic Norway, the study examines community-oriented, environmental, and economic development initiatives through the lens of legitimacy theory. The findings show that these initiatives contribute unevenly to different forms of legitimacy. Community and economic initiatives are widely recognized and generate tangible local benefits, providing a relatively strong basis for pragmatic legitimacy. Environmental initiatives, although substantial, are less consistently aligned with the normative concerns through which stakeholders evaluate environmental responsibility, resulting in a more contested basis for moral legitimacy. The findings further show that cognitive legitimacy may develop through normalization and coexistence without implying active endorsement, particularly among stakeholders who experience trade-offs from aquaculture development. The study contributes to SLO research by showing that local social acceptance can be sustained through an uneven configuration of pragmatic, moral, and cognitive legitimacy, and that legitimacy established in one dimension should not be assumed to transfer automatically to others.
10.12991/jrespharm.1725886: Channa striata fish, commonly known as the “striped snakehead”, is a freshwater fish species widely distributed in Southeast Asia, particularly in Indonesia. The aims of this study were to evaluate the physicochemical characteristics, fatty acids composition and antioxidant activity of Channa striata fish oil from Konda, Southeast Sulawesi affected of purification adsorbent. The Soxhlet method was used for fish oil extraction. The result was found that the purification of fish oil using bentonite and activated charcoal adsorbents resulted in a reduction of acid value, peroxide value, and refractive index, while no significant differences were observed in iodine value and saponification value across treatments. Purification of the oil using activated charcoal resulted in an increased relative percentage of saturated fatty acids, specifically heptadecanoic acid (5.76%) and arachidic acid (11.07%), accompanied by a decrease in monounsaturated fatty acids such as palmitoleic acid (23.33%) and the absence of polyunsaturated fatty acids, notably gamma-linolenic acid, which was not detected. The chelating agent activity of fish oil increased following purification with both bentonite and activated charcoal. However, an enhancement in DPPH radical scavenging activity was observed only in the samples purified with bentonite. In contrast, purification with activated charcoal led to a reduction in ABTS radical scavenging activity. The sPLS-DA technique, using FTIR spectral absorbance data as variables, effectively discriminated between crude fish oil and fish oil purified with bentonite and activated charcoal. In conclusion, oil purification enhances the physicochemical properties of snakehead (Channa striata) fish oil.
10.1088/1748-3190/aec1ad: Abstract Flying fish evade predatory threats through cross-medium gliding manoeuvres, in which the ventral fins play a pivotal regulatory role. Although previous studies have examined the influence of ventral fin configuration on gliding stability, the dynamic characteristics of escape trajectories and the regulatory effects of ventral fin posture on gliding attitude remain poorly understood. Here, we employ a biomimetic approach to elucidate the gliding patterns exhibited by flying fish during escape manoeuvres. We systematically investigate how ventral fin posture regulates gliding attitude and identify an optimal ventral fin mounting configuration. Combining full-factor experimental testing with computational fluid dynamics (CFD) simulations, we propose that flying fish adopt distinct gliding trajectories to evade predators in different media, with dynamic ventral fin adjustments acting as a key regulatory mechanism. Furthermore, by extending the parameter space beyond that accessible through biological observation, this study provides new theoretical guidance for the aerodynamic design and optimisation of multi-fin biomimetic robots.
10.3390/biology15222068: Muscle-associated lipids influence fish flesh composition, nutritional value, and sensory quality, but inconsistent definitions obscure comparisons among studies. This review distinguishes adipose tissue between anatomically distinct muscles, adipocytes within muscle connective tissue, lipid droplets within myofibers, and chemically measured muscle lipid content. In salmonids, myoseptal adipose tissue occupies the partitions between adjacent myomeres, whereas perimysial adipocytes lie within myomeres. We examine how these compartments develop, how their lipid storage is regulated, and how genetic and nutritional approaches can improve flesh quality. Salmonid precursor cultures support adipogenic differentiation involving PPARγ and C/EBPs, while evidence for depot-specific progenitor lineages remains limited. Genetic studies identify heritable variation and associated genomic regions for muscle lipid traits, but association, expression, and functional evidence frequently address different phenotypes or tissues. Translating these findings requires standardized sampling, spatially resolved measurements, and functional testing of candidate mechanisms. Research priorities include distinguishing adipocyte recruitment from lipid loading, separating cell-composition changes from intracellular regulation, and connecting causal variants with depot-specific phenotypes. Breeding objectives should integrate lipid distribution and fatty acid composition with processing quality, growth, feed efficiency, and environmental robustness. Imaging and multi-omics can support this integration when calibrated against defined biological traits and validated across populations and production environments.
10.1111/rec.70605: Abstract Introduction Richardson et al. contest the identity of oyster species that historically constructed subtidal shellfish reefs in South-East Queensland, Australia, suggesting that “ historical drift/dredge oysters may have been misidentified as S. glomerata .” Objectives To provide historic scientific evidence pertaining to subtidal shellfish reefs along Australia's east coast, to help inform the conservation status of Saccostrea glomerata . Methods Evidence provided by Richardson et al. is reviewed and compared to historical evidence. Results Evidence provided by Richardson et al. remains consistent with historic evidence that S. glomerata is capable of recruiting to both intertidal and subtidal habitats. Increased historical survival of S. glomerata spat in subtidal areas prior to 1893 was probably due to what observers at the time described as “astronomical recruitment,” facilitated by a lack of sedimentation and eutrophication. In contrast, subtidal spat settlement today is severely constrained by sedimentation and algal turfs, Queensland Unknown disease, and possibly also by relatively increased predation due to a potential Allee Effect. Conclusions The misidentification hypothesis appears to be built on a logical fallacy arising from shifting baseline syndrome.
10.3390/phycology6040122: This study provides a comprehensive assessment of the biomass and taxonomic and morpho-functional composition of stranded macroalgae and seagrasses on a highly productive shellfish bank in NW Iberia (Galicia), frequently affected by green tides, based on a year-long monitoring program and multivariate analyses. Macroalgal biomass showed marked seasonal and spatial variability, with the highest values recorded in spring. Chlorophyta dominated stranded biomass, particularly Ulva lacinulata, which accounted for over 63% of the total. Thin foliose morphotypes also made a major contribution to biomass across seasons and sampling locations. Linear mixed-effects modelling revealed a significant interaction between transect and intertidal level, indicating that spatial biomass patterns varied across the intertidal gradient. An interaction between season and intertidal level was also detected, although its statistical support was less consistent in sensitivity analyses. The absence of a consistent vertical zonation pattern suggests that stranded biomass distribution may be influenced by detachment, transport and deposition processes, rather than solely reflecting local macroalgal production. These findings highlight the importance of considering taxonomic and morpho-functional groups composition, spatial variability and hydrodynamic context when monitoring and managing valuable estuarine environments affected by green tides.
10.3390/w18222827: High-altitude freshwater ecosystems are particularly vulnerable to anthropogenic impacts, yet spatial and seasonal variations in biological responses remain poorly understood. This study assessed the health status of narrow-clawed crayfish (Pontastacus leptodactylus) and habitat condition in two hydrologically and environmentally distinct bays of Lake Sevan, Armenia, using an integrated hydrochemical and multibiomarker approach. Water quality and crayfish populations were measured in Lichk and Lchashen Bays in May, July, and October 2024 and 2025. In total, 120 crayfish specimens were examined, and oxidative stress responses were assessed in the hepatopancreas, gills, and muscle using MDA, GSH, GST, KAT, and SOD. Lchashen Bay experienced more adverse environmental conditions, characterized by pronounced hypoxia in the summer (3.4-3.9 mg O2 L-1), higher biochemical oxygen demand and permanganate oxidation, and elevated K, Na, and Mg concentrations. Biomarker responses showed significant seasonal variation, typically with highest values in July. Crayfish from Lchashen Bay consistently demonstrated higher biomarker responses than crayfish from Lichk Bay across all tissues and sampling periods. Integrated biomarker response (IBR) values confirmed this spatial pattern, indicating greater physiological stress in Lchashen Bay. The combined hydrochemical and biomarker approach demonstrates the suitability of P. leptodactylus as an indicator species for assessing sublethal environmental stress in Lake Sevan.
10.3390/fishes11110665: This study assessed bycatch composition, nominal catch rates, capture mortality and release condition in the Cypriot pelagic longline fishery targeting swordfish and albacore tuna. Observations covered 142 fishing days across 16 vessels during 2018-2024 and 335,340 hooks, recording 643 bycatch individuals from 23 species. Bycatch comprised 10.7% of the total catch biomass, with pooled rates of 1.92 individuals and 14.20 kg per 1000 hooks. Elasmobranchs accounted for 63.5% of bycatch individuals, and pelagic stingray alone accounted for 60.0%. Mean fishing-day bycatch biomass, expressed per 1000 hooks and 12 h, was 2.75 times as high in swordfish fishing as in albacore fishing (95% vessel-bootstrap confidence interval [CI] 1.53-3.68). Overall capture mortality was 26.4% (95% CI 23.2-30.0%), including 2.7% in elasmobranchs, 69.1% in teleost fishes and 60.7% in sea turtles. The low pooled elasmobranch mortality masked substantial taxonomic variation: 11 out of 22 sharks were dead at haulback (50.0%), whereas no deaths were observed among the 386 pelagic stingrays. Of the 406 individuals released alive, 396 (97.5%) were classified as Good for vitality, nine as Fair and one as Poor; all were coded as having Minor injury. Release condition remains a descriptive, uncalibrated indicator, and post-release survival was not measured. Sampling was partly opportunistic, and target fishery was partly confounded with year; results therefore describe the observed sample rather than the whole fleet. However, these findings establish a baseline for fishery-specific monitoring and mitigation and highlight the importance of distinguishing shark and stingray capture mortality.
10.1371/journal.pbio.3004065: Many organisms alternate between distinct life stages and can reproduce either sexually or asexually, yet the mechanisms coordinating these developmental and reproductive transitions remain poorly understood. Here, we investigate the molecular basis of life stage identity and reproductive mode in the kelp Laminaria pallida , a multicellular organism with a complex life cycle. By combining gene expression analyses with developmental experiments and natural population-level approaches, we characterize the transcriptional signatures associated with developmental state transitions in both sexual and asexual contexts. We show that asexual reproduction is associated with endoreduplication and reduced fitness, while it is retained but rarely expressed in two natural populations. Moreover, we find that the presence of potential mating partners reduces asexual development, revealing that reproductive mode is adjusted in response to reproductive opportunities. Together, these findings suggest that asexual reproduction functions as a conditional alternative to sex, promoting persistence when sexual reproduction is constrained while preserving the long-term benefits of sexual reproduction when mates are available. More broadly, our results reveal how organisms integrate developmental, environmental, and reproductive cues to balance alternative reproductive strategies across complex life cycles.
10.3389/fpubh.2026.1933985: Background Dietary ingestion is a major exposure pathway for environmental radionuclides, and the radiological safety of seafood, an important component of the global diet, has attracted increasing public concern. As a Chinese coastal city where seafood is a traditional part of local residents’ daily diet, Ningbo lacks systematic baseline data on radionuclide levels in locally common edible seafood and associated dietary radiological risks for local residents. Methods Five categories of locally common edible seafood (fish, shrimp, crabs, mollusks and algae) were collected from the southern coastal area of Ningbo during 2022-2025. Specific activities of 11 target γ-emitting radionuclides were quantified via high-purity germanium γ spectrometry in accordance with GB/T 16145-2022, and annual effective ingestion dose (AED) was estimated using local per capita seafood consumption data and ingestion dose conversion coefficients recommended in ICRP Publication 119. Results Natural radionuclides dominated across all five seafood categories, with 40 K detected in 100% of samples. Algae had the highest detection rates of 238 U (77.8%) and 210 Pb (55.6%), crabs had the highest 228 Ra detection rate (100%), and 226 Ra was detected at the highest rate in both crabs and algae (77.8%). For specific activities, algae exhibited the highest specific activities of 238 U (median 0.78, maximum 12.80 Bq/kg), 40 K (284.10, 931.00 Bq/kg) and 210 Pb (0.41, 7.96 Bq/kg); crabs had the highest 226 Ra (0.54, 13.09 Bq/kg); shrimp had the highest median 228 Ra activity (1.26 Bq/kg) while algae had the highest maximum activity (7.90 Bq/kg). Mollusks had the lowest median specific activities overall, but a higher 238 U detection rate than fish, shrimp and crabs. Only trace 137 Cs was detected in one fish (0.05 Bq/kg) and one mollusk (0.02 Bq/kg) sample from 2025. The median total AED was 30.43 μSv/y, with a conservative constructed upper-bound maximum of 133.64 μSv/y. Conclusion For the measured γ-emitting radionuclides only, natural radionuclides dominate in seafood from the study area, and all regulated radionuclides meeting China’s food radiological safety requirements. Artificial radionuclides were negligible with no significant anthropogenic perturbation, and the dietary dose for local adults in the study area remains below the ICRP-recommended public dose limit.
10.1007/s00203-026-05302-w: The present study aimed to investigate the occurrence of Arcobacter butzleri in seafood from the Mumbai coast, India and evaluated its genetic potential associated with virulence and antimicrobial resistance through comprehensive analysis of virulence-associated factors and antimicrobial resistance (AMR) determinants. Among the 70 samples screened, 44 were positive for A. butzleri, resulting in an overall prevalence of 62.86%. A higher rate of prevalence was reported from bivalves (84.62%), followed by crustaceans (78.57%), finfish (60.61%) and cephalopods (33.33%). Characterization of isolates based on putative virulence-associated genes revealed that most of them harboured more than five genes. Genes such as tlyA, cadF, ciaB, mviN and pldA were found dominant, whereas irgA and hecA were the limiting ones. Sample level characterization of total number of virulence-associated genes yielded significant differences among the seafood categories tested, with significant association between iroE gene and the sample category (P < 0.05). Phenotypic analysis of antibiotic susceptibility revealed 88.1% of the isolates to be multidrug resistant, with an average MAR indices of 0.39. The β-lactam resistant gene (blaOXA-464) was found to be the dominant gene in the present study, followed by macA. This study, underscores the significance of seafood as a possible carrier of pathogenic and antimicrobial-resistant A. butzleri and emphasizes the need for continuous surveillance and implementation of stringent hygienic practices.
10.3389/fmars.2026.1969343: Introduction Reef fish assemblages are widely used as indicators of coral reef condition. Yet, diver-based surveys provide limited temporal resolution and are constrained by logistical demands. We evaluated an autonomous underwater imaging system based on cameras programmed for unattended image acquisition to monitor reef fish assemblages in the southern Gulf of Mexico. Methods Five terrestrial trail cameras adapted for underwater deployment were operated at Bajo de Diez reef during two seasonal deployments in 2024 and 2025, yielding 191,758 valid underwater images at a nominal 3-min interval. Image quality, camera view, species diversity, and daily assemblage dynamics were evaluated using expert annotations of 27,471 images, iNEXT-4steps, multivariate analyses, and an RF-DETR Medium object-detection model applied to the complete valid underwater record. Results Across the expert-sampled record, the mean daily proportion of images containing at least one fish was 17%, and 65 species were recorded. Laplacian variance distinguished lower- from higher-quality images. Assemblage composition differed clearly between the two deployment contexts and showed smaller but statistically detectable heterogeneity among fixed camera views within each deployment, while daily observations revealed structured temporal variation. On the held-out image-level test set, RF-DETR Medium achieved mAP@50 = 0.741, mAP@50:95 = 0.545, precision = 0.794, and recall = 0.650. Across 68 dates shared by the expert and CV analyses, expert- and CV-derived Bray-Curtis temporal structure was positively correlated (ρ = 0.63; Mantel permutation test, p ≤ 0.0001), with similar concordance for daily richness and the image-based relative abundance index. Applied to nearly seven times the number of manually annotated images, RF-DETR expanded temporal support from 68 to 110 dates. Discussion Autonomous imaging can extend reef fish monitoring beyond discrete surveys through repeated acquisition, while computer vision can reduce manual processing within a human-supervised workflow. Within the site and deployment periods evaluated, combining sustained fixed imaging, expert annotation, and computer vision made fuller use of the image archive and provided daily information on reef fish assemblage structure and its variation through time.
10.1139/cjfas-2025-0391: In the Northwest Atlantic, acoustic telemetry is widely used to assess aquatic species movements and habitat use within and among conservation areas. We examined the contribution of acoustic telemetry to research and monitoring in St. Anns Bank Marine Protected Area (MPA) off Cape Breton Island (Mi’kmaq: Unama’ki), Nova Scotia. Acoustic telemetry receivers have been deployed within the MPA since 2015 (26 to 46 receivers per year), with tagging of Atlantic cod, Atlantic halibut, and Atlantic striped wolffish. Through integration with the Ocean Tracking Network (OTN), a dataset was assembled that included animals tagged within the MPA and animals tagged by other projects that subsequently passed through the area. This dataset directly informs biodiversity conservation objectives by documenting distinct spatial and temporal fluxes of migratory and seasonally resident species (15 species, 504 individuals). Findings demonstrated far reaching connectivity, strong affinity for a predominant shallow bathymetric feature (Scatarie Bank), and relationships with recorded bottom temperature and depth. This study demonstrates the utility of acoustic telemetry for long-term baseline monitoring of species occurrence, movement, and ecological change.
10.1007/s12562-026-02049-7: The potential utility as growth indices of mRNA levels of insulin-like growth factor (IGF)-1 and IGF-binding protein-1 subtypes in juvenile and larval shishamo smelt Spirinchus lanceolatus under captivity was examined. Juveniles of 3 g were subjected to a long-term fasting and refeeding experiment for 56 days, and liver and muscle samples were collected. Liver igf-1 levels decreased after fasting for 28 days and were restored to the fed control levels 28 days after refeeding. Liver igfbp-1a showed a response opposite to that of igf-1, being high in fasted fish and low in refed fish. In muscle, igf-1 showed a response similar to that in the liver whereas igfbp-1a levels in refed fish were lower than those of fed fish, suggesting that igf-1 and igfbp-1a respond to changes in feeding status regardless of the tissues examined. Another fasting experiment using larvae of 0.1 g revealed that (tail) muscle igf-1 and igfbp-1a levels decreased and increased after 18 days of fasting, respectively. The present study suggests that igf-1 and igfbp-1a are candidates as positive and inverse growth indices, respectively, in larval and juvenile shishamo smelts.
10.66073/refocus-conf/1311073: The article examines methods for preventing scoliosis in sturgeon species and the specific features of using specialized feed enriched with vitamin and mineral supplements. The research subjects were individuals of the ship sturgeon (Acipenser nudiventris). The main objective of the study was to evaluate the effects of specialized compound feed on the physiological condition, growth performance, and occurrence of scoliosis symptoms in fish. During the experiment, the body weight indicators, survival rate, hemoglobin concentration, and total protein content in the blood of fish from the experimental and control groups were examined. The results demonstrated that the use of feed enriched with vitamin and mineral supplements can improve fish growth performance and reduce the occurrence of scoliosis symptoms.
10.1002/aff2.70367: ABSTRACT The continued use of prohibited fishing gear in inland waters around the world poses a direct threat to the sound management of global fish stocks. This is also the case in Benin, where there has been a drastic decline in shrimp production since 2002, particularly in the Nokoué lagoon. This study aimed to compare the capture capacity (in space and time) of two types of fishing gear (traps and nets) that are less destructive on shrimp catches in the Nokoué lagoon and its inlet complex (North, South, Centre, East and West), as part of a sustainable exploitation strategy. In total, two genera of shrimp were sampled: Macrobrachium Spence Bate, 1868 and Penaeus Fabricius, 1798. Analysis of variance (ANOVA) analyses and Tukey's post hoc tests revealed a pronounced seasonal pattern in catches, particularly for Macrobrachium , with a peak in September and a low-catch period from March to June. Nets showed a prolonged period of low catches, whereas traps revealed four seasonal catch levels. For Penaeus , five seasonal catch levels were identified, corresponding to prolonged peaks in catches between January and June, followed by a gradual decline to the annual minimum in October and November. The spatial distribution of catches reflects significant heterogeneity between stations. For Macrobrachium , traps caught mainly at Western station, characterized by a high density of ‘Acadja’, whereas nets showed a peak at Eastern station. For Penaeus , Western station had the highest catches for both types of gear, whereas the other stations had intermediate or low yields, highlighting the importance of spatial configuration and artificial habitats in the distribution of populations. Kolmogorov-Smirnov tests confirmed that there were no significant differences between the seasonal effectiveness of traps and nets for both genera, indicating comparable overall performance. However, the chi-square test revealed a moderate but significant difference in the size frequencies of Penaeus , with nets capturing proportionally larger individuals 150-180 mm, whereas traps favoured intermediate sizes 90-120 mm. For Macrobrachium , no significant difference was observed, reflecting a population dominated by juveniles and adults. Chi-square residual analysis corroborated these observations, showing an overrepresentation of large Penaeus sizes in nets and intermediate sizes in traps. For Macrobrachium , differences in catch according to size class remain limited to individuals measuring 90-120 mm, mainly caught by traps. These results highlight the complex interaction between gear selectivity, seasonal dynamics, and spatial heterogeneity, underscoring the importance of these factors for the sustainable management of shrimp populations in the Nokoué lagoon.
10.1002/aff2.70365: ABSTRACT The expansion of aquaculture has intensified the search for sustainable alternatives to fishmeal. The mopane worm, Gonimbrasia belina (syn. Imbrasia belina ), is a traditionally consumed southern African insect whose protein, lipid and micronutrient contents have prompted interest in its use as an aquafeed ingredient. This semi-systematic review evaluates the nutritional value and digestibility of mopane worm meal and its effects on growth, feed utilisation and physiological responses in fish. Several experimental studies on mopane worm meal in fish diets, reviews and related insect-meal research used to examine its nutritional potential were identified. The available evidence suggests species-specific and inclusion-dependent responses. Mozambique tilapia ( Oreochromis mossambicus ) tolerated partial fishmeal replacement and exhibited increased activity of some digestive enzymes, although the fishmeal-based control achieved the highest growth. By contrast, increasing replacement levels reduced growth, protein utilisation and digestibility in African catfish ( Clarias gariepinus ) and were associated with greater hepatic alteration. Dusky kob ( Argyrosomus japonicus ) showed favourable growth and feed-utilisation responses at moderate inclusion levels without major changes in digestive enzymes or haematological variables. Overall, the evidence supports mopane worm meal as a potentially valuable supplementary protein, particularly in locally formulated diets and when replaced in moderate proportions (18% for Dusky kob). Although there are studies suggesting replacements up to 60% for Mozambique tilapia, there is no scientific evidence regarding the optimal range. However, the small number of short-term feeding trials, variability in ingredient composition and processing, incomplete digestibility data and uncertain sustainability of wild harvesting prevent broad commercial recommendations. Standardised, long-term and independently replicated studies are required to establish species-specific inclusion thresholds and evaluate physiological, economic and ecological outcomes.
10.3856/vol54-issue5-fulltext-3526: Ophichthus remiger, commonly known as the common eel, is commercially important in Ecuador because Asian markets have high demand. Since industrial fishing began in 2004, no systematic population monitoring has been conducted, limiting understanding of the species' population dynamics and challenging sustainable management efforts. This study provides essential biological parameters of O. remiger in the Gulf of Guayaquil, Ecuador, including size structure, sex ratio, length-weight relationship, and size at first sexual maturity (SFSM), estimated as the median length at sexual maturity (L50). Between August 2013 and December 2014, 17,186 specimens were sampled monthly using bottom longlines and traps. The results indicate a captured length range of 24 to 138 cm, with females comprising 61% of the population among sexed specimens (n = 5,876). Reproductive activity occurs year-round, with peak the gonadosomatic index in October and April. The condition index (K) is not different between females and males, there are no differences in the length-weight relationship; the specimens exhibit allometric growth. The SFSM, expressed as L50, was 56.7 cm for females (95% CI: 56.2-57.2 cm; n = 1,847) and 63.2 cm for males (95% CI: 62.6-63.8 cm; n = 1,109). Based on the estimated size at 50% sexual maturity (L50), minimum capture sizes of approximately 57 cm total length (TL) for females and 63 cm TL for males are recommended as a management reference for O. remiger in the Gulf of Guayaquil. These data provide a robust basis for sustainable management measures, crucial to conserving this high-demand species in international markets.
10.3390/fishes11110659: This study provides a comprehensive situation analysis of Oman’s fisheries sector, which remains under-researched despite its strategic importance for economic diversification under Oman Vision 2040. Adopting an integrated PESTEL-SWOT framework, the research evaluates the political, economic, social, technological, environmental, and legal dimensions of the sector to identify systemic constraints and development opportunities. The methodology employs a mixed-methods approach, triangulating quantitative data from national and international repositories with qualitative insights from 382 semi-structured interviews conducted across all coastal governorates between 2023 and 2025. Findings reveal that while the sector contributed approximately OMR 521.6 million (1.1%) to the national GDP at constant prices in 2025, it remains characterized by significant inefficiencies. Internal weaknesses include low value addition, with less than 15% of landings undergoing domestic processing, and high post-harvest losses historically estimated at 20% of catch value, highlighting gaps in cold-chain infrastructure. Environmentally, while small pelagic stocks appear stable, high-value species such as kingfish and abalone face overexploitation, further complicated by climate-driven productivity shifts. The analysis highlights critical policy implications, emphasizing the need for a transition from wealth-maximization to welfare-maximization to protect the artisanal fleet, which accounts for approximately 90% of national fisheries production. Key recommendations include the adoption of risk-based food safety management to access high-value global markets, the integration of climate-resilient provisions into legal frameworks, and targeted programs to strengthen youth participation in artisanal fisheries. Ultimately, the study provides an evidence-based diagnostic baseline for an under-researched region, aligning Oman’s fisheries management with the global mandates of SDG 14 and the economic objectives of the “Blue Economy”.
10.1080/09654313.2026.2758888: Research on Europe’s twin transition has moved to the territorial scale, mapping where green and digital innovation co-occur and asking which regions are becoming twin innovators. Co-presence, however, is not integration, and how much integration European territories actually produce remains unknown. We address this for agriculture, forestry and fisheries, using 79,378 patent publications in 36,185 families matched to 1,767 patenting entities through Orbis. Validating the standard co-classification rule, we find two systematic sources of false positives: 44.7 per cent of the families it identifies as integrated carry as their only climate tag a subclass covering energy efficiency in digital technologies themselves, and a further set is attached to primary-sector entities through assignee matching failures. Validation reduces the category from 47 families to three, all linked to the sector through inventor-applicants and none under a stricter attribution rule; of 89 NUTS-2 regions, 14 register as twin-active on a co-occurrence indicator while two retain a validated integrated invention. Examining co-filing, we find that green and digital inventions are co-filed with partner populations that barely intersect, the digital ones mostly through individual applicants. We propose a validation protocol for twin-transition indicators and draw out implications for territorial monitoring and cohesion policy.
10.3390/aquacj6040058: Artificial intelligence is increasingly applied to crab research, yet no prior review has mapped this work or its progress toward real-world use. This scoping review maps artificial intelligence applications in true crabs (Brachyura) across aquaculture, fisheries, ecology, and processing. Following the PRISMA extension for Scoping Reviews, five databases were searched for records published from 2016 to 14 June 2026, yielding 11,172 records, most from databases whose broad field coverage returned papers mentioning crabs or artificial intelligence only in passing. Of these, 88 peer-reviewed English-language primary studies applying artificial intelligence to brachyuran data and reporting at least one quantitative performance metric were included. Each study was charted for species, task domain, model architecture, dataset, performance, and deployment maturity (Technology Readiness Level). The literature is young and expanding rapidly, with nearly half published since 2025, and heavily concentrated, with China contributing most affiliations and three species accounting for more than two-thirds of studies. Twelve task domains were identified, dominated by quality assessment and sex classification. The field has converged on object detectors with attention modules, but accuracy is rarely comparable because datasets and protocols are proprietary. Most systems remain at laboratory validation. Reported accuracy has therefore advanced faster than demonstrated deployment.
10.3856/vol54-issue5-fulltext-3674: Incidental capture of devil rays (Mobula spp.) occurs in several artisanal fisheries worldwide, yet biological information from many regions remains limited. This study examines species composition, morphometrics, sex ratio, and sexual maturity of devil rays incidentally captured in artisanal fisheries along Guatemala's Pacific coast. Fishing operations were monitored from February 2019 to February 2020 and from October 2022 to February 2024, including 246 fishing trips, 143 of which recorded mobulids. Data on species identification, disc width, total length, sex, and maturity stage were collected from landed individuals. A total of 453 devil rays were recorded. Of these, 447 were identified to species level: Mobula munkiana (n = 238), M. thurstoni (n = 205), M. mobular (n = 3), and M. birostris (n = 1); the remaining six individuals could only be identified to genus level (Mobula spp.). Of the total captures, 40.4% occurred in small-scale fisheries targeting Caranx caballus, 32.6% in fisheries targeting large pelagic species, and 27.0% could not be assigned to a specific fishery. In M. thurstoni, males exhibited a significantly larger mean disc width (131.78 ± 32.28 cm) than females (105.14 ± 26.46 cm; P < 0.05), with a male-biased M:F sex ratio of 2.01:1 (χ² = 22.56; P < 0.05). Similarly, in M. munkiana, males were significantly larger (89.27 ± 10.28 cm) than females (82.12 ± 10.52 cm; P < 0.05), and the sex ratio was also male-biased (1.64:1; χ² = 13.65; P < 0.05). These findings provide baseline information on species composition and morphometrics relevant to fisheries management and devil ray conservation.
10.1007/s12562-026-02045-x: Stock enhancement is recognized as one of the most direct and effective means for conserving aquatic biological resources. However, the mechanisms by which enhancement strategies influence the spatiotemporal distribution of target species remain unclear. To evaluate the effects of stock enhancement on the abundance and distribution of Rhopilema esculentum, this study analyzed survey data collected before the R. esculentum fishing season in the southern Bohai Sea from 2015 to 2024. A two-way analysis of variance (ANOVA) and Duncan’s multiple comparison test were used to examine the spatiotemporal variation in R. esculentum resources. A generalized additive model (GAM) was applied to analyze the relationships among R. esculentum density, environmental factors, and stock enhancement variables (release number, timing, and location). The results showed that sampling stations could be divided into high- and low-density groups, while years could be classified into better and poorer resource groups. GAM analysis indicated that the spatial structure (tensor product smooth term of longitude and latitude) had the most significant effect on R. esculentum density (P < 0.01), followed by salinity (P < 0.05). The number of R. esculentum released had a significant positive effect on resource density (P < 0.01), contributing to 61.2% of the interannual variation in biomass. This positive effect was significantly enhanced when releases were conducted in late May (20-31 May) and in the western area of the southern Bohai Sea (P < 0.05). These findings confirm that well-timed and appropriately located stock enhancement can significantly increase R. esculentum biomass, but the effect is context-dependent, and poorly timed releases may yield limited benefits. Given the dominance of spatial structure in the study area, future enhancement efforts should prioritize early-season releases in the western coastal waters to maximize resource recovery. Continued monitoring and adaptive management are recommended to further evaluate the long-term effectiveness and potential ecological trade-offs of stock enhancement practices.
10.1007/s41208-026-01267-1: In the Mediterranean Sea, citizen science projects have gained momentum in monitoring, detecting, and recording non-indigenous species. By combining mining data from social media platforms, citizen science-based observations and specific field surveys conducted between 2018 and 2025 along the western and eastern Libyan coasts, it was possible to document six non-indigenous and range-expanding fish taxa, namely: the Lionfish (Pterois miles), the Redcoat (Sargocentron rubrum), a fish of the genus Abudefduf, the Red Sea goatfish (Parupeneus forsskali), the Monrovia doctorfish (Acanthurus monroviae), and the African hind (Cephalopholis taeniops). These records update the known occurrence ranges of the studied taxa in Libya and are consistent with broader Mediterranean distribution changes. Their opportunistic nature does not allow population trends or dispersal directions to be established.
10.1111/jfb.70718: Abstract Estuarine wetlands are critical zones of land-sea interaction that play vital roles in maintaining biodiversity and ecosystem functioning. As the only remaining natural estuarine wetland in the Yangtze River Estuary, Jiuduansha's fish and macrobenthic diversity and community assembly mechanisms remain poorly understood due to limitations of traditional survey methods in protected areas. We conducted eDNA metabarcoding surveys at 11 sampling sites (6 intertidal zone and 5 riverine sites) in the Jiuduansha Wetland Nature Reserve during May and July of 2023-2024, combined with measurement of environmental variables, to systematically analyse the mechanisms of species composition, diversity patterns and community assembly of the Jiuduansha Wetland. A total of 64 fish species and 35 macrobenthos were detected. The eDNA approach identified approximately 40% more species than historical traditional surveys. Spatially, fish diversity was higher in riverine sites (average 18.6 ± 2.7 species/site), while macrobenthos were more concentrated in the intertidal zone (average 14.2 ± 2.5 species/site). Seasonal patterns differed: fish species richness was higher in May, whereas macrobenthos peaked in July. Generalized linear models (GLMs) indicated that total nitrogen (TN) and chemical oxygen demand (COD) were key environmental factors that have negative influence on both communities' richness. Beta diversity decomposition showed that species turnover was the dominant component of community variation within the study scale (70.7%-70.9% for fish, 60.0%-69.3% for macrobenthos). Neutral community model (NCM) fitting revealed increased migration rates, with Nm values increased from 4 in 2023 to 17 in 2024 for fish and from 9 to 18 for macrobenthos, based on samples collected in May and July of each year. This indicates enhanced dispersal between communities. Both βNTI analysis (|βNTI| 90% contribution of ecological drift) demonstrated that stochastic processes, particularly ecological drift, dominated community assembly.
10.70963/soc.v3i1.970: This study aims to identify and explain the communication strategies employed by the Malabero Beach Fishermen’s Group in Bengkulu City in dealing with the decline in fish catches. This study employed a qualitative method with a case study approach. The research informants were selected using purposive sampling and consisted of the group leader, senior members, and active fishermen. Data were collected through observation, interviews, and documentation, while data analysis employed the interactive model of Miles and Huberman, which includes data reduction, data display, and conclusion drawing and verification. The study was analyzed using Hafied Cangara’s (2016) communication strategy theory, which encompasses five elements: communicator, message, media, receiver, and effect. The findings show that the communication strategies employed by the Malabero Beach The findings show that the communication strategies employed by the Malabero Beach Fishermen’s Group involved open communication, deliberation, and a family-oriented approach. The group leader and senior members acted as communicators in directing the members, while the messages conveyed included information about fishing locations, weather conditions, wind direction, sea conditions, and appeals to maintain group solidarity. The communication media used included face-to-face communication at the fishing base and mobile phones while at sea. Although mobile phone network connectivity posed a challenge, group members were able to adapt through direct communication. These communication strategies helped maintain coordination, strengthen cooperation, increase participation, and preserve group solidarity in dealing with the decline in fish catches.
10.3856/vol54-issue5-fulltext-3672: The Chilean silverside (Basilichthys microlepidotus) is an endemic freshwater species with emerging potential for aquaculture and conservation-oriented production. However, key bioengineering parameters required for system design and biomass management remain poorly defined. This study evaluated how body size and stocking density affect total ammonia nitrogen (TAN) excretion rates in a recirculating aquaculture system (RAS) under controlled conditions. Two stocking densities (1.1 and 1.8 kg m-3) and two size ranges (7.8-77.8 g and 80-297 g), as well as their interaction, were tested using a factorial design with triplicate tanks per treatment. Mean TAN excretion rates ranged from 24.5 to 30.6 mg TAN kg-1 fish h-1. A clear diurnal excretion pattern was observed, with peak TAN release occurring 2-4 h after feeding, followed by a gradual decline. Neither body size nor stocking density significantly affected TAN excretion within the evaluated ranges, indicating that these results provide bioengineering parameters for RAS design and scaling.
10.3390/toxins18110490: The analytical characteristics of Lyngbya wollei toxin 4 (LWTX4), a rare derivative of saxitoxin (STX), remain insufficiently documented due to its limited availability. In the present study, therefore, LWTX4 was synthesized using the previously reported synthetic route developed by Looper to elucidate its fundamental chromatographic behavior. Additionally, three other paralytic shellfish toxin analogues, STX, decarbamoyl saxitoxin (dcSTX), and 12-epi-LWTX4, were prepared from a common intermediate. Analysis of synthetic LWTX4 using the AOAC OMA 2011.02 HPLC-PCOX-FLD method yielded a retention time of 19.8 min, which overlapped with that of STX, and revealed that its FLD response was one-fourteenth that of STX. Meanwhile, under the AOAC 2021 HILIC-MS/MS conditions, LWTX4 eluted at 7.29 min, producing major product ions at m/z 205.1204, 182.0926, 164.0822, and 110.0720. These chromatographic and mass spectrometric characteristics provide useful reference data for assessing the possible presence of LWTX4 during PST profiling of biological samples. The synthetic STX and dcSTX exhibited chromatographic behavior consistent with that of their corresponding certified reference materials (CRMs) under the standard HPLC-PCOX conditions, supporting the potential use of synthesis as a complementary approach to the isolation of PSTs from dinoflagellates for the preparation of CRMs.
10.1111/rec.70597: Abstract Introduction Shellfish reef restoration occurs across diverse ecological settings. Techniques that perform well in one habitat or species assemblage may perform poorly elsewhere. Objectives We examined how field observations, constraints, and unexpected outcomes shaped restoration structures and developed Adaptive Restoration Engineering (ARE), a framework for iterative refinement and diversification of restoration systems. Methods We assessed 1081 remnant shellfish reef bommies across five Queensland sites and reviewed five restoration structures developed from 2018 to 2026 as practice-based design pathways: chicken-wire baskets, mild steel Robust Oyster Baskets, Stainless Steel Robust Oyster Baskets (SS ROBs), Quilted Oyster Doonas, and Living Oyster Gardens (LOGs). Project records, field observations, design modifications, and deployment outcomes were reviewed to identify constraints, drivers, and design responses. Results Remnant reef morphology showed reefs commonly formed discrete bommies rather than continuous platforms, supporting modular design. Field observations drove shifts from galvanized and woven mesh to mild steel and welded stainless steel. Observed burial and subsidence led to seeding racks, shell foundations, and LOGs, while mussel-dominated recruitment led to SS ROBs where cohesive reefs had not formed before mild-steel degradation. Handling, transport, and decentralized manufacture shaped unit size and fabrication techniques. These observations formed the basis of ARE, which links observation, driver identification, design response, implementation, and monitoring. Conclusions Multiple designs can be refined for contrasting settings rather than relying on a standard unit. ARE provides a restoration-specific application of adaptive management for translating field observations into context-specific design responses.
10.3389/fmars.2026.1892884: Syngnathid fishes, including seahorses and pipefishes, are ecologically and economically important but remain vulnerable to overfishing, habitat degradation, and trade-driven exploitation. This study documents syngnathid occurrence, habitat associations, body-size observations, and genomic resources in the Sembilan Archipelago, Malaysia, using SCUBA-based visual surveys and high-resolution photographic analysis. Across 32 dives at seven reef sites, we recorded 54 occurrence records belonging to four species: Hippocampus kuda , H. comes , Doryrhamphus janssi , and Trachyrhamphus bicoarctatus . Species differed in their observed habitat associations, while size-depth relationships varied among species. A brooding male and two juvenile seahorses provided evidence of local reproductive activity during the survey period. To establish baseline genomic resources for Malaysian syngnathids, we generated high-quality PacBio HiFi genome assemblies for six individuals from three species, with genome sizes ranging from 0.45-0.61 Gbp and BUSCO completeness scores of 92.3-98.8%. The assemblies were characterized through repeat annotation, protein-coding gene prediction, orthology analysis, and phylogenomics. Complete mitochondrial genomes were generated for all six individuals. These genomic resources provide a foundation for future comparative and population genomic studies of genetic diversity, connectivity, and evolutionary relationships. Together, the ecological observations and genomic resources provide a baseline for future standardized monitoring and conservation research on Malaysian syngnathids.
10.3390/cimb48111198: Vibrio parahaemolyticus and Vibrio vulnificus biofilms pose a major challenge to seafood safety owing to their persistence on food-contact surfaces and increased tolerance to antimicrobial interventions. This study investigated the antibiofilm efficacy and mechanisms of quercetin using integrated structural, physiological, and molecular approaches. Quercetin exhibited concentration-dependent biofilm inhibition and reduced mature biofilms on abiotic surfaces, while its efficacy in inhibiting biofilm formation was evaluated on seafood. Quercetin suppressed early biofilm establishment by reducing cell surface hydrophobicity, bacterial adhesion, autoaggregation, motility, cellular respiration, and ATP production, thereby limiting bacterial attachment and microcolony formation. Fourier-transform infrared spectroscopy revealed changes in the EPS-associated spectral profiles of both species, indicating alterations in the biochemical composition of the biofilm matrix. These spectral changes varied between V. vulnificus and V. parahaemolyticus. Gene expression analysis demonstrated coordinated downregulation of quorum sensing (QS), adhesion, and EPS biosynthesis genes, accompanied by increased membrane permeability, intracellular protein leakage, and metabolic dysfunction. In a 6 h screen, 1/2 MIC caused only minor changes in the color and texture of shrimp and oyster, whereas MIC caused larger changes; no cytotoxicity was detected under the tested conditions. Collectively, these findings demonstrate that quercetin disrupts Vibrio biofilms through coordinated mechanisms with limited short-term effects on seafood color and texture at 1/2 MIC, supporting further evaluation as a natural, industry-relevant strategy for controlling seafood-associated Vibrio biofilms and improving seafood safety.
10.1111/jfb.70719: Abstract Tidal freshwater reaches may provide early-life habitat for diadromous fishes, but long-term evidence of their use remains limited. Size-resolved records are needed as a reference for monitoring under the Yangtze fishing ban introduced in 2021. We analysed monitoring data from Jingjiang, 240 km upstream of the river mouth (2002-2017; 519 effective surveys; 10,560 measured individuals), combining size-based catch indices, environmental-window analyses and otolith Sr/Ca profiles from 115 Japanese grenadier anchovy Coilia nasus . Individuals <120 mm standard length were classified operationally as juveniles during August-October, when scale readings supported an age-0 interpretation, whereas individuals ≥180 mm were treated as a descriptive large-fish category throughout the year. Juveniles occurred in every survey year; annulus-free individuals also occurred in winter and spring. The Juvenile Recruitment Index (JRI) showed negative associations with tidal range across the April-July spawning and larval-transport period, although none of the 72 environmental-window correlations remained significant after Benjamini-Hochberg correction at a 5% false-discovery rate. Monthly models also showed a negative lagged association. None of the 40 autumn recruits sampled across four capture years had an accepted elevated Sr/Ca zone; such zones were more frequent in later developmental groups. Total catch obscured contrasting size structures: 2016 combined the series-high JRI with few large fish, whereas 2010 combined the series-high large-fish catch rate with a mid-range JRI. These findings document recurrent early-life use of a tidal freshwater reach and provide a size-resolved pre-ban reference, without establishing a disproportionate contribution to adult production.
10.1007/s12562-026-02050-0: Abstract Knowledge of gastric and intestinal food passage rates are useful to both the fish culture industry and for estimates of a species daily rations in the wild. This study compared gastric and intestinal food passage in two very different species, Mozambique tilapia Oreochromis mossambicus and rainbow trout Oncorhynchus mykiss . Both species were fed a common pelleted meal. The effects of meal size were investigated at temperatures at which each of the species is commonly cultured. Also, the two species were compared at a common water temperature. In addition, the use of chromic oxide as a measure of food passage through the intestine was evaluated. Meal size did not affect gastric emptying times in either species when expressed as a proportion of the meal consumed regressed on the natural log of time since fed. Gastric emptying in tilapia required 24 h at 25 °C and more than 45 h for trout at 13 °C. Chromic oxide was a good indicator for the progression of the meal through the intestinal tract in both species. Meal size did not affect intestinal emptying. Tilapia required 45 h compared with 65 h for trout. Gastric and intestinal emptying at 19 °C did not differ between the two species.
10.1007/s12562-026-02046-w: Abstract Stable hatchery production of yellowtail requires effective brood stock management, particularly control of vitellogenic progression. Although the absence of males impairs oocyte maturation and ovulation in several fish species, its influence on yellowtail reproduction remains unclear. This study compared female-only and mixed-sex groups over two reproductive seasons, referred to as year 1 and year 2, respectively. Oocyte diameter, ovarian histology, and gonadosomatic index were evaluated before human chorionic gonadotropin (HCG) administration, and ovulation was assessed. In both years, maximum oocyte diameter before HCG administration was significantly lower in the female-only group than in the mixed-sex group. The female-only group exhibited individual variation, with some females progressing through vitellogenesis, whereas others showed arrested vitellogenic development. The proportion of ovulated HCG-treated females was significantly lower in the female-only group during year 1 and showed a similar numerical trend in year 2. However, some females with oocyte diameters > 600 μm ovulated under female-only conditions. These results indicate that the absence of males is associated primarily with delayed vitellogenic progression, whereas ovulation can be induced in females that complete vitellogenesis. Therefore, the absence of males should be considered a potential risk factor in brood stock management and may provide a foundation for future maturation control strategies.
10.9734/ajfar/2026/v28i111187: Background: Oyster-producing lagoons and estuaries are exposed to environmental pressures that may affect habitat condition and fishery sustainability. Aims: To assess and compare the ecological condition of the Densu estuary and Anyanui lagoon by integrating benthic macroinvertebrate assemblages with physicochemical characteristics and water-quality indices and to examine the implications of the findings for sustainable oyster fisheries management in Ghana. Study Design: Water and benthic macroinvertebrate samples were collected from four ecologically distinct zones selected to represent the major environmental gradients within the lagoon: (i) the upstream freshwater-influenced section, (ii) the central channel, (iii) the downstream section adjacent to the lagoon outlet, (iv) an area adjacent to agricultural lands/graveyards where diffuse runoff was expected to influence water quality (mapped using QGIS). These locations were selected to capture spatial variability in physicochemical conditions and benthic communities across the lagoon. The modified Delphi technique was adopted to identify priority water quality parameters affecting Crassostrea tulipa growth. Place and Duration of Study: The Densu Estuary and Anyanui Lagoon were studied from November 2023 to December 2024. Methodology: Physicochemical variables were analysed using the Canadian Council of Ministers of the Environment Water Quality Index (CCME-WQI), while benthic macroinvertebrate assemblages were used as biological indicators of ecological integrity. Expert consultation informed the selection and weighting of key physicochemical variables included in the index. Macroinvertebrate assemblages revealed greater taxonomic diversity and ecological integrity in the Anyanui Lagoon than in the Densu Estuary. Results: Macroinvertebrate assemblages revealed greater taxonomic diversity and ecological integrity in the Anyanui Lagoon than in the Densu Estuary. The occurrence of taxa such as Lithophaga lithophaga and Leptocerus sp. indicated relatively stable environmental conditions in Anyanui, whereas the higher Hilsenhoff Biotic Index in Densu (5.06), compared with Anyanui (3.82), suggested greater organic pollution pressure in the Densu Estuary. CCME-WQI scores classified the Anyanui lagoon as marginal (47.14) and the Densu estuary as poor (38.69), indicating environmental conditions that may limit oyster growth, recruitment and long-term fishery productivity. Although both approaches provided complementary information, benthic macroinvertebrates offered a more integrative assessment of ecological condition than physicochemical measurements alone. Conclusion: These findings demonstrate the value of integrating biological and physicochemical indicators for ecosystem assessment and provide a scientific basis for prioritising habitat restoration, long-term ecological monitoring and adaptive management to sustain Ghana's brackish-water oyster fisheries.
10.55885/jucep.v6i2.1232: Coastal fishing communities often depend on selling fresh catches, limiting opportunities to increase product value through processing. In Tanjung Binga, Belitung, this highlights the need to strengthen Koperasi Konsumen Usaha Mandiri (KUM) 's processing capacity. This community service programme aimed to develop skills in producing natural fish stock powder and support the cooperative’s product development capacity. Conducted from March to July 2026, it involved 20 women from fishing households and adopted a participatory technology-transfer approach. Activities included socialisation on fisheries downstreaming, processing training, product application, laboratory nutritional analysis, and assistance with packaging, labelling, branding, and business management. The resulting product, Formio, was made from laisi fish and vegetables without added MSG through grinding, cooking, dehydration, and dry milling. Laboratory analysis recorded 52.00% protein, 1,268 mg/100 g calcium, and 855 mg/100 g phosphorus. However, moisture content reached 21.00%, indicating the need to optimise drying and assess water activity, microbiological quality, and storage stability. Overall, the programme established a foundation for valorising local fish resources and strengthening cooperative-based enterprise capacity. The results demonstrate progress in product development and skills transfer, while identifying product standardisation and market assessment as priorities for subsequent development.
10.1086/743937: The Estuary and Gulf of St. Lawrence in Canada is experiencing a decline in oxygen levels, adversely affecting marine life, particularly commercial northern shrimp. This study develops a biological model that links oxygen saturation to the growth rate of northern shrimp to assess how variations in oxygen saturation impact shrimp populations. By simulating scenarios where oxygen saturation levels are increased by 5-25 percentage points, the research indicates that such intervention could have led to significant profit increases from 1995 to 2018, especially under restricted fishing efforts. The findings underscore the importance of effective fishery management practices in maximizing the economic benefits of improved environmental quality. Proactive measures to enhance oxygen saturation can help sustain marine ecosystems and support the fishing industry before the region becomes hypoxic.
10.54254/2753-8818/2026.38927: The aquatic ecosystems of the rivers maintain aquatic biodiversity, and freshwater fish are important bioindicators for the ecological health of a river. Compound stress on fish populations all over the world has been caused by hydrological changes and water quality degradation due to intensive human activities such as dam regulation and pollutant discharge. This study focused on the lower reaches of the Yellow River, and investigated the independent and interactive impacts of river flow and water quality on the dynamics of freshwater fish populations based on multiple-year field monitoring data from 2014 to 2023. Flow variation accounted for 21% of the temporal variation in fish community and was found to have a significant influence on fish spawning cues, habitat availability, and physiological metabolism of the fish, while water quality accounted for 15% of the temporal variation in fish community and was the most limiting factor in the most heavily polluted river reach. Low flow conditions increased risk of pollutant accumulation, flood conditions increased both pollutant accumulations and introduced non-point source pollution risks; there were non-additive coupled interactions between flow and water quality. Benthic resident fish had higher tolerance to composite stress while pelagic and migratory fish had higher sensitivity to hydrological/water quality co-stress. Single factor regulation would hardly be enough to restore fish communities, coordinated regulation of flow regime and water environment was needed. This paper offers scientific evidence for watershed ecological controls and fish biodiversity conservation under various human disturbances.
10.56201/ijaes.vol.12.no10.2026.pg137.14: This research investigated the effects of digital extension and e-learning intervention and adoption among cassava and fish farmers in Bayelsa State. A quasi-experimental design incorporating pre test and post-test assessments was employed, involving 240 active smallholder farmers selected from Yenagoa, Ogbia and Sagbama Local Government Areas. Agricultural advisory content was delivered through WhatsApp groups, Interactive Voice Response (IVR) and YouTube videos over a twelve-week period. The data obtained were subjected to descriptive and inferential statistical analyses. The results indicated that farmers’ technical knowledge improved after the interventions. Cassava and fish farmers acknowledged the positive contributions of the interventions, with fish farmers expressing greater perceived benefits. The interventions also shaped production decisions and farm management practices, particularly in fertiliser and feed application, input selection, disease control and weed management. Technology adoption emerged as a significant predictor of changes in farmers’ practices after the interventions. Nevertheless, inconsistent mobile network connectivity, expensive data subscriptions, unreliable electricity and inadequate digital literacy limited effective engagement. The research concluded that digital extension and e-learning interventions offer opportunities for enhancing agricultural knowledge dissemination and improving farming practices. It recommended the establishment of public-private partnerships to improve rural network infrastructure and provide subsidised data packages for farmers.
10.12873/ncdh-2026-237: associated with poor maternal nutritional status, anemia, and adverse birth outcomes. Food-based supplementation using locally available nutrient-dense ingredients, such as foxtail millet (Setaria italica) and mackerel fish, may provide a sustainable strategy to improve maternal nutrition. To evaluate the effectiveness of foxtail millet flour cookies fortified with mackerel fish flour in improving body weight, mid-upper arm circumference (MUAC), and hemoglobin levels among pregnant women with CED. A quasi-experimental study using a non-randomized pretest-posttest control group design was conducted among 40 pregnant women with CED selected through purposive sampling. Participants were allocated to an intervention group (n = 20), which received foxtail millet flour cookies fortified with mackerel fish flour, or a control group (n = 20), which received foxtail millet flour cookies without mackerel fish flour, for 90 days. Body weight, MUAC, and hemoglobin levels were measured at baseline and after the intervention. Between-group differences in changes from baseline were analyzed using the Mann-Whitney U test. After 90 days, participants in the intervention group experienced significantly greater increases in body weight (7.95 vs. 5.00 kg, p = 0.001), MUAC (2.09 vs. 2.02 cm, p = 0.035), and hemoglobin concentration (1.64 vs. 1.24 g/dL, p = 0.003) compared with the control group. Foxtail millet cookies fortified with mackerel fish flour were more effective than non-fortified foxtail millet cookies in improving maternal nutritional status, as reflected by greater increases in body weight, MUAC, and hemoglobin levels among pregnant women with CED. These findings support the use of locally sourced, nutrient-rich supplementary foods as a practical strategy to address maternal undernutrition in resource-limited settings
10.1186/s12986-026-01241-x: Owing to the continuous, tight-junction-sealed architecture of capillary endothelium in skeletal muscle, the trans-endothelial transport of fatty acids from capillary lumen to myofibers constitutes a critical determinant of intramuscular fat (IMF) deposition, thus playing a crucial role in meat quality. This study aimed to investigate the effects of fish oil on trans-endothelial fatty acids transport and lipid deposition in skeletal muscle and explore the underlying vascular regulatory mechanisms. Firstly, preliminary exploratory analyses indicated there may exist an association between IMF content in porcine longissimus dorsi muscle (LDM) and serum VEGF-B level, as well as VEGF-B expression within LDM, hinting at a potential involvement of VEGF-B in skeletal muscle lipid deposition. Meanwhile, the transwell experiments confirmed that VEGF-B enhanced trans-endothelial fatty acid transport by upregulating expression and membrane localization of fatty acid transporters. In addition, DHA, a key bioactive component of fish oil, enhanced trans-endothelial fatty acid transport by promoting VEGF-B expression and secretion of C2C12 myotubes. Mechanistically, the GPR120-CaMKK2-AMPK pathway was involved in DHA-induced VEGF-B expression and secretion. More importantly, fish oil supplementation significantly increased lipid deposition of mice tibialis anterior muscle, alongside the activation of GPR120-CaMKK2-AMPK pathway, the elevated expression of VEGF-B and fatty acid transporters. Overall, these findings suggested that fish oil might enhance trans-endothelial fatty acids transport and lipid deposition in skeletal muscle by promoting muscular VEGF-B expression via GPR120-CaMKK2-AMPK pathway, providing potential molecular targets and nutritional technologies to increase IMF in animal skeletal muscle.
10.21275/sr261107134834: An organic compound, dimethyl phthalate (DMP) is a category of plasticizer that is commonly utilized in plastic materials. The prediction of acute toxicity in fish through an in silico approach is an active assessment because fish is an edible diet of human beings. The objective of the present study was to predict an in silico acute toxicity (median lethal concentration or LC50 at 96hrs exposure) of DMP on fish as per simulated molecular descriptors by using toxicity estimation software tool (T.E.S.T.). The LC50 value of fish was predicted of about 15.97 mg/L or 4.09 -Log10(mol/L) as per similarity coefficient ≥0.5 of mean absolute error (MAE) of 0.03. Different molecular descriptors such as chi connectivity indices, topological descriptor, molecular properties, molecular distance-edge vector, burden eigenvalue descriptors, 2D autocorrelation descriptors, electrotopological state indices, information indices, molecular fragments, etc. were obtained. The average value was predicted for LC50 value as per all of these descriptors. It is concluded that the acute toxicity of fish for DMP was easily predicted after simulation of different molecular descriptors within T.E.S.T tool. It is suggested to evaluate fish toxicity with other phthalate compounds.
10.56201/ijaes.vol.12.no10.2026.pg173.19: Tidal rivers that pass through growing Niger Delta towns sustain artisanal fisheries, but surveys rarely collect fish and water quality data at the same places and times. We sampled three stations on the Egbelu reach of the New Calabar River, Rivers State, Nigeria, each month from May to July 2026. On every visit we measured eleven physico-chemical variables and caught fish with gill nets, cast nets and hooks. Salinity, conductivity and total dissolved solids differed among stations (p < 0.001), while only temperature and pH changed from month to month. Dissolved oxygen (6.50-6.80 mg L-1) and BOD5 (2.50-2.80 mg L-1) pointed to well oxygenated water with modest organic loading. We caught 1,533 fish belonging to 20 species and 11 families. Cichlidae made up 28.6% of individuals, Clupeidae 16.0% and Alestidae 11.4%, and Sarotherodon melanotheron was the most abundant species (12.5%). Every species turned up at every station, diversity was almost the same everywhere (H′ = 2.91-2.93; J′ = 0.97-0.98), and Bray-Curtis similarity was above 92%. Sampling month, on the other hand, explained 81% of the variation in assemblage composition (PERMANOVA, pseudo-F = 11.04, p = 0.028), against only 4% for station (p = 0.861). Mugil cephalus, Neochelon falcipinnis, Elops lacerta and other marine-associated species declined from May to July, as Brycinus spp., Hemichromis fasciatus and Chrysichthys nigrodigitatus became more common. In the early rainy season, then, the assemblage changed far more over time than across space, and monitoring of the reach should follow the seasonal cycle rather than add stations.
10.2478/contagri-2026-0019: Abstract Aquaculture has become an essential sector in Nigeria’s agriculture, significantly contributing to food security, rural employment, and economic diversification. Despite the sector’s rapid growth, Nigeria’s aquaculture industry operates below its potential, with technical efficiency levels far from optimal. This study assesses the determinants of technical efficiency among catfish farmers in Nigeria, using secondary data from a survey of 604 farmers. The result indicate that, despite significant growth in Nigeria’s aquaculture sector, technical efficiency remains suboptimal, with farmers operating at about 67% of their potential output. Using a stochastic frontier production function, we identify key factors affecting productivity and efficiency, including fish stock, household size, culture type, management system, and membership in farmers’ associations. The study highlights the need for targeted policies to enhance resource utilization, promote diversified farming practices, and support farmer associations to optimize technical efficiency in Nigeria’s catfish farming sector. These findings have important implications for improving productivity and ensuring food security in the country.
10.3390/fishes11110655: Integrated multi-trophic aquaculture (IMTA) combines fed and extractive species, yet appropriate biomass allocation among trophic groups remains poorly defined. This study investigated water quality regulation and stocking biomass ratios in a black seabream (Acanthopagrus schlegelii)-mussel (Mytilus coruscus)-seaweed (Ulva lactuca) IMTA system. Sequential monoculture, two-species, and three-species experiments were conducted in 300 L aquaria over 15 days, with three replicates per treatment. Black seabream monoculture increased NH4+-N and PO43--P accumulation relative to controls, whereas U. lactuca reduced dissolved nutrient concentrations. Fish-mussel co-culture did not prevent nutrient accumulation, while increasing fish biomass in fish-seaweed co-culture was associated with greater nutrient accumulation and lower seaweed RGR, which may have also been influenced by direct grazing by black seabream. Conversely, seaweed relative growth rate (RGR) increased with mussel biomass in mussel-seaweed co-culture. Among three-species treatments, FMU1 (80 g fish, 600 g mussels, and 150 g seaweed; initial biomass ratio 1:7.5:1.875) showed the best overall balance among the three tested fish biomass levels under the experimental conditions. After 15 days, NH4+-N decreased by 41.18% in FMU1 but increased by 15.91% and 61.65% in FMU2 and FMU3, respectively. These findings highlight the importance of balancing fish loading with extractive biomass to improve water quality regulation and sustain seaweed growth in coastal IMTA systems.
10.3390/aquacj6040057: Aquaculture is an important source of food, employment and economic development, but maintaining appropriate water quality remains a major challenge for farmers. Parameters like temperature, pH, dissolved oxygen (DO), turbidity and salinity have significant effects on the growth, health, feeding efficiency and survival of aquatic organisms. Traditional monitoring relies mainly on manual sampling and periodic measurements, which is time-consuming and may not provide sufficient spatial and temporal information for precision aquaculture. This paper proposes an IoT-based mobile water-quality monitoring architecture with an unmanned aerial vehicle UAV (drone) integrated with an autonomous autopilot system. The system receives the registered GPS coordinates of an aquaculture pond and automatically navigates the UAV to the pond for measurement. When the UAV arrives at the pond, it visits several preselected sites and submerges a detachable multi-parameter sensing module to collect the water-quality parameters. An embedded controller processes the sensor data and transmits the measurements, GPS coordinates and time stamps to a cloud database via wireless communication. One mobile sensing unit can monitor multiple ponds and form a spatially indexed historical database of water quality. The architecture lays a foundation for AI-based anomaly detection, water-quality prediction, disease-risk assessment, and intelligent decision support for precision aquaculture.
10.1139/er-2026-0153: The ocean, the world's largest carbon pool, plays a critical role in regulating the global climate. Within this system, the microbial carbon pump (MCP) is a key mechanism for long-term carbon sequestration, converting organic carbon into diverse and structurally complex dissolved molecules that persist in the environment. Despite the dramatic expansion of bivalve aquaculture in recent decades, its contribution to carbon sequestration through the MCP remains poorly understood and understudied. This article critically assesses the impact of bivalve aquaculture on the carbon cycle, particularly its role in enhancing the MCP. Bivalve aquaculture influences the carbon cycle in several ways. First, it increases dissolved organic carbon (DOC) in surrounding waters through direct excretion by bivalves and enhances primary productivity, particularly in oligotrophic waters. These changes boost microbial biomass and may potentially accelerate the production of recalcitrant dissolved organic carbon (RDOC), a key component of long-term carbon storage; however, increased DOC release and microbial activity do not by themselves demonstrate RDOC production, and direct evidence from bivalve aquaculture is currently lacking. Second, intensive bivalve aquaculture alters phytoplankton community structure, shifting dominance from diatoms to cyanobacteria and picophytoplankton. These smaller phytoplankton groups tend to release more RDOC into the environment compared to diatoms and microphytoplankton, further contributing to carbon sequestration. By elucidating the mechanisms through which bivalve aquaculture enhances carbon sequestration via the MCP, this article provides valuable insights for developing sustainable bivalve fisheries and aquaculture management strategies. Such strategies can harness the potential of bivalve aquaculture to mitigate climate change impacts while supporting global food security.
10.1108/jadee-04-2026-0301: Purpose This study examines aquaculture households' intentions to transition to organic aquaculture in Thanh Hoa, Vietnam. Building on the theory of planned behavior (TPB) and the norm activation model (NAM), the study distinguishes perceived benefits into economic and non-economic dimensions, incorporates moral norm as an internal moral consideration and examines the moderating role of subjective norm in the relationship between moral norm and transition intention. Design/methodology/approach A quantitative research design was employed using survey data collected from 323 aquaculture households in Thanh Hoa, Vietnam. The proposed model was tested using partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM) to examine the hypothesized direct, indirect and moderating relationships. Findings Perceived economic benefits, perceived non-economic benefits, subjective norm, perceived behavioral control and moral norm are positively associated with transition intention, with moral norm showing the strongest association.
